knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select an action minimizing estimated total cost, with branching required when no admissible enforcement action can make certified progress.

notation.meaning: set of admissible enforcement and branching actions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-based choice between direct enforcement and semantics-preserving branching.

source_refs.locator: 6.6 Impact on the State of the Art in Integer Programming p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\mathcal A_E\cup\mathcal A_B\) be the currently admissible enforcement and branching actions. Assign each action an immediate cost \(c(a)\) and a predicted residual search cost \(T(a)\), using a common estimation model, and choose \[a^{\star}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathcal A}\bigl(c(a)+T(a)\bigr).\] An enforcement action is admissible only if it produces certified progress, such as separation or domain reduction. If no enforcement action is admissible, selection must use a valid branching action; if no action is valid, the handler must report failure rather than discard the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the valid enforcement or branching action with least estimated total work; branch when direct enforcement cannot certify progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement–Branching Selection

source_witnesses.locator: 6.6 Impact on the State of the Art in Integer Programming p. 87

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The argmin rule is an architecture-dependent heuristic policy, not a generally established principle. The cited sources do not support the additive predicted-cost objective or the asserted mandatory selection behavior.

children.title: Constraint Specialization Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Migration from general representations to specialized constraint classes.

children.title: Constraint Upgrading
children.top_down_role: Recognition and migration of general representations into stronger constraint forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Upgrading
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic-preserving replacement of a generic constraint by a recognized specialized constraint within the current domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a constraint instance \(C\), current domain \(D\), and ordered upgrade rules \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\), select the first rule whose recognition predicate \(R_k(C,D)\) holds. Construct \(C'=u_k(C,D)\), require \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C')\cap D\), transfer all required flags and state, replace \(C\) by \(C'\), and assign \(C'\) to its specialized handler. If no predicate holds, retain \(C\). The output is therefore domain-equivalent to the input, although the specialized handler may provide stronger propagation, separation, or enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the first eligible specialization rule, replacing a constraint only when its feasible assignments on the current domain are preserved; otherwise retain the original constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the current search domain.
Each upgrade rule terminates and declares its recognition predicate.
Required operational state can be transferred without changing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C')\cap D\)

notation.meaning: Current variable domain or search region.
Eligibility predicate of upgrade rule k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no source supports first-match rule ordering, domain-relative equivalence, state transfer, or handler reassignment. These architecture-specific requirements cannot be validated as stated.

children.title: Constraint Specialization
children.top_down_role: Specialized constraint classes with dedicated semantic and inference services.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-relative semantic refinement used by a constraint-handler specialization hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) and \(C'\) be constraints over the same variables and let \(D\) be a current domain. The constraint \(C'\) is a specialization of \(C\) on \(D\) when \(\operatorname{Sol}(C')\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D\) and the representation of \(C'\) belongs to a more specific recognized constraint class. Specialization is semantic equivalence relative to \(D\), not merely implication; its purpose is to permit algorithms tailored to the recognized structure without altering the feasible assignments represented at that search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specialized constraint has exactly the same satisfying assignments on the current domain as the original, but exposes a more specific recognized structure.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(C'\) have the same variable scope.
\(D\) is fixed while equivalence is assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C'\preceq_D C\iff \operatorname{Sol}(C')\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D\)

notation.meaning: C-prime specializes C on domain D.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but the proposed domain-relative equivalence relation and recognized-class requirement are uncited and may not match CIP constraint specialization semantics.

children.title: Upgrade Eligibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural and semantic conditions limiting safe migration to specialized handlers.

knowledge_statements.title: Upgrade Eligibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary safety conditions delimiting when handler-level constraint upgrading is admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An upgrade rule \(u\) is eligible for a constraint \(C\) at domain \(D\) exactly when its structural recognition predicate \(R_u(C,D)\) holds, the constructed constraint \(C'=u(C,D)\) is well-defined, and \(\operatorname{Sol}(C')\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D\). Eligibility additionally requires preservation or explicit transfer of all operational attributes that affect enforcement, propagation, separation, checking, and local validity. Failure of any condition places the instance outside the rule's eligibility boundary and mandates retaining \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upgrade is allowed only when its pattern matches, construction succeeds, domain-relative solutions are unchanged, and every operational attribute affecting correctness is preserved or transferred.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) specifies both recognition and construction.
Operational attributes relevant to correctness are identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Eligible}_u(C,D)\iff R_u(C,D)\land u(C,D)\downarrow\land \operatorname{Sol}(u(C,D))\cap D=\operatorname{Sol}(C)\cap D\land \operatorname{StateOK}_u(C,D)\)

notation.meaning: The upgrade construction is defined and terminates successfully.
All correctness-relevant operational state is preserved or transferred.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the boundary leaf, but the claimed biconditional and exhaustive operational-state requirements need a specialized CIP source.

children.title: CIP Model Abstraction
children.top_down_role: Unified model objects combining general constraints, variables, objectives, and solver-facing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: CIP Model Abstraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic representation of a constraint integer program with handler-defined constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint integer program is represented as \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ C_i(x)\text{ holds for every }i\in I\},\] where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) includes variable bounds and prescribed integrality restrictions. Each constraint object \(C_i\) denotes a satisfaction set \(S_i\subseteq X\), so the feasible region is \(F=X\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}S_i\). The model abstraction exposes objective, variables, domains, and constraint objects while delegating recognition and algorithmic treatment of each \(C_i\) to its constraint handler.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CIP minimizes an objective over bounded or integral variable domains intersected with handler-defined constraint satisfaction sets.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
The objective and every satisfaction predicate are well-defined on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=X\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}S_i\)

notation.meaning: Variable domain including bounds and integrality restrictions.
Satisfaction set represented by constraint object i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not establish the stated CIP constraint-object and handler-delegation architecture. A specialized CIP source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Constraint-Handler Ownership
children.top_down_role: Allocation of semantic, inference, relaxation, enforcement, and lifecycle responsibilities to constraint classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Handler Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique semantic ownership of each active constraint object by one handler.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the active constraint objects and \(\mathcal H\) the registered handlers. Ownership is a total function \(h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal H\). For every \(C\in\mathcal C\), the owner \(h(C)\) defines its satisfaction predicate and supplies or delegates all required resolution operations. Generic search services may invoke these operations but must not independently reinterpret \(C\). Replacing \(C\) by an upgraded object \(C'\) requires an atomic reassignment from \(h(C)\) to \(h(C')\), preserving the model's satisfaction set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every active constraint has one owning handler that defines its semantics and resolution services; upgrades atomically transfer ownership without changing feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: Every active constraint type has a registered handler.
Required handler operations have defined return semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall C\in\mathcal C\;\exists! H\in\mathcal H:\ h(C)=H\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role is plausible, but unique semantic ownership, delegation obligations, and atomic ownership reassignment are architecture-specific assertions without evidence.

children.title: Integrated CIP Search Calculus
children.top_down_role: Coordination of domain inference, mathematical relaxations, branching, and bounding in integrated search.

children.title: Domain-Inference Services
children.top_down_role: Constraint-specific filtering, propagation scheduling, probing, and objective-driven reductions.

children.title: Propagation Fixpoint Calculus
children.top_down_role: Specialized reductions and coordination of interacting propagators.

children.title: Constraint-Specific Filtering
children.top_down_role: Specialized domain reductions derived from individual constraint classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Specific Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound domain reduction performed by a propagator specialized to one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraint \(C_i\) and current product domain \(D=\prod_{j=1}^nD_j\), a constraint-specific filter computes \(F_i(D)\subseteq D\). It may delete a value \(v\in D_j\) only when no assignment \(x\in D\) satisfying \(C_i\) has \(x_j=v\). If \(D_j\) becomes empty, it reports infeasibility; otherwise it returns the reduced domain and the reasons for its deletions. Soundness requires \(\operatorname{Sol}(C_i)\cap F_i(D)=\operatorname{Sol}(C_i)\cap D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-specific filter deletes only values lacking support in that constraint, reports an empty domain as infeasible, and preserves every satisfying assignment.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_j\) is the current domain of variable \(x_j\).
The filter's support test is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_i(D)\subseteq D\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{Sol}(C_i)\cap F_i(D)=\operatorname{Sol}(C_i)\cap D\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, and the preservation equation is mathematically plausible. The cited introductory CP page does not adequately support the formal support-deletion rule or the requirement to return reasons.

children.title: Propagation Fixpoints
children.top_down_role: Stable inference states reached through repeated interaction among propagators.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Fixpoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common fixpoint of all active constraint-specific filtering operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be contracting, solution-preserving filtering operators on domains ordered by inclusion. A domain \(D^*\) is a propagation fixpoint when \(F_i(D^*)=D^*\) for every active operator \(i\). Starting from \(D^0\), any fair sequence of operator applications that changes the domain only by strict contraction terminates at such a fixpoint when the domain lattice has finite height. The resulting fixpoint need not equal the set of globally feasible assignments and can depend on the operators' filtering strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation fixpoint is a domain unchanged by every active filter; finite-height domains and fair scheduling ensure termination, but not global consistency.
assumptions_latex: Every \(F_i\) is contracting and solution-preserving.
The domain lattice below \(D^0\) has finite height.
The application sequence is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*\text{ is a fixpoint}\iff \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\ F_i(D^*)=D^*\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixpoint definition is plausible, but the record also asserts a convergence theorem. The cited introductory section does not support its exact fairness, termination, and finite-height hypotheses, so the mathematical version remains insufficiently sourced.

children.title: Propagator Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Priority, wake-up, incremental, and event-based coordination of inference services.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven fair worklist scheduling of constraint-specific filtering operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the queue \(Q\) with every active propagator. Repeatedly remove a propagator \(F_i\), compute \(D'=F_i(D)\), and stop with infeasibility if any component of \(D'\) is empty. If \(D'\subsetneq D\), set \(D\leftarrow D'\) and enqueue every propagator subscribed to an event caused by the reduction, suppressing duplicate queue entries. Stop when \(Q\) is empty and output \(D\). If every reduction event schedules every operator that it can invalidate, an empty queue certifies a common propagation fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process propagators from an event-driven queue, rescheduling affected propagators after reductions; an empty queue yields a common fixpoint when subscriptions are complete.
assumptions_latex: All filters are contracting and solution-preserving.
Event subscriptions cover every dependency that can invalidate a previous fixpoint.
Queue selection is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\varnothing\Longrightarrow \forall i,\ F_i(D)=D\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the cited general CP section does not establish duplicate suppression, subscription completeness, fairness, or the empty-queue fixpoint certificate.

children.title: Fixpoint Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additional propagation rounds yield limited reductions relative to their expense.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixpoint Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invocation bound for finite-domain event-driven propagation under duplicate-suppressing scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose there are \(m\) propagators, at most \(q\) strict value-deletion events before the domain reaches a fixpoint, and each event has at most \(\Delta\) subscribed propagators. With one initial enqueue per propagator and duplicate suppression, the worklist performs at most \(m+q\Delta\) propagator invocations. If invocation \(k\) costs \(T_k\), total propagation time is at most \(\sum_k T_k\), with at most \(m+q\Delta\) terms. Without finite domain height, complete subscriptions, or duplicate control, this bound does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite deletions, at most Delta affected propagators per event, and duplicate suppression, fixpoint computation uses at most m plus qDelta propagator invocations.
assumptions_latex: At most \(q\) strict value-deletion events occur.
Each event subscribes at most \(\Delta\) propagators.
A scheduled propagator has at most one pending queue entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{invoke}}\le m+q\Delta\)

notation.meaning: Maximum number of strict value-deletion events.
Maximum number of propagators subscribed to one event.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role exactly fits the leaf, but the bound depends on an architecture-specific definition of deletion events, subscriptions, and invocations. No source is supplied for that cost model or bound.

children.title: Speculative Objective Inference
children.top_down_role: Speculative and objective-aware inference within the shared search state.

children.title: Probing
children.top_down_role: Speculative inference under temporary decisions within shared search state.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reversible speculative domain restriction followed by propagation and inference extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a probe assumption \(P\), save the current domain \(D\), impose \(P\), and propagate to a fixpoint \(D_P\) or detect infeasibility. Record deductions together with reasons, then restore \(D\) exactly. Optionally repeat under the complementary assumption \(\neg P\). If the \(P\)-branch is infeasible, permanently infer \(\neg P\); if both branches are feasible, retain only deductions valid in both branches or a certified disjunction combining their outcomes. The persistent output must be entailed by the unprobed model and domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporarily impose an assumption, propagate, record consequences, and restore the domain; retain only consequences certified globally or by complementary-branch analysis.
assumptions_latex: The probe state can be restored exactly.
Propagation deductions are sound and carry valid reasons.
\(P\) and \(\neg P\) exhaust the current cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\cap\operatorname{Sol}\subseteq D_P\cup D_{\neg P}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but exact restoration, reason recording, complementary-branch transfer, and certified-disjunction behavior require a probing or CIP implementation source.

children.title: Objective Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction driven by incumbent values, objective bounds, and conditional cost information.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain filtering induced by a linear objective cutoff and current variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with cutoff \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le U\) and product domain \(D=\prod_jD_j\), compute \(m_k=\min\{c_kv:v\in D_k\}\). For each variable \(j\), delete \(v\in D_j\) whenever \(c_jv+\sum_{k\ne j}m_k>U\). If every value of some \(D_j\) is deleted, the node cannot contain a solution meeting the cutoff. Otherwise the retained domains contain every assignment in \(D\) whose objective value is at most \(U\); the procedure may be iterated after any domain or cutoff improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the objective cutoff and minimum contributions of other variables to delete values that cannot participate in a sufficiently good solution.
assumptions_latex: The objective is separable and linear.
Every \(D_j\) is nonempty before filtering.
Each minimum \(m_k\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'_j=\{v\in D_j:c_jv+\sum_{k\ne j}m_k\le U\}\)

notation.meaning: Minimum possible objective contribution of variable k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The filtering formula is mathematically plausible for a separable linear objective over product domains, but the cited introductory integer-programming page does not support this objective-propagation algorithm or its exact conclusion.

children.title: Probe-Derived Inference Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of deductions, conflicts, or bound changes obtained during speculative analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Probe-Derived Inference Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates for transferring deductions from temporary probe branches to the parent domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let complementary probe assumptions \(P\) and \(
eg P\) partition the parent domain. A deduction \(L\) transfers to the parent if the probe records certify both \(P\Rightarrow L\) and \(
eg P\Rightarrow L\). If the \(P\)-branch instead certifies contradiction, then \(
eg P\) transfers. More generally, branch deductions \(P\Rightarrow L_P\) and \(
eg P\Rightarrow L_{
eg P}\) certify the parent-valid disjunction \(L_P\lor L_{
eg P}\). Verification consists only of checking the branch implications and the tautology \(P\lor
eg P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parent deduction is certified when both complementary probes imply it; an infeasible branch certifies the opposite assumption, and distinct branch deductions yield a valid disjunction.
assumptions_latex: \(P\lor\neg P\) is valid on the parent domain.
Every recorded branch implication has a checkable sound reason.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(((P\Rightarrow L)\land(\neg P\Rightarrow L))\Rightarrow L\)

notation.meaning: Deductions certified in the two probe branches.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits, and the propositional transfer rules are plausible. No source establishes that these implications and disjunctions constitute the intended CIP probe-transfer certificate or its checkable reason interface.

children.title: Relaxation-Cut Service Calculus
children.top_down_role: LP and other mathematical bounds used inside constraint-oriented search.

children.title: LP-MIP Relaxation Service Family
children.top_down_role: Linear and mixed-integer bounding models embedded in integrated search.

children.title: LP Relaxation Services
children.top_down_role: Continuous linear bounding models embedded in integrated search.

assumptions_latex: The node subproblem has feasible set \(F=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and objective \(c^\top x\).
A polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is available with \(F\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For minimization, \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\le \inf\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\); infeasibility of \(P\) certifies infeasibility of \(F\).

notation.meaning: feasible solutions of the current node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous linear relaxation at one node of a minimization-oriented CIP search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An LP relaxation service for a node with feasible set \(F\) and objective \(c^\top x\) constructs a polyhedron \(P\supseteq F\), solves \[z_{\mathrm{LP}}=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in P\},\] and returns one of: an optimizer \(\bar x\in P\), an unboundedness report, or an LP infeasibility certificate. For minimization, every finite value satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\le \inf\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\). If \(P=\varnothing\), then \(F=\varnothing\). The service may additionally return dual multipliers, reduced costs, and basis information without changing the relaxation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP service solves a polyhedral superset of the node domain, yielding a valid minimization lower bound or, when the relaxation is infeasible, a node-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: LP Relaxation Services

children.title: MIP Relaxation Services
children.top_down_role: Partially integral bounding models used as subordinate hybrid search services.

assumptions_latex: The current node has feasible set \(F\subseteq D\) and objective \(c^\top x\).
A mixed-integer representable set \(M\) satisfies \(F\subseteq M\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For minimization, \(z_{\mathrm{MIP}}\le \inf\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\), and \(M=\varnothing\) implies \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible solutions of the current node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer subrelaxation used as a bounded search service inside a CIP node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A MIP relaxation service replaces the node feasible set \(F\) by a mixed-integer representable superset \(M\) and seeks \[z_{\mathrm{MIP}}=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in M\}.\] A complete call returns an optimal solution, proves \(M=\varnothing\), or proves unboundedness. A truncated call may return a certified lower bound \(L\le \inf\{c^\top x:x\in M\}\) and an optional incumbent in \(M\). Since \(F\subseteq M\), both \(z_{\mathrm{MIP}}\) and \(L\) are valid lower bounds for the original node problem, while infeasibility of \(M\) certifies infeasibility of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP service solves a mixed-integer superset of the node domain, returning a valid bound, a relaxation solution, or a proof that the node is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: MIP Relaxation Services

children.title: Relaxation-Service Selection
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among bound strength, integrality retention, invocation frequency, and computational expense.

assumptions_latex: At node state \(s\), each available service \(r\in\mathcal R(s)\) has an estimated benefit \(B_r(s)\ge 0\) and cost \(C_r(s)>0\).
The node has remaining relaxation budget \(H(s)\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected service is admissible under the budget and maximizes the declared benefit-to-cost score among admissible services.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted choice between LP, MIP, or no relaxation call at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given state \(s\), initialize the admissible set by \[\mathcal A(s)=\{r\in\mathcal R(s):C_r(s)\le H(s)\}.\] If \(\mathcal A(s)=\varnothing\), return the null service and leave the budget unchanged. Otherwise select \[r^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{r\in\mathcal A(s)}\frac{B_r(s)}{C_r(s)},\] execute \(r^*\), incorporate every certified bound or infeasibility conclusion it returns, and update the budget to \(H(s)-C_{r^*}(s)\). Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic ordering. The algorithm stops after this single selection and outputs the chosen service together with its certified results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among affordable relaxation calls, select the service with greatest estimated benefit per cost; otherwise skip relaxation. Incorporate only certified results and debit the service budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Service Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio rule is a particular budgeted service-selection algorithm, not a canonical consequence of the surrounding taxonomy. No source is supplied for this policy, its one-call stopping rule, or the interpretation and estimation of benefit and cost. A source supporting this precise algorithm or an explicitly identified established policy is required.

children.title: CP-to-Relaxation Inference Transfer
children.top_down_role: Domain and logical inference transferred into the mathematical relaxation.

children.title: CP-Driven Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Domain and logical deductions transferred into relaxation variable bounds.

assumptions_latex: The current CP domain is a box \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\), and the current-node feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq D\).
Sound propagation returns sets \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\) such that either some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), or \(F\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every \(D_i'\) is nonempty and bounded, adding its hull bounds preserves every point of \(F\) and can only strengthen the relaxation; if some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), then \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: lower and upper hull bounds of a nonempty bounded propagated domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of sound CP domain reductions into variable bounds of a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose sound CP propagation returns sets \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\). If some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), soundness implies \(F=\varnothing\). Otherwise, for each nonempty bounded \(D_i'\), define \(\ell_i'=\inf D_i'\) and \(u_i'=\sup D_i'\). Adding \[\ell_i'\le x_i\le u_i'\] to any relaxation containing \(F\) is valid whenever \(F\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i'\). If \(x_i\) is required to be integral, the strengthened integer bounds \[\lceil\ell_i'\rceil\le x_i\le\lfloor u_i'\rfloor\] are valid. These transferred bounds preserve every member of \(F\) and can only strengthen the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound CP propagation can transfer the hull bounds of each nonempty bounded reduced domain to the relaxation. If propagation empties a domain, it certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: CP-Driven Bound Tightening

children.title: CP-Driven Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-valid restrictions derived from constraint-programming structure or inference.

assumptions_latex: The current node feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
A CP inference establishes that every \(x\in F\) satisfies \(a^\top x\le\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\) may be added to any relaxation of \(F\) without excluding a feasible node solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certificate for a linear cut derived from CP reasoning at one node.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CP-derived linear inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\) is a valid relaxation cut at the current node precisely when \[\sup\{a^\top x:x\in F\}\le\beta.\] A verifiable certificate may consist of a sound CP derivation establishing this implication for every assignment in \(F\), or a finite disjunction \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^q F_k\) together with bounds \(\sup\{a^\top x:x\in F_k\}\le\beta\) for all \(k\). The certified inequality can be added to a relaxation \(P\supseteq F\); if some relaxation point violates it, the cut removes that point without removing any member of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CP-derived inequality is a valid cut when sound inference proves it for every node-feasible assignment; adding it removes relaxation points but no feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: CP-Driven Cut Generation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition for a linear inequality is mathematically precise, but the cited generic CP and disjunctive-programming sections do not inspectably support the asserted CP-derived certificate forms or a CP-driven cut-generation procedure. In addition, the record is framed as a validity certificate rather than as cut generation. A specific source for deriving and certifying cuts from CP inference is required before the mathematical role and formulation can be settled.

children.title: Inference-to-Relaxation Transfer
children.top_down_role: Validity, strength, timing, and persistence of CP information injected into mathematical relaxations.

assumptions_latex: A CP inference transforms a node domain \(D\) into \(D'\subseteq D\) with \(F\subseteq D'\).
A relaxation set \(P\) satisfies \(F\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any representable set \(Q\) with \(D'\subseteq Q\) yields the valid strengthened relaxation \(P'=P\cap Q\supseteq F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity rule encompassing transferred bounds, cuts, and representable CP consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let sound CP inference produce \(D'\subseteq D\) with \(F\subseteq D'\), and let \(Q\) be any LP- or MIP-representable superset of \(D'\). For a current relaxation \(P\supseteq F\), define \[P'=P\cap Q.\] Then \(F\subseteq P'\subseteq P\), so replacing \(P\) by \(P'\) is a valid inference-to-relaxation transfer. Bounds and linear cuts are special cases obtained by choosing \(Q\) as a box or halfspace. If the transferred representation is exact for \(D'\), no information is lost at the representation step; otherwise validity remains, but strengthening may be incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer a sound CP inference by intersecting the relaxation with any representable superset of the reduced CP domain; validity is preserved, though strength may be lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Inference-to-Relaxation Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-intersection rule is mathematically coherent and the principle content kind fits the abstract transfer container, but no source supports this hybrid CP-to-LP/MIP transfer formulation, including the exact-versus-inexact representation distinction. Supply a specific authoritative locator.

children.title: Relaxation Feedback to Propagation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation values, reduced regions, and bounds used to guide CP inference.

assumptions_latex: The current-node feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq P\cap D\), where \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a relaxation and \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) is the current CP domain.
A relaxation computation returns certified bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) that hold for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Updating each domain by \(D_i'=D_i\cap[\ell_i,u_i]\) preserves \(F\); if some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), then \(F=\varnothing\). An uncertified relaxation solution may guide search or propagation priorities but cannot by itself justify pruning.

notation.meaning: CP domain after intersection with certified relaxation bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified relaxation consequences fed back into CP propagation; fractional values alone provide guidance, not pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relaxation feedback is sound when only certified consequences are used to reduce the CP domain. If a relaxation computation certifies bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) for every \(x\in F\), update \[D_i'=D_i\cap[\ell_i,u_i],\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] Then every member of \(F\) remains in \(\prod_{i=1}^n D_i'\), and if some \(D_i'=\varnothing\), then \(F=\varnothing\). A relaxation optimizer \(\bar x\in P\) that is not certified to belong to \(F\) may be used to rank variables, values, or propagators, but it cannot by itself justify excluding assignments. Thus certified bounds support domain reduction, whereas uncertified relaxation values support guidance only.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified relaxation bounds may safely reduce CP domains, and an empty reduced domain certifies infeasibility. Relaxation solutions may guide priorities but cannot by themselves justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Feedback to Propagation

children.title: Hybrid Search-Control Calculus
children.top_down_role: Search decisions combining domain, constraint, relaxation, and failure information.

children.title: Branching Object Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Branching families spanning CP assignments and MIP disjunctions.

children.title: Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Search partitions selected through variable-level discrete or bound decisions.

assumptions_latex: The current node domain is \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\), with some \(D_j\) containing at least two admissible values.
Children are formed by predicates whose union covers \(D_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child domains cover the parent domain, so exhaustive exploration preserves completeness.

notation.meaning: child index sets for values of the selected variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-partition branching on one variable in a complete single-tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Variable branching selects an index \(j\) and nonempty sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_q\subseteq D_j\) satisfying \(D_j=\bigcup_{k=1}^q S_k\). It replaces the parent domain \(D\) by child domains \[D^{(k)}=D\cap\{x:x_j\in S_k\},\qquad k=1,\ldots,q.\] Hence \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^q D^{(k)}\), so every parent-feasible assignment occurs in at least one child. The sets may overlap, although a partition avoids duplicate search. For an integer variable and threshold \(t\), the standard binary choice is \(S_1=\{v:v\le t\}\) and \(S_2=\{v:v\ge t+1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable branching covers a variable's current domain by child value sets. Because the resulting child domains cover the parent, exhaustive child search remains complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Branching

children.title: Value Branching
children.top_down_role: Search partitions centered on candidate values, value sets, or assignment alternatives.

assumptions_latex: A variable \(x_j\) with finite current domain \(D_j\) has been selected.
The value-ordering rule returns a permutation of \(D_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule changes exploration order but not the union of searched assignments, provided no value is discarded without a valid inference.

notation.meaning: current finite domain of the selected variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value ordering and value-versus-remainder branching after selecting a finite-domain variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Value branching selects an ordering \((v_1,\ldots,v_q)\) of the finite domain \(D_j\) of a chosen variable \(x_j\). In enumeration form, child \(k\) imposes \(x_j=v_k\). In value-versus-remainder form, the first two children impose \[x_j=v_1\qquad\text{or}\qquad x_j\in D_j\setminus\{v_1\}.\] Both forms cover every assignment allowed by the parent domain. The ordering determines which value is explored first and may depend on relaxation values, incumbent agreement, or propagation scores. It does not justify deleting a value; deletion requires a separate valid inference or bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value branching orders a selected variable's values or splits one preferred value from the remainder. It affects search order, while completeness requires retaining every uncertified value.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The enumeration and value-versus-remainder constructions are coherent, but no source is supplied for treating both as the exact local meaning of Value Branching or for the asserted guidance signals. A specific CP or hybrid-search source is required.

children.title: Constraint Branching
children.top_down_role: Search disjunctions derived from unresolved constraint structure.

assumptions_latex: The current node feasible set is \(F\subseteq D\).
Predicates \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) satisfy \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^q\{x\in D:C_k(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child feasible sets cover \(F\); if the predicates are mutually exclusive on \(D\), they partition the parent domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive branching on general constraint predicates rather than a single variable domain.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Constraint branching chooses predicates \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) whose disjunction is valid for every parent-feasible solution: \[F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^q\{x\in D:C_k(x)\}.\] Child \(k\) adds predicate \(C_k\), giving \(F_k=F\cap\{x:C_k(x)\}\). Consequently \(F=\bigcup_{k=1}^q F_k\), which preserves completeness under exhaustive child exploration. If the predicates are pairwise incompatible on \(D\), the children form a partition; otherwise feasible assignments may occur in several children. Variable branching is the special case in which every \(C_k\) restricts the domain of one variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint branching creates children from a valid disjunction of predicates. Their feasible sets must cover the parent feasible set; mutually exclusive predicates avoid duplicate search.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Branching

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

children.title: Branching-Family Selection
children.top_down_role: Criteria for choosing among variable-, value-, or constraint-centered search partitions.

assumptions_latex: At state \(s\), each admissible branching family \(f\in\mathcal F(s)\) can generate at least one complete child cover.
Each family has a declared finite score \(Q_f(s)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a highest-scoring admissible family and a complete child cover generated by that family.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection among variable, value, and constraint branching families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given search state \(s\), form the admissible family set \(\mathcal F(s)\) by retaining exactly those families that can generate children covering every feasible assignment at \(s\). If \(\mathcal F(s)=\varnothing\), return failure. Otherwise compute \(Q_f(s)\) for each \(f\in\mathcal F(s)\) and choose \[f^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{f\in\mathcal F(s)}Q_f(s).\] Resolve ties by a fixed ordering, invoke \(f^*\) to generate its highest-scoring branching object, and verify the child-cover condition before committing the branch. Output the selected family, branching object, and children. Scores affect efficiency only; admissibility and cover verification preserve completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score all branching families capable of a complete child cover, choose the highest-scoring family deterministically, generate its preferred branch, and verify coverage before committing it.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Family Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a particular scored family-selection algorithm rather than a taxonomy-level consequence. No source supports the maximum-score policy, the second-stage branching-object choice, or the proposed cover-verification step, and the score itself is unspecified. A precise algorithmic source is required.

children.title: Hybrid Search Guidance Coupling
children.top_down_role: Cross-use of relaxation impact, propagation strength, and failure histories.

children.title: Relaxation-Guided Search
children.top_down_role: Search priorities informed by relaxation values, bounds, fractional structure, or impact.

assumptions_latex: At node state \(s\), a relaxation returns a solution \(\bar x\) and a certified lower bound \(L(s)\) for a minimization problem.
An incumbent objective value \(U\) is available, and pruning by bound occurs only when \(L(s)\ge U\).
The search tree is finite, or the node-selection policy is fair so that every unpruned generated node is eventually processed; all other pruning uses valid infeasibility or dominance certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation-derived scores may order nodes, variables, values, or branching objects without changing completeness, provided they affect only order and every pruning decision uses a valid certificate.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for a minimization node
objective value of the current incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Use of relaxation solutions and bounds as search-order signals, separated from pruning validity and subject to finite or fair exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relaxation-guided search maps certified relaxation output and solution features into priority scores. For an integer variable, one possible fractionality score is \[q_j(s)=\min\{\bar x_j-\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor,\lceil\bar x_j\rceil-\bar x_j\}.\] Nodes may likewise be ordered using the certified minimization bound \(L(s)\). Such scores may choose the next node, variable, value, or branching predicate. They do not themselves justify pruning: infeasibility pruning requires a valid infeasibility certificate, and bound pruning requires \(L(s)\ge U\). If the search tree is finite, or node selection is fair, changing these guidance scores changes exploration order and effort but does not remove any unpruned node from eventual consideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation solutions and certified bounds may prioritize nodes and branching choices. Completeness is preserved when guidance affects only order, pruning uses valid certificates, and the search is finite or fairly explores every unpruned node.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided Search

children.title: Propagation-Guided Search
children.top_down_role: Search priorities informed by domain reduction, failure history, or inference strength.

assumptions_latex: The current CIP node has domain store \(D\), constraint set \(C\), and a finite candidate branching set \(B\).
Propagation reaches a sound fixpoint for every trial branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected branch maximizes the prescribed propagation-impact score over \(B\).

notation.meaning: variables fixed or domain values deleted by propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step branching rule based on trial propagation at a single CIP search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node state \((D,C)\), a finite candidate set \(B\), and nonnegative weights \(w_j\), temporarily apply each \(b\in B\), propagate \(C\) to a fixpoint, and record the domain reductions \(\Delta(b)\). Define \[s_P(b)=\sum_{j\in\Delta(b)}w_j,\] assigning \(s_P(b)=+\infty\) when propagation proves the trial branch infeasible. Select \(b^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in B}s_P(b)\), branch on \(b^*\), restore the unmodified node state before creating children, and stop the guidance computation after this branch is selected. Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate candidate branches by temporary propagation, score their domain reductions or detected infeasibility, and branch on a candidate with maximum propagation impact.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Guided Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this CIP-specific rule. Moreover, assigning infinite score to an infeasible trial and then branching on the maximizer selects a branch already proved infeasible; the record must instead specify pruning or score a branching object through its child outcomes.

children.title: Hybrid Guidance Signals
children.top_down_role: Combination and calibration of relaxation, propagation, and failure-based search information.

assumptions_latex: Relaxation and propagation scores are available for every candidate \(b\in B\).
Each score family is normalized to a common bounded scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid signal ranks candidates by a weighted combination of relaxation and propagation information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar coupling of relaxation and propagation scores; normalization is part of the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite candidate set \(B\), let \(r,p:B\to[0,1]\) denote normalized relaxation and propagation scores, with larger values preferred. For a coupling parameter \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), define \[h_\lambda(b)=\lambda r(b)+(1-\lambda)p(b),\qquad b\in B.\] A hybrid-guided decision is any \(b^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in B}h_\lambda(b)\). The endpoints \(\lambda=1\) and \(\lambda=0\) recover purely relaxation-guided and purely propagation-guided rankings, respectively. Any deterministic tie-breaking rule completes the representation as a single-valued decision rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize relaxation and propagation scores, combine them by a convex weight, and choose a candidate maximizing the resulting hybrid score.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Guidance Signals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex score is internally precise, but it is a particular normalization and coupling convention rather than a canonical hybrid-guidance representation. A source is required to establish that this convention fits the CIP leaf.

children.title: Guidance Conflict Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where relaxation signals and propagation signals favor incompatible search choices.

assumptions_latex: The candidate set \(B\) is finite and contains at least two elements.
Relaxation and propagation scores induce weak rankings on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The statistic \(\kappa\) separates agreement, partial-conflict, and complete-reversal regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise classification of disagreement between two guidance rankings, excluding tied comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume neither guidance score ties any distinct pair in \(B\). For relaxation score \(r\) and propagation score \(p\), define \[\kappa=\frac{1}{M}\left|\left\{\{b,c\}\subseteq B:(r(b)-r(c))(p(b)-p(c))<0\right\}\right|,\qquad M=\binom{|B|}{2}.\] The guidance regime is agreement when \(\kappa=0\), partial conflict when \(0<\kappa<1\), and complete reversal when \(\kappa=1\). Thus conflict is present exactly when some candidate pair is ordered oppositely by the two signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify two guidance rankings by the fraction of candidate pairs they order oppositely: zero means agreement, an intermediate fraction partial conflict, and one complete reversal.
knowledge_statements.title: Guidance Conflict Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statistic is a normalized pairwise ranking distance and the stated classifications are mathematically consistent under the no-ties assumption, but no evidence connects these chosen thresholds and regime names to the target CIP concept.

children.title: Primal Solution Improvement Family
children.top_down_role: Solution completion, repair, and improvement using integrated constraint services.

children.title: Primal Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Solution construction, completion, repair, and polishing using integrated constraint services.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving incumbent construction for minimization CIP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal heuristic for a minimization CIP is a terminating procedure that maps a search state to either failure or a point \(x^H\in F\). If an incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) exists, the heuristic accepts \(x^H\) only when \(f(x^H)<f(\bar x)\), after independently checking all original constraints and variable domains. Upon acceptance it replaces \(\bar x\) by \(x^H\); failure or rejection leaves the incumbent unchanged. The procedure need not prove that no improving feasible point exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal heuristic proposes a feasible solution; it updates the incumbent only after feasibility validation and strict objective improvement.
assumptions_latex: The CIP feasible set is \(F\) and the objective is minimized.
The current search state supplies domains, relaxations, and optionally an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted heuristic output lies in \(F\) and strictly improves the incumbent when one exists.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the original CIP

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Restricted reoptimization around incumbent or partially fixed solutions.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) is available for a minimization problem.
A neighborhood mapping assigns a restricted set \(N(\bar x)\subseteq F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either an improving point in \(N(\bar x)\) or the unchanged incumbent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or truncated search over a feasible incumbent neighborhood.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), a neighborhood \(N(\bar x)\subseteq F\), and a resource limit \(L\). Initialize \(x^*=\bar x\). Search the restricted problem \[\min\{f(x):x\in N(\bar x)\}\] until it is solved or \(L\) is exhausted. Whenever a validated point \(x\in N(\bar x)\) satisfies \(f(x)<f(x^*)\), set \(x^*=x\). Return \(x^*\); hence the returned point is feasible and satisfies \(f(x^*)\leq f(\bar x)\), even when the restricted search terminates early.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a restricted feasible region around the incumbent, retain every validated improvement, and return the best found point when solved or the resource limit expires.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Search

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: CP-Defined Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods shaped by domains, global constraints, logical structure, or propagation.

assumptions_latex: The incumbent \(\bar x\) satisfies the original constraint set \(C\).
Additional CP constraints are interpreted over the original variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CP-defined neighborhood is the feasible set of \(C\) intersected with the added neighborhood constraints.

notation.meaning: CP neighborhood constraints parameterized by the incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhoods expressed by CP constraints and filtered by the original CIP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the original CIP constraints over domain store \(D\), and let \(C_N(\bar x)\) be CP constraints parameterized by an incumbent \(\bar x\). The CP-defined neighborhood is \[N_{CP}(\bar x)=\{x\in D:x\text{ satisfies }C\cup C_N(\bar x)\}.\] Examples of admissible neighborhood constraints include a Hamming-distance bound on discrete variables, cardinality restrictions on changed assignments, or global constraints selecting movable components. Because \(C\) is retained, every member of \(N_{CP}(\bar x)\) is feasible for the original CIP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add CP constraints around an incumbent while retaining every original constraint; their common feasible set is the CP-defined neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: CP-Defined Neighborhoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set definition is coherent, but the cited general CP section does not specifically support incumbent-parameterized CP neighborhoods inside a CIP architecture or the listed neighborhood constructions. A directly relevant hybrid-neighborhood source is required.

children.title: MIP-Assisted Solution Repair
children.top_down_role: Relaxation or sub-MIP services used to restore feasibility or improve candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: A candidate assignment \(\tilde x\) may violate constraints or integrality.
A mixed-integer repair model can represent permitted deviations from \(\tilde x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted repair is feasible for the original model and minimizes the chosen repair cost within the restricted repair model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted MIP projection of a candidate assignment onto the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a candidate \(\tilde x\), original feasible set \(F\), repair restrictions \(R(\tilde x)\), nonnegative distance \(d\), and resource limit \(L\). Form the mixed-integer subproblem \[\min\{d(x,\tilde x):x\in F\cap R(\tilde x)\}.\] Solve it until optimality, infeasibility, or exhaustion of \(L\). Return the best validated feasible solution found, or failure if none is found. When solved to optimality, the output is a minimum-distance permitted repair; under early termination it remains a valid, though not necessarily closest, repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a restricted MIP that minimizes deviation from a candidate while enforcing the original model, then return its best validated feasible repair.
knowledge_statements.title: MIP-Assisted Solution Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resource-limited repair algorithm is mathematically coherent and distinguishes optimal from early termination, but no source supports this particular restricted-MIP projection as the intended CIP solution-repair method.

children.title: CIP Conflict-Learning Calculus
children.top_down_role: Explanation-based reuse of infeasible nodes, propagated deductions, and relaxation conflicts.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Conflict Analysis in Mixed Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Conflict Analysis in Mixed Integer Programming

children.title: Propagation Reason Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Reason interfaces connecting bound deductions to later conflict analysis.

children.title: Propagation Reasons
children.top_down_role: Recorded justifications for bound changes and domain deductions.

assumptions_latex: A sound propagator infers a bound literal \(q\) from the current bound literals.
The reported reason is finite and checkable against the propagator's constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid reason certifies that its literals logically imply the propagated literal \(q\).

notation.meaning: finite set of antecedent bound literals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical certificate for one bound inference produced during CIP propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a propagated bound literal \(q\) obtained from a constraint \(c\), a propagation reason is a finite set \(R\) of bound literals active before the inference such that \[c\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\;\Longrightarrow\;q.\] Equivalently, \(c\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\land\neg q\) is infeasible. The certificate is sound when this implication is valid over the declared variable domains. It is locally verifiable by checking the stated infeasibility without relying on literals assigned after \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation reason is a finite set of earlier bound facts that, together with the responsible constraint, logically forces the propagated bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Reasons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is a plausible reason certificate, but CIP-specific sources are needed to confirm the literal semantics, responsible-constraint interface, temporal restriction on antecedents, and proposed local verification requirement.

children.title: Reverse Propagation
children.top_down_role: Backward analysis of deductions to recover conflict-relevant antecedents.

assumptions_latex: A propagator previously inferred a bound literal \(q\) from constraint \(c\).
The pre-inference domain state is reproducible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reverse propagation returns a sound antecedent set \(R\) satisfying \(c\land R\Rightarrow q\).

notation.meaning: candidate antecedent literals active before the inference

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason reconstruction by querying a propagator after an inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the responsible constraint \(c\), propagated literal \(q\), and the finite set \(A\) of literals active immediately before \(q\) was inferred. Initialize \(R=A\). Repeatedly remove any \(r\in R\) for which \[c\land\bigwedge_{s\in R\setminus\{r\}}s\;\Longrightarrow\;q\] remains valid, stopping when no tested removal succeeds or a resource limit is reached. Return \(R\). The output is sound because the maintained invariant is \(c\land\bigwedge_{r\in R}r\Rightarrow q\); exhaustive successful deletion additionally makes \(R\) inclusion-minimal relative to \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct a propagation reason from the earlier domain state, deleting unnecessary antecedents while preserving implication of the inferred bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion procedure preserves a sound reason, but it is a reason-minimization algorithm and may not match the established CIP meaning of reverse propagation. A source is necessary before fixing the algorithmic statement for this exact leaf.

children.title: Reason Interface Quality
children.top_down_role: Granularity, availability, validity, and reuse of handler-provided explanations.

assumptions_latex: Every returned reason is sound for its propagated literal.
Reason extraction has a finite computational budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dominance requires no worse reason size and extraction cost, and at least one strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of sound reason interfaces by reason size and extraction cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sound reason interfaces \(I\) and \(J\) on a finite test set \(\mathcal I\), say that \(I\) dominates \(J\) when, for every \(i\in\mathcal I\), \[|R_I(i)|\leq |R_J(i)|\quad\text{and}\quad T_I(i)\leq T_J(i),\] and at least one inequality is strict for some instance. A reason interface is Pareto-efficient on \(\mathcal I\) if no other sound interface dominates it. This condition separates logical correctness, which is mandatory, from the competing quality objectives of concise explanations and inexpensive extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare sound reason interfaces by explanation size and extraction cost; one dominates another only when it is never worse and sometimes strictly better.
knowledge_statements.title: Reason Interface Quality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-test-set dominance relation is internally valid, but it is a locally invented quality criterion. Evidence is needed that reason-interface quality is appropriately characterized only by cardinality and extraction cost and by this strong per-instance dominance order.

children.title: Conflict-Derived Restriction Learning
children.top_down_role: Learned restrictions derived from branching and propagated bound histories.

children.title: Conflict-Graph Analysis
children.top_down_role: Graph-based organization of branching decisions, deductions, and infeasibility causes.

assumptions_latex: A conflict is detected after a finite sequence of reason-certified bound propagations.
Each propagated literal has antecedents assigned earlier in the search state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward traversal identifies an implication cut whose antecedent literals jointly imply the conflict.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed implication-graph analysis for bound-based CIP conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a directed graph \(G\) with one vertex for each active bound literal and a conflict vertex \(\bot\). For every reason \(R\) of an inferred literal \(q\), add arcs \(r\to q\) for \(r\in R\); connect the literals in the final infeasibility reason to \(\bot\). Starting at \(\bot\), traverse predecessors and resolve expanded inferred vertices with their reasons until a prescribed cut \(U\) separates decision-side vertices from \(\bot\). Output the literals associated with \(U\); their conjunction implies infeasibility under the recorded constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a directed graph from propagation reasons, traverse backward from conflict, and select a cut whose bound literals jointly explain infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outline resembles implication-graph conflict analysis, but the admissible cut, resolution process, treatment of constraints, and conditions making the cut literals imply infeasibility are not specified sufficiently without a CIP conflict-analysis source.

children.title: Bound-Disjunction Learning
children.top_down_role: Learned restrictions expressed through alternatives over variable bounds.

assumptions_latex: A finite conjunction of active bound literals \(L\) has been certified infeasible.
Each literal in \(L\) is a lower- or upper-bound restriction on one variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disjunction of the complementary bound literals is valid for every feasible solution.

notation.meaning: logical complement of a bound literal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Learned disjunction obtained by negating an infeasible conjunction of bound literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\}\) be bound literals satisfying \[F\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^k\{x:x\text{ satisfies }\ell_i\}=\varnothing.\] Then the learned bound disjunction \[\bar\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\bar\ell_k\] is valid for every \(x\in F\). For an integer variable, the complement of \(x_j\leq u\) is \(x_j\geq u+1\), and the complement of \(x_j\geq l\) is \(x_j\leq l-1\). The infeasibility certificate for the conjunction therefore certifies the learned restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a conjunction of variable bounds is infeasible, negate its literals to obtain a bound disjunction valid for every feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Disjunction Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Negating an infeasible conjunction yields the stated valid disjunction, including the integer-bound complements. Nevertheless, the record has no citation, and a source should also establish whether this learning leaf is best represented as a certificate rather than a learning rule or validity property.

children.title: Graph-to-Disjunction Derivation
children.top_down_role: Structural transfer from analyzed conflicts to reusable bound-based restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The implication graph is a directed acyclic graph whose source literals encode branching decisions and propagated bound changes.
A conflict vertex represents a contradiction, and every non-source vertex is justified by its incoming predecessors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned disjunction excludes the analyzed conflicting conjunction while remaining valid for every feasible solution satisfying the graph justifications.

notation.meaning: vertex set on the source side of the selected cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-based derivation of a bound disjunction from a CIP implication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an implication graph ending at a contradiction vertex \(\bot\). Choose a directed cut separating all decision sources from \(\bot\), and let \(C\subseteq V\setminus\{\bot\}\) contain the frontier vertices on the source side whose outgoing arcs cross the cut. If every directed source-to-conflict path meets \(C\), collect the corresponding bound literals \(\ell_v\). The conflicting conjunction is \(\bigwedge_{v\in C}\ell_v\); derive and store its negation
\[D_C=\bigvee_{v\in C}\neg\ell_v.\]
Optionally replace literals by weaker bounds only when the resulting disjunction remains implied by the original CIP constraints. Output \(D_C\) as the learned restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut every path from decisions to contradiction, collect the frontier bound literals, and learn the disjunction of their negations.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-to-Disjunction Derivation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the derivation leaf, and the notation is coherent, but no citation supports the precise cut orientation, frontier convention, or validity-preserving weakening step.

children.title: Learned-Restriction Persistence
children.top_down_role: Scope, aging, locality, and retention of conflict-derived restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Every learned restriction is valid either globally or under an explicitly recorded set of local node assumptions.
Search nodes inherit the assumptions of their ancestors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A learned restriction may be reused exactly at nodes whose active assumptions imply its validity context; globally valid restrictions persist throughout the search tree.

notation.meaning: feasible set of a learned restriction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-scoped persistence of conflict-derived restrictions across a branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original feasible set and let a learned restriction have feasible set \(L\). If \(F\subseteq L\), the restriction is globally valid and may remain active at every search node. If instead the restriction was derived under local assumptions \(A_w\) and satisfies only \(F\cap A_w\subseteq L\), it may remain active at a node \(u\) only when \(A_u\subseteq A_w\), equivalently when the assumptions at \(u\) imply those supporting the derivation. Deletion for memory management may remove a reusable restriction but cannot enlarge the set declared feasible by any still-active learned restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global learned restrictions apply everywhere; local ones persist only where current node assumptions imply their derivation context.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Restriction Persistence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the persistence leaf. The global/local distinction is plausible, but the claimed node-reuse criterion and assumptions-as-sets convention require a specific CIP conflict-learning source.

children.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Explanation System
children.top_down_role: Integration of relaxation infeasibility with constraint-based explanations.

children.title: LP Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility information obtained from linear relaxation states.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation consists of linear inequalities together with current local variable bounds.
The relaxation is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonnegative Farkas multiplier vector identifies a subset of active rows and bounds whose conjunction is infeasible and can seed conflict analysis.

notation.meaning: matrix and right-hand side of all active linear rows and encoded bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-based explanation of infeasible node LP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Normalize the active node LP as \(Ax\le b\), including finite local bounds as rows. An LP-conflict certificate is a vector \(y\ge0\) satisfying
\[y^{\mathsf T}A=0,\qquad y^{\mathsf T}b<0.\]
For every \(x\) satisfying all rows with \(y_i>0\), multiplication and summation would give \(0=y^{\mathsf T}Ax\le y^{\mathsf T}b<0\), which is impossible. Hence the support \(I=\{i:y_i>0\}\) is an infeasible subsystem. Rows in \(I\) arising from local bounds are translated into their bound literals, while structural rows remain reasons, producing an LP-based conflict explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Farkas ray selects active LP rows and local bounds whose conjunction is infeasible, yielding an LP conflict explanation.
knowledge_statements.title: LP Conflicts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits LP conflicts, and the normalized Farkas conditions are standard. However, the record contains proof text and lacks a source for the CIP-specific translation from supported rows and local bounds to a conflict explanation.

children.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations combining relaxation evidence with constraint and domain reasoning.

assumptions_latex: Each inference service returns a reason expressed in constraints, bound literals, or an independently checkable infeasibility certificate.
All local assumptions used by a reason are recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A hybrid explanation is valid when its collected reasons imply contradiction under its recorded context, regardless of which solver service generated each reason.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified infeasibility certificate combining logical, propagation, and relaxation reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hybrid infeasibility explanation for context \(A\) is a finite family \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) of reason predicates obtained from possibly different services, such that each reason is justified by the original model and its recorded antecedents, and
\[F\cap A\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^{k}R_i=\varnothing.\]
The explanation is independently checkable when every propagation reason is an implication valid on \(F\cap A\), every relaxation reason has a valid dual or Farkas certificate, and every logical reason is entailed by an active constraint. Negating the participating assumption or bound literals yields a restriction valid on the same context \(A\); it is global only if no local assumption is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reasons from propagation, logic, and relaxations form a hybrid explanation when their certified conjunction is infeasible in the recorded context.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Explanations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate, but the meanings of the reason predicates and their connection to the literals negated in the learned restriction are not formalized sufficiently to validate the conclusion without a source.

children.title: Relaxation-to-Logic Explanation Transfer
children.top_down_role: Conversion of numerical infeasibility evidence into reusable logical or bound-based explanations.

assumptions_latex: An infeasible relaxation has a valid certificate supported on active structural rows and local bound rows.
Every supported local bound has a corresponding logical bound literal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Translating certified bound rows into literals produces a logically valid conflict clause or bound disjunction in the certificate's validity context.

notation.meaning: support of the relaxation infeasibility certificate
bound literal associated with supported bound row \(i\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-preserving transfer from relaxation infeasibility to logical bound learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an infeasibility certificate with support \(I\), partition \(I=I_s\cup I_b\) into structural rows and current bound rows. Verify the certificate using all supported rows. For every \(i\in I_b\), map the bound row to its active literal \(\ell_i\). Retain structural rows in \(I_s\) as justification, or recursively replace them by valid antecedent literals when such explanations are available. If the resulting literals satisfy
\[F\cap A\cap\bigcap_{i\in I_b}\ell_i=\varnothing,\]
output the logical restriction \(\bigvee_{i\in I_b}\neg\ell_i\). Record \(A\) as its validity context and classify it as global only when the certificate uses no local-only row or assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify the relaxation certificate, translate its supported bound rows to literals, and learn their negated disjunction with the correct validity scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-to-Logic Explanation Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the transfer leaf. A source is needed to justify when structural certificate rows may be retained implicitly or recursively replaced and when the resulting bound disjunction follows in the stated context.

children.title: Explanation Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Tolerance, locality, and representation conditions limiting explanation reuse.

assumptions_latex: A candidate explanation was derived from a relaxation or propagator under a recorded model state.
Search may later change local bounds, rows, or approximations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explanation is reusable only where every dependency remains valid; otherwise treating it as global can exclude feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between globally reusable and context-dependent infeasibility explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an explanation derived at node \(w\) establishes only \(F\cap A_w\subseteq L\). It may be transferred to a node \(u\) only if the active state at \(u\) entails every dependency used in the derivation, including local bounds, locally added rows, relaxation-validity assumptions, and transformations. If \(A_u\not\subseteq A_w\), global reuse is unjustified. Concretely, for \(F=\{0,1\}\), the local assumption \(A_w=\{x=0\}\) permits the learned restriction \(x=0\); applying it outside that branch deletes the feasible point \(x=1\). Thus omission of context metadata destroys soundness even when the original local explanation was correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation cannot outlive a local bound, row, approximation, or transformation on which its validity depends; global reuse may remove feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Validity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind precisely fits the leaf, and the counterexample correctly illustrates unsafe global reuse. The complete list and treatment of CIP dependency contexts remain unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Constraint-Handler Extension Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Solver phases and extension families through which integrated CIP services are realized.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Constraint-handler properties, callbacks, presolvers, propagators, separators, relaxators, and heuristics

children.title: Presearch Processing Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Model conversion, upgrading, simplification, aggregation, and early inference phases.

children.title: Model Transformation
children.top_down_role: Conversion of original model objects into solver-facing variables, constraints, and representations.

assumptions_latex: The original model has feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\).
Each transformation records a reconstruction map and preserves feasibility and objective values on represented solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformed model is search-equivalent to the original when feasible solutions correspond through reconstruction and have equal objective values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-preserving conversion from the original CIP model to its internal search model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A model transformation replaces an original CIP \((F,f)\) by an internal model \((F',f')\), together with a reconstruction map \(\rho:F'\to F\). It is search-equivalent when
\[f'(z)=f(\rho(z))\quad\text{for every }z\in F',\]
and for every \(x\in F\) there exists \(z\in F'\) with \(\rho(z)=x\) and \(f'(z)=f(x)\). Variables, constraints, and handler-owned data referenced after transformation must be mapped to their transformed counterparts. Consequently, infeasibility and optimal values are preserved, and every transformed feasible or optimal solution can be reconstructed as an original feasible or optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model transformation creates an internal search model with mappings that preserve feasibility, objective values, and reconstruction of original solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Transformation
