intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits model transformation. The stated surjective feasible-solution correspondence is a strong form of equivalence, and a CIP lifecycle source is required to establish that this is the intended transformation contract.

children.title: CIP Presolve
children.top_down_role: Simplification, aggregation, upgrading, and early inference before main search.

assumptions_latex: Every presolve reduction supplies a validity condition and any data required to reconstruct eliminated variables.
Presolve terminates when no enabled reduction changes the model or a stopping limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a certified infeasibility conclusion or a reduced CIP equivalent to the input for optimization and solution reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterated, handler-coordinated reduction of a transformed CIP before tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(M_0\) as the transformed CIP and \(\rho\) as the identity reconstruction. In each round, enabled handlers apply sound reductions such as bound tightening, redundant-constraint deletion, aggregation, coefficient strengthening, and constraint upgrading. A reduction from \(M_t\) to \(M_{t+1}\) must preserve infeasibility and optimal value and extend \(\rho\) so solutions of \(M_{t+1}\) reconstruct to solutions of \(M_t\). Propagate every change to affected handlers and repeat until a fixed point or prescribed limit. If a handler certifies \(F(M_t)=\varnothing\), output infeasible; otherwise output the final reduced model and accumulated reconstruction data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CIP presolve repeatedly applies sound handler reductions, propagates changes, and returns infeasibility or an equivalent reduced model with reconstruction data.
knowledge_statements.title: CIP Presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits CIP presolve. The reduction loop is plausible, but its claims about optimal-value preservation, reconstruction, handler coordination, and termination statuses require an authoritative CIP source.

children.title: Handler Initialization
children.top_down_role: Preparation of constraint-handler state, relaxation interfaces, and event dependencies.

assumptions_latex: Model transformation is complete before transformed-problem initialization.
Each constraint handler declares the transformed constraints and shared services it requires.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful initialization establishes all handler-owned search data and registrations needed for subsequent presolve and node processing.

notation.meaning: set of transformed constraints owned by handler \(h\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required consistency condition for initializing a constraint handler before presolve and search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint handler \(h\) is initialized for the transformed model precisely when its state \(S_h\) satisfies all of the following: every constraint in \(C_h\) refers only to live transformed objects; all handler-owned indices, watches, event subscriptions, and auxiliary relaxation objects agree with \(C_h\); every registered callback has its declared data available; and repeated initialization does not duplicate registrations. If initialization creates a row, variable, or auxiliary constraint, that object must be linked to the transformed model and included in later consistency updates. Search services for \(h\) may be scheduled only after these conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A handler is initialized when its transformed constraints, internal data, watches, callbacks, and auxiliary objects are live, consistent, and uniquely registered.
knowledge_statements.title: Handler Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the initialization leaf, but watches, subscriptions, callback data, auxiliary objects, and idempotent registration are implementation-specific lifecycle requirements with no supporting API or architecture citation.

children.title: Presearch State Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of transformed objects, presolved structure, and initialized plugin state.

assumptions_latex: Transformation, handler initialization, and presolve have completed without an infeasibility certificate.
Every accepted reduction has updated all dependent model and handler data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tree search may start only if the reduced model, reconstruction data, and all handler states describe the same current problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-component invariant required at the transition from presolve to tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presearch state consistency holds for \((M^*,\rho,(S_h)_h)\) when: every active constraint and variable in \(M^*\) has valid identifiers and bounds; every handler state \(S_h\) references exactly the live transformed objects it owns or observes; cached activities, watches, locks, rows, and event registrations reflect the final presolved domains; no deleted object remains reachable by a scheduled service; and \(\rho\) reconstructs every feasible solution of \(M^*\) into an original feasible solution with the same objective value. The root node may be created only after these predicates hold simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before root creation, the reduced model, handler caches and registrations, live objects, bounds, and solution reconstruction map must agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Presearch State Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the consistency leaf. The proposed invariant is coherent but combines implementation-specific ownership, cache, scheduling, and reconstruction requirements that need a concrete CIP architecture source.

children.title: Node-Processing Service Cycle
children.top_down_role: Repeated handler participation in node processing and candidate evaluation.

children.title: Node Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference performed during node processing.

assumptions_latex: A search node has an active local domain and a set of constraints valid at that node.
Each propagation inference can provide a valid reason from active constraints and antecedent bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation returns a local fixpoint, a resource-limited state, or a certified contradiction, while recording reasons for every accepted domain reduction.

notation.meaning: variable domain vector after propagation round \(t\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Handler-driven domain propagation at one node of the shared search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D^0\) with the node's inherited and branching bounds. Repeatedly schedule every handler \(h\) affected by a domain change and compute \(D^{t+1}=P_h(D^t)\subseteq D^t\). Accept each tightening only with a reason entailed by constraints active at the node, notify all dependent handlers, and continue until no scheduled handler tightens a domain or a resource limit is reached. If some component domain becomes empty, return cutoff together with the recorded reasons. Otherwise return the final domains; at an unlimited termination they satisfy \(P_h(D^*)=D^*\) for every enabled handler \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a node, handlers repeatedly tighten domains with recorded reasons until fixpoint, limit, or an explained empty domain is reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits node propagation. A source is needed for the handler scheduling model, reason requirement, resource-limited status, and simultaneous fixpoint claim, particularly because monotonicity alone does not establish termination.

children.title: Node Separation
children.top_down_role: Generation of relaxation-valid restrictions at a search node.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation has solution \(\bar x\).
Every generated inequality is valid for all integer-feasible solutions in its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node separation adds only valid inequalities violated by the current relaxation solution and returns either a strengthened relaxation, cutoff, or no-cut status.

notation.meaning: integer-feasible set valid at the node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-handler separation of a fractional or constraint-violating node relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node \(u\) and relaxation solution \(\bar x\), invoke eligible separators and constraint handlers. A returned inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) is accepted only if \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in F_u\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon\) for the prescribed feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Add accepted inequalities to the local or global relaxation according to their validity scope, resolve the relaxation, and repeat subject to scheduling and resource limits. Return cutoff if the strengthened relaxation is infeasible, separated if at least one accepted cut changed it, and no-cut otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Handlers add scope-valid inequalities violated by the current relaxation point, re-solve, and report strengthening, cutoff, or no cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits node separation, and the validity and violation tests are mathematically coherent. The precise handler workflow, tolerance convention, validity scopes, and return-status semantics require a CIP-specific source.

children.title: Node Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Handler responses to unresolved relaxation or solution candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Enforcement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enforcement service for an active constraint handler at one search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_v\) be the local domain at node \(v\), let \(x^*\) solve the current node relaxation, and let \(\mathcal C_v\) be the active constraints owned by a handler. The enforcement oracle returns exactly one status in \(\{\mathrm{feasible},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{reduce},\mathrm{branch},\mathrm{infeasible}\}\). It returns feasible only if \(x^*\) satisfies every constraint in \(\mathcal C_v\); otherwise it must produce, respectively, a valid separating inequality, a sound domain reduction, an exhaustive branching disjunction, or a certificate that \(D_v\cap\bigcap_{C\in\mathcal C_v}C=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a node, an enforcement handler either accepts the relaxation point or returns a valid cut, domain reduction, exhaustive branch, or infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in D_v\) is available from the current node relaxation.
Every returned inference or disjunction is valid for \(D_v\cap\bigcap_{C\in\mathcal C_v}C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is accepted only when all active handled constraints are satisfied; otherwise node processing receives a sound corrective action.

notation.meaning: local variable domain at node v
active handled constraints at node v

review_flags: Exact handler-result semantics require an authoritative CIP framework source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Node Enforcement, but the claim that the oracle returns exactly one of five statuses and must provide the stated artifacts is framework-specific and may omit legitimate enforcement results. An authoritative CIP handler API or architecture reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Node-Service Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Invocation order, frequency, priority, and repetition of node-level handler services.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Service Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-and-delay scheduling of propagation, separation, and enforcement services.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the finite set of node services. Each \(s\in S\) has priority \(p_s\), frequency predicate \(f_s(v,r)\), and delay predicate \(d_s(\sigma)\), where \(\sigma\) is the current node state. In round \(r\), schedule eligible services satisfying \(f_s(v,r)\) in nonincreasing \(p_s\), omitting a delayed service while \(d_s(\sigma)\) holds. After any cut, domain reduction, or branching decision, update \(\sigma\) and restart every service whose eligibility may have changed. Stop when no eligible service can change \(\sigma\), or the node is pruned or branched.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node services run by eligibility and priority, with permitted delays; state-changing results trigger reconsideration until quiescence, pruning, or branching.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and every service call terminates.
A service result identifies whether it changed the node state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cycle terminates at service quiescence or with a node-pruning or branching action.
review_flags: Scheduling policies are framework-specific and need a CIP implementation reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the scheduling leaf, but the restart policy is implementation-specific. Finiteness of the service set and termination of individual calls do not imply termination of repeated state-changing rounds, so the stated quiescence conclusion requires stronger hypotheses and an authoritative source.

children.title: Plugin-Event Service Coupling
children.top_down_role: Propagators, separators, relaxators, branching rules, heuristics, and state observers.

children.title: CIP Plugin Families
children.top_down_role: Propagators, separators, relaxators, branching rules, heuristics, and related solver extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: CIP Plugin Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional partition of plugins in a single-tree constraint integer programming solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the plugin system as a typed family \(\mathcal P=\mathcal H\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal R\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal S\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal B\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal N\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal E\), where \(\mathcal H\) contains constraint handlers, \(\mathcal R\) relaxation solvers, \(\mathcal S\) separators, \(\mathcal B\) branching rules, \(\mathcal N\) node selectors, and \(\mathcal E\) event handlers. Each plugin exposes callbacks only for its declared type. Solver state changes are admitted only through callback results satisfying the validity contract of that type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CIP solver partitions extensions into typed plugin families, each having defined callbacks and validity obligations for any state changes it requests.
assumptions_latex: Every installed plugin has one declared service type in the displayed partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a disjoint typed interface decomposition of the solver extension layer.
review_flags: The exact plugin taxonomy varies across CIP frameworks and requires a primary architecture source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate role, but the six displayed families are not established as an exhaustive disjoint partition of a CIP plugin system, and the one-type-per-plugin assumption is framework-dependent. A primary architecture or plugin API source is required.

children.title: Event Services
children.top_down_role: Notifications for bound changes, node transitions, solution events, and solver-state changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Event Services
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subscription and dispatch semantics for solver-state events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be event types and \(L(t)\) the ordered listener set for \(t\in\mathcal T\). Registration adds a listener to \(L(t)\), deregistration removes it, and occurrence of event \(e=(t,\pi,\tau)\) creates an immutable record containing its type, payload, and sequence time. Dispatch invokes each listener present in a snapshot of \(L(t)\). Callback-generated state modifications are submitted as validated solver actions; they do not retroactively alter \(e\) or the listener snapshot used for its dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Event services manage typed subscriptions and dispatch immutable event records to a listener snapshot, while routing callback changes through validated solver actions.
assumptions_latex: Event sequence times \(\tau\) are totally ordered within one solver execution.
Each callback terminates and obeys the solver action interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every emitted event is dispatched consistently to the listeners subscribed at its dispatch snapshot.

notation.meaning: typed event with payload and sequence time

review_flags: Dispatch ordering and mutation semantics require a framework-specific event API source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Event Services, but immutable event records, total sequence ordering, listener snapshots, and mutation routing are implementation-specific guarantees. They need support from a precisely located event API or architecture source.

children.title: Plugin–Event Coupling
children.top_down_role: Subscriptions, callbacks, state dependencies, and communication between plugins and event mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Plugin–Event Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable coupling between plugin callbacks and typed solver events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(\mathcal P\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal T,A)\) be a directed bipartite graph. An arc \((p,t)\in A\) means plugin \(p\) subscribes to event type \(t\); an arc \((t,p)\in A\) means an action of \(p\) may emit type \(t\). For any emitted event, only plugins joined by a subscription arc are eligible for notification. Removing \((p,t)\) therefore removes that notification dependency without changing the mathematical feasibility region, provided \(p\) is observational for \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bipartite graph records which plugins consume or emit events; removing an observational subscription removes notification coupling without changing feasibility.
assumptions_latex: All plugin-event dependencies are declared by arcs of \(G\).
Plugin \(p\) is observational for \(t\), so its callback requests no feasibility-changing action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting \((p,t)\) suppresses notifications of type \(t\) to \(p\) while preserving the feasible region.
review_flags: The coupling model is an architectural abstraction needing an authoritative CIP source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the leaf, but the bipartite graph is a synthesized abstraction rather than an established CIP interface property. The completeness of declared arcs and the effect of removing a subscription require an authoritative source.

children.title: Extension Interaction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ordering, ownership, reentrancy, and performance limits across interacting solver extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Extension Interaction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for extension-induced changes to shared solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) be the feasible set represented at node \(v\), and let an extension propose transition \(\sigma\mapsto\sigma'\). The transition is admissible only if every removed point is provably infeasible, every added inequality is valid for \(F_v\), every branching family \((F_i)_{i=1}^k\) satisfies \(F_v\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k F_i\), and all shared-state changes occur through declared solver interfaces. Undeclared mutation, invalid relaxation strengthening, or nonexhaustive branching lies outside the extension boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extension may alter shared state only through declared interfaces and only with sound reductions, valid inequalities, or exhaustive branching.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\) denotes the node-feasible set before the proposed transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma\mapsto\sigma'\) is admissible exactly when its mathematical changes are valid and its state changes use declared interfaces.

notation.meaning: feasible set represented at node v
solver states before and after an extension action
child feasible sets proposed by branching

review_flags: Interface restrictions and callback contracts require a primary CIP framework source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is an appropriate role, but the claimed exact characterization of admissibility is too broad: the listed requirements do not cover all solver-state, objective, numerical, and lifecycle invariants. A primary framework contract is needed to determine the correct necessary and sufficient conditions.

children.title: Constraint Lifecycle State System
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle management for delayed, useful, obsolete, local, and global constraints.

children.title: Constraint Activation
children.top_down_role: Enabled, disabled, delayed, or conditionally active constraint states.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation state of a handled constraint at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint \(C\) and node \(v\), define the activation indicator \(a_C(v)\in\{0,1\}\). The constraint is active at \(v\) when \(a_C(v)=1\), meaning that its handler may use \(C\) for the lifecycle services enabled by its flags, such as propagation, separation, or enforcement. It is inactive when \(a_C(v)=0\). Activation changes service eligibility but does not delete \(C\) or alter the feasible set represented by \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activation makes a constraint eligible for its enabled handler services at a node; deactivation suspends those services without deleting the constraint.
assumptions_latex: Constraint \(C\) is present in the solver at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_C(v)=1\) is precisely the predicate that \(C\) is eligible for its enabled node services at \(v\).

notation.meaning: activation indicator of C at v

review_flags: Activation semantics and enabled-service flags require a CIP lifecycle reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Constraint Activation, but identifying activation precisely with eligibility for enabled propagation, separation, or enforcement services is framework-specific. The assertion that activation never changes represented feasibility also needs qualification from a lifecycle specification.

children.title: Constraint Aging
children.top_down_role: Usefulness tracking, retention, retirement, and reactivation of constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inactivity-based aging and retirement of removable constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each removable constraint \(C\) an age \(g_C\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), initialized to zero, and threshold \(G_C\geq1\). After a service round, set \(g_C\leftarrow0\) if \(C\) produced a prescribed useful effect; otherwise set \(g_C\leftarrow g_C+1\). When \(g_C\geq G_C\), the solver may deactivate or delete \(C\) only if \(C\) is marked removable and deletion preserves the solver's validity invariants. Essential model constraints are never deleted solely because of age.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A removable constraint gains age during unproductive rounds, resets after useful work, and may be retired at a threshold without compromising validity.
assumptions_latex: The solver defines which service outcomes count as useful effects.
Only constraints explicitly marked removable are eligible for age-based deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Age-based retirement can remove only a removable, sufficiently old constraint while preserving solver validity.
review_flags: Usefulness, reset, and deletion policies differ by CIP implementation and need sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Constraint Aging, but the per-round increment, useful-effect reset, threshold rule, and distinction between deactivation and deletion vary across implementations. A directly located CIP aging specification is required.

children.title: Constraint Locality
children.top_down_role: Node-local, subtree-local, and globally valid constraint scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Locality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-subtree scope of a local constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a rooted search tree and \(v\in T\). A constraint \(C\) introduced locally at \(v\) has scope \(\operatorname{desc}(v)=\{w\in T: v\preceq w\}\), where \(v\preceq w\) means that \(v\) is an ancestor of \(w\). Thus \(C\) may restrict the represented feasible set at \(v\) and its descendants, but it must not restrict any node \(u\notin\operatorname{desc}(v)\). A global constraint instead has scope equal to every live node where it is applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint local to a node applies only at that node and its descendants, never outside the rooted subtree.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a rooted search tree with ancestor order \(\preceq\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scope of a constraint local to \(v\) is exactly \(\operatorname{desc}(v)\).

notation.meaning: v is an ancestor of w

review_flags: Standard branch-and-bound locality semantics need a direct CIP lifecycle source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits Constraint Locality, but no evidence or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied. A direct CIP lifecycle source should confirm that local constraints have exactly the stated subtree scope and clarify the meaning of applicability for global constraints.

children.title: Lifecycle State Interactions
children.top_down_role: Effects of activity, age, and validity scope on propagation, separation, and enforcement.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle State Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility rules among presence, locality, activation, and age.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every constraint \(C\) and node \(v\), let \(q_C(v)\), \(s_C(v)\), and \(a_C(v)\) denote presence, scope membership, and activation. Lifecycle consistency requires \(a_C(v)\leq q_C(v)s_C(v)\): an active constraint must be present and in scope. Deactivation may change \(a_C(v)\) without changing \(q_C(v)\); deletion sets \(q_C(w)=a_C(w)=0\) at every affected node \(w\). Aging may trigger deactivation or permitted deletion, but it cannot enlarge scope or activate an out-of-scope constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activation requires presence and scope; deactivation preserves presence, deletion removes both, and aging cannot enlarge scope or activate an inapplicable constraint.
assumptions_latex: All lifecycle indicators take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
Deletion respects the constraint's local or global scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every valid lifecycle transition preserves \(a_C(v)\leq q_C(v)s_C(v)\) at every node \(v\).

notation.meaning: presence indicator for C at v
scope-membership indicator for C at v
activation indicator for C at v

review_flags: The formal state-transition model is synthesized and needs confirmation against a CIP lifecycle specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the interaction leaf, but the indicator model and deletion effects are synthesized and may not match an actual CIP lifecycle. In particular, the affected-node semantics of deletion and the relation among presence, scope, and activation require authoritative confirmation.

children.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Master–subproblem decomposition in which general inference and proof structures replace the exclusive reliance on LP duality.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Basic theory, inference duality, classical realization, and applications

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition for Large-Scale Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Fundamentals, classical Benders specialization, branch-and-check, planning, and scheduling
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition for Large-Scale Optimization

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Master-Subproblem Decomposition Pair
children.top_down_role: Structural separation of coordinating decisions from conditional feasibility or optimization reasoning.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition for Large-Scale Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition for Large-Scale Optimization

children.title: Master Representation Architecture
children.top_down_role: Coordinating variables, projected structure, and master-side approximations.

children.title: Master Decisions
children.top_down_role: Coordinating variables retained in the decomposition master.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master variables fixing the decisions passed to logic-based subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original feasible set be \(F=\{(y,x)\in Y\times X: H(y,x)\}\), where \(y\) contains the complicating decisions and \(x\) the remaining decisions. The master decisions are the components of \(y\) chosen by the master problem. For a master assignment \(\bar y\), the associated subproblem feasible set is \(X(\bar y)=\{x\in X:H(\bar y,x)\}\). A valid logic-based Benders iteration tests \(X(\bar y)\) and returns information expressed solely in master variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master decisions are the complicating variables fixed before solving a subproblem; subproblem feedback must be expressible in those master variables.
assumptions_latex: The variables admit a partition \((y,x)\in Y\times X\).
Fixing \(y=\bar y\) leaves a well-defined subproblem over \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is the master-decision vector and \(X(\bar y)\) is the subproblem feasible set induced by assignment \(\bar y\).

notation.meaning: subproblem feasible set after fixing the master decision

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

review_flags: The locator supports decomposition structure provisionally; logic-based Benders terminology requires confirmation.

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Master Decisions and the variable partition is coherent. However, the cited block-structure section does not specifically support the logic-based Benders requirement that subproblem feedback be expressed solely in master variables. A dedicated logic-based Benders source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Master Linking Structure
children.top_down_role: Relations connecting coordinating decisions to conditional subproblem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Linking Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based representation linking master assignments to subproblem feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{(y,x)\in Y\times X:H(y,x)\}\), define the exact feasible master projection \(P_Y(F)=\{y\in Y:\exists x\in X,\ H(y,x)\}\). A master representation has the form \(M=\{(y,\theta):y\in Y,\ R_0(y,\theta),\ B_k(y,\theta)\text{ for }k\in K\}\), where \(R_0\) is an initial relaxation and each \(B_k\) is a valid logic-based Benders constraint. Feasibility cuts progressively enforce the linking requirement \(y\in P_Y(F)\); optimality cuts additionally bound the subproblem value represented by \(\theta\).

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(X\) are the master and subproblem domains.
Every added constraint \(B_k\) is valid for the projected original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linking structure is exact when the projection of \(M\) onto \(y\) equals \(P_Y(F)\), with \(\theta\) correctly representing the subproblem value when present.

children.title: Initial Master Relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Initial Master Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph master used before any logic-based Benders cuts are generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the original problem be 
\[\inf\{c(x)+f(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in Y(x)\},\]
and define the subproblem value by \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)\), with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when \(Y(x)=\varnothing\). If \(M_0\supseteq\{x\in X:Y(x)\neq\varnothing\}\) and \(L_0(x)\le Q(x)\) for every feasible master decision, then an initial master relaxation is
\[\inf\{c(x)+\eta:x\in M_0,\ \eta\ge L_0(x)\}.\]
Its feasible region may admit subproblem-infeasible decisions and underestimate finite recourse values; subsequent feasibility and optimality cuts remove these deficiencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The initial master optimizes master costs plus a valid lower estimate of the subproblem value, before feasibility or optimality cuts are added.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the domain of master decisions.
\(c(x)\) and \(f(x,y)\) are extended-real-valued objective terms.
\(L_0(x)\) is a valid lower bound wherever the original subproblem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in M_0,\,\eta\ge L_0(x)}(c(x)+\eta)\le \inf_{x\in X,\,y\in Y(x)}(c(x)+f(x,y))\).

children.title: Master Representation Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Coverage, strength, and size of the initial coordinating representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Representation Adequacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for a lower-bounding logic-based Benders master representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For 
\[v^*=\inf\{c(x)+f(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in Y(x)\},\]
a master representation \(M\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\) is adequate as a relaxation if every original feasible pair \((x,y)\) has at least one represented pair \((x,\eta)\in M\) satisfying \(\eta\le f(x,y)\). Equivalently, its lower-envelope function \(\ell_M(x)=\inf\{\eta:(x,\eta)\in M\}\) must satisfy \(\ell_M(x)\le Q(x)\) whenever \(Q(x)<+\infty\). Consequently, minimizing \(c(x)+\eta\) over \(M\) yields a valid lower bound on \(v^*\); equality additionally requires an exact represented optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master is adequate when it represents every feasible master decision with a subproblem-value estimate no larger than the true value.
assumptions_latex: The original infimum is well defined in the extended reals.
The master objective is \(c(x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(x,\eta)\in M}(c(x)+\eta)\le v^*\).

notation.meaning: master feasible set in decision-epigraph space
lowest value represented by the master at x

children.title: Feasibility Subproblems

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subproblem whose sole role is testing extendability of a fixed master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) be fixed by the master and let \(Y(x)=\{y\in Y:g(x,y)\le0,\ h(x,y)=0\}\). The associated feasibility subproblem is the decision problem
\[\operatorname{FEAS}(x):\quad\text{find }y\in Y(x),\]
or an equivalent phase-I optimization problem having optimum zero exactly when \(Y(x)\neq\varnothing\). A feasible output certifies that \(x\) extends to a feasible original solution. A sound infeasibility certificate establishes \(Y(x)=\varnothing\) and supports a master feasibility cut that excludes \(x\), or a justified family containing \(x\), without excluding any extendable master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility subproblem tests whether a fixed master decision can be extended to satisfy all remaining constraints.
assumptions_latex: The master decision \(x\) is fixed during the subproblem solve.
Subproblem infeasibility can be certified soundly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{FEAS}(x)\text{ is feasible}\iff Y(x)\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Optimization Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Conditional evaluation of recourse cost or objective contribution under master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-producing subproblem induced by a fixed feasible master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed master decision \(x\in X\), the optimization subproblem is
\[Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}.\]
If \(Y(x)=\varnothing\), set \(Q(x)=+\infty\). Otherwise, a solution \(y_x\in Y(x)\) with \(f(x,y_x)=Q(x)\) supplies a feasible completion and its exact recourse cost. A valid master optimality cut is any constraint imposing a lower estimator \(B_x(z)\le Q(z)\) on its declared domain and satisfying \(B_x(x)=Q(x)\) when exactness at the evaluated decision is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimization subproblem computes the best remaining objective value after the master decision is fixed.
assumptions_latex: The master decision is fixed while optimizing over \(y\).
The infimum is interpreted in the extended reals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)\), with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) if \(Y(x)=\varnothing\).

children.title: Subproblem Role Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for using feasibility-only, optimization, or mixed subproblem roles.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Role Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for choosing feasibility-only versus value-producing subproblem inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the decomposed objective be \(c(x)+Q(x)\). A feasibility subproblem is sufficient only when the subproblem contributes no decision-dependent objective information to the master, meaning that on every extendable decision its contribution is a known function already represented in the master. If unknown finite values \(Q(x)\) affect comparison of master decisions, an optimization subproblem or another sound value oracle is required. Thus role selection is determined by the information needed for correctness: extendability requires feasibility inference, whereas globally valid lower bounding of an unrepresented recourse term requires value inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use feasibility subproblems to test extendability; use optimization subproblems when unresolved subproblem costs influence which master decision is best.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition separates master cost \(c(x)\) from subproblem value \(Q(x)\).
Cuts returned by either role are valid on their declared master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)\text{ unrepresented and decision-dependent}\implies\text{value inference is required for objective correctness}.\)

notation.meaning: objective contribution represented directly in the master

children.title: Master Feedback by Subproblem Role

knowledge_statements.title: Master Feedback by Subproblem Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between subproblem outcomes and valid master feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a queried master decision \(x^k\), subproblem feedback has two distinct validity obligations. If \(Y(x^k)=\varnothing\), a feasibility inference is a set \(F_k\subseteq X\) such that every extendable decision belongs to \(F_k\) and \(x^k\notin F_k\); the master adds \(x\in F_k\). If \(Q(x^k)<+\infty\), a value inference is a function \(B_k:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) satisfying \(B_k(x)\le Q(x)\) on its declared domain; the master adds \(\eta\ge B_k(x)\). Feasibility feedback removes invalid decisions, while value feedback raises valid lower estimates without removing any true epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible subproblems return feasibility cuts; feasible optimization subproblems return lower bounds on subproblem value for the master epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=+\infty\) exactly when no feasible subproblem extension exists.
Every returned inference is valid beyond the queried point as declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(x^k)=\varnothing\Rightarrow x^k\notin F_k\); \(Q(x^k)<+\infty\Rightarrow \eta\ge B_k(x)\text{ is valid whenever }\eta\ge Q(x)\).

children.title: Independent Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Components with no cross-component subproblem interaction.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional independence of subproblem blocks after fixing master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each fixed \(x\in X\), subproblem blocks indexed by \(k\in K\) are independent when
\[Y(x)=\prod_{k\in K}Y_k(x)\quad\text{and}\quad f(x,y)=\sum_{k\in K}f_k(x,y_k),\]
with no constraint or subproblem variable shared between distinct blocks after \(x\) is fixed. When all block infima are well defined and the finite sum convention applies, the value function separates as
\[Q(x)=\sum_{k\in K}Q_k(x),\qquad Q_k(x)=\inf_{y_k\in Y_k(x)}f_k(x,y_k).\]
Hence the block problems may be solved independently, including in parallel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblems are independent when fixing the master makes their feasible sets Cartesian and their objective additive, with no shared subproblem decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Each block infimum is well defined and no indeterminate extended-real sum occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{k\in K}Q_k(x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise master epigraph representation for separable independent subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(Q(x)=\sum_{k\in K}Q_k(x)\). A disaggregated master represents subproblem value using one epigraph variable \(\eta_k\) per block and imposes separately generated bounds
\[\eta_k\ge B_{k,j}(x)\qquad(k\in K,\ j\in J_k),\]
where every \(B_{k,j}(x)\le Q_k(x)\) on the master domain. Its objective contains
\[c(x)+\sum_{k\in K}\eta_k.\]
This is a valid lower-bounding representation because summing the block inequalities cannot exceed the total subproblem value. It preserves block-specific inference instead of aggregating all block feedback into one inequality.

children.title: Coupled Subproblems

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of conditional product structure among subproblem blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Subproblem blocks are coupled at a fixed master decision \(x\) when their feasible set cannot be written as \(\prod_{k\in K}Y_k(x)\), or their objective cannot be written as \(\sum_{k\in K}f_k(x,y_k)\), because a residual constraint, shared variable, or nonseparable term links two or more blocks. In that case, independently minimizing nominal block problems does not generally determine
\[Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(x,y).\]
A correct decomposition must retain the coupling in a joint subproblem or introduce coordinating variables, constraints, or dual information whose validity recovers the omitted linkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblems are coupled when shared variables, linking constraints, or nonseparable costs remain after the master decision is fixed.
assumptions_latex: The proposed blocks are indexed by a finite set \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(x)\neq\prod_{k\in K}Y_k(x)\text{ or }f(x,y)\neq\sum_{k\in K}f_k(x,y_k)\Rightarrow Q(x)\text{ need not equal }\sum_{k\in K}Q_k(x).\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounding surrogate obtained by enlarging the fixed-master subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed master decision \(x\), let
\[Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}.\]
A subproblem relaxation replaces \(Y(x)\) by a tractable set \(R(x)\supseteq Y(x)\), and optionally replaces the objective by \(\underline f(x,y)\le f(x,y)\) on \(Y(x)\), to define
\[Q_R(x)=\inf\{\underline f(x,y):y\in R(x)\}.\]
Whenever the extended-real infima are well defined, \(Q_R(x)\le Q(x)\). Thus relaxation infeasibility certifies original infeasibility, while relaxation feasibility alone does not certify an original feasible extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem relaxation enlarges the feasible set or lowers its objective, producing a tractable lower bound on the true subproblem value.

\[R(x)=\varnothing\Longrightarrow Y(x)=\varnothing.\]
A restricted surrogate \(S(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Value Checks

children.title: Inference Proof Objects

knowledge_statements.title: Inference Proof Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proof objects for conditional conclusions returned by a logic-based Benders subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be the master domain, let \(Q:Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the subproblem value function, and let \(R\subseteq Y\). An inference proof object is a finite, independently checkable object \(\pi\) for which a verifier \(V\) returns one of the conclusions \(V(\pi,R)=\operatorname{LB}(\beta)\) or \(V(\pi,R)=\operatorname{EXCL}\). Sound verification means, respectively, \[V(\pi,R)=\operatorname{LB}(\beta)\Longrightarrow (\forall y\in R)\ Q(y)\geq\beta,\] or \[V(\pi,R)=\operatorname{EXCL}\Longrightarrow (\forall y\in R)\ Q(y)=+\infty.\] The object records the inference premises, permitted inference rules, derived statements, and terminal conclusion needed by \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof object is finite verifier-readable evidence that every master assignment in a stated region has a given subproblem lower bound or is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq Y\) is explicitly encoded.
\(V\) checks every recorded inference against a specified rule system.
