children.title: Classical Benders as an LP-Inference Specialization
children.top_down_role: The linear-duality realization of the broader inference-based framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Benders as an LP-Inference Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Benders cuts viewed as inference certificates supplied by LP duality and Farkas alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\), consider \[Q(y)=\min\{d^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\geq b-By,\ x\geq0\}.\] If this linear program has a finite optimum, strong duality gives \[Q(y)=\max\{u^{\mathsf T}(b-By):A^{\mathsf T}u\leq d,\ u\geq0\}.\] Hence every dual-feasible \(u\) is an inference certificate for the globally valid optimality cut \(\theta\geq u^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\). If a Farkas ray \(r\geq0\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}r\leq0\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}(b-B\bar y)>0\), it certifies infeasibility at \(\bar y\) and yields the feasibility cut \(r^{\mathsf T}(b-By)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical Benders is the linear case in which dual solutions certify recourse lower bounds and Farkas rays certify infeasibility, producing optimality and feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a finite-dimensional linear program.
Strong LP duality and the relevant Farkas alternative apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual points and rays instantiate inference proof objects whose conclusions are classical Benders cuts.
review_flags: The mathematical specialization is standard, but no supplied locator specifically supports classical Benders dual cuts.
standard_field_rationale: LP strong duality and Farkas alternatives furnish the two classical Benders certificate types.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LP-duality and Farkas formulas have the standard sign pattern and the representation kind fits the specialization leaf. However, no cited locator supports the Benders correspondence, and the dimensions and domains of the LP data and epigraph variable are not fully specified.

children.title: Non-LP Benders Specialization Family
children.top_down_role: Inference systems whose proof structures arise from non-LP subproblems.

children.title: CP Specializations
children.top_down_role: Inference structures originating in constraint-programming subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: CP Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based Benders realization whose subproblem and inference certificates use constraint-programming propagation and explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in Y\) fix master decisions and let the subproblem be a finite-domain constraint program \(P(y)\) with value \(Q(y)\). A CP specialization supplies an explanation-producing inference engine that, after solving or propagating \(P(\bar y)\), returns a region \(R\ni\bar y\) and either \[(\forall y\in R)\ Q(y)\geq\beta\] or \[(\forall y\in R)\ P(y)\text{ is infeasible}.\] The explanation must identify master literals and sound CP inference rules sufficient for the conclusion. Translating the explanation into a master constraint gives, respectively, a conditional optimality cut or a nogood excluding \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a CP specialization, propagation or search explanations identify master conditions that imply a recourse bound or infeasibility, and these explanations become master cuts.
assumptions_latex: Each master assignment defines a finite-domain CP subproblem.
Every explanation step is checkable under the declared CP semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sound CP explanation represents a conditional Benders certificate and induces a valid master cut.

notation.meaning: Master region covered by the CP explanation.
Optimal subproblem value, with infinity for infeasibility.

review_flags: The supplied CP textbook locator introduces CP but does not establish this logic-based Benders specialization.
A source on explanation-based CP subproblem cuts is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and finite-domain CP scope fit the leaf, but the available general CP textbook locator does not support the claimed explanation-based logic-based Benders translation.

children.title: Combinatorial Specializations
children.top_down_role: Inference structures originating in discrete combinatorial subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders specialization using discrete structural arguments instead of LP dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a discrete master domain and let \(Q(y)\) be the optimum of a combinatorial subproblem. A combinatorial specialization replaces an LP-dual certificate by a polynomially or finitely checkable witness \(w\) and a verifier establishing, on some \(R\subseteq Y\), either \[(\forall y\in R)\ Q(y)\geq L_w(y)\] or \[(\forall y\in R)\ Q(y)=+\infty.\] The function \(L_w\) may arise from counting, packing, covering, matching, path, or exchange arguments. The corresponding master cut is \(y\in R\Rightarrow\theta\geq L_w(y)\), or \(y\notin R\) in the infeasible case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combinatorial specialization derives Benders cuts from checkable discrete structures such as packings, paths, or counting arguments rather than from linear-programming duality.
assumptions_latex: The witness semantics determine a checkable implication over the declared region \(R\).
\(\theta\) is the master recourse-value variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The witness-defined implication yields a valid conditional optimality or feasibility cut.

notation.meaning: Scope on which the witness conclusion is valid.

review_flags: The specialization family is broad; a canonical source is required to delimit its accepted witness classes.
No supplied locator specifically supports combinatorial logic-based Benders inference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record plausibly represents combinatorial inference as a non-LP Benders specialization, but its broad witness classes and certificate claims have no inspectable supporting locator.

children.title: Problem-Specific Specializations
children.top_down_role: Inference structures tailored to recognizable application structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Specific Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders specialization based on application-specific valid inference rules and certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the value function of an application-specific subproblem. A problem-specific specialization consists of a certificate language \(\mathcal C\), a verifier \(V\), and a translation \(T\) such that every accepted \(c\in\mathcal C\) identifies a scope \(R_c\subseteq Y\) and a conclusion \(Q(y)\geq L_c(y)\) or \(Q(y)=+\infty\) for all \(y\in R_c\). The translated constraint \(T(c)\) must be logically implied by that conclusion over the master domain. Thus domain-specific scheduling, routing, or allocation arguments are admissible precisely when their verifier and translation are sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-specific specialization defines its own checkable certificate language and converts every accepted domain argument into a master cut valid on the certificate’s scope.
assumptions_latex: The application defines exact semantics for certificates in \(\mathcal C\).
The translation \(T\) preserves every accepted certificate conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(c)=\operatorname{accept}\Rightarrow T(c)\) is valid for the original decomposed model.

notation.meaning: Translation from certificates to master constraints.

review_flags: A source formalizing problem-specific inference duals or certificate translations is required.
The examples of application domains are illustrative, not source-certified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits this specialization-family leaf, but the certificate language, verifier, and translation interface are architecture-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Logic-Cut Proof Interface
children.top_down_role: Soundness, scope, and translation of subproblem reasoning into master refinements.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Validity of generalized Benders cuts under preserved inference

children.title: Logic-Cut Validity Principle
children.top_down_role: Validity organization for master refinements supported by reusable subproblem inference.

children.title: Scope-Soundness Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Relationship between the proof system and the region of master space covered by a cut.

children.title: Proof Soundness
children.top_down_role: Reliability requirements for subproblem-derived master refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Soundness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic soundness condition for proofs accepted by the logic-cut interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be the master domain, let \(\mathcal M(y,\theta)\) mean that \((y,\theta)\) is extendable to a feasible solution of the original decomposed model, and let \(V(\pi)=c_\pi\) mean that proof \(\pi\) is accepted with translated master constraint \(c_\pi(y,\theta)\). The proof system is sound exactly when \[(\forall\pi)(\forall y\in Y)(\forall\theta\in\mathbb R)\quad V(\pi)=c_\pi\ \wedge\ \mathcal M(y,\theta)\Longrightarrow c_\pi(y,\theta).\] Consequently, adding any accepted cut cannot remove an original feasible master projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof soundness requires every accepted translated cut to hold for every original feasible solution within the declared master domain.
assumptions_latex: The verifier either rejects \(\pi\) or returns a definite constraint \(c_\pi\).
\(\mathcal M\) uses the semantics of the original decomposed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted cut preserves the projection of the original feasible set onto master variables.

notation.meaning: Extendability to an original feasible solution.
Master constraint certified by proof pi.

review_flags: A formal source for the logic-cut proof interface is required.
standard_field_rationale: soundness is semantic preservation of every feasible model under accepted consequences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind correctly captures semantic proof soundness, and the formula expresses preservation of original feasible master projections. A formal source for this logic-cut verifier interface is still required.

children.title: Master-Domain Scope
children.top_down_role: Regions of master space covered by a retained certificate.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) includes all master integrality restrictions and bounds relevant to certificate validity.
The representation of \(S_\pi\) has unambiguous membership semantics.
\(\mathcal M(y,\theta)\) denotes extendability to a feasible solution of the original decomposed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate asserts \(P_\pi(y,\theta)\) only for feasible master projections with \(y\in S_\pi\).

notation.meaning: Predicate expressing extendability to an original feasible solution.

review_flags: The definition is architecture-specific and needs a source for the intended scope convention.
The original formula checked a general cut only at theta equal to Q(y), which is insufficient without a monotonicity assumption.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The domain over which a logic-cut certificate claims semantic validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the ambient space of master variables, let \(Y\subseteq D\) be the domain enforced by the original master constraints, and let \(\mathcal M(y,\theta)\) mean that \((y,\theta)\in Y\times\mathbb{R}\) is extendable to a feasible solution of the original decomposed model. The master-domain scope of a certificate \(\pi\) is an explicitly represented set \(S_\pi\subseteq Y\) on which its semantic conclusion \(P_\pi(y,\theta)\) is certified: \[(\forall y\in S_\pi)(\forall\theta\in\mathbb{R})\quad \mathcal M(y,\theta)\Longrightarrow P_\pi(y,\theta).\] The certificate makes no assertion for \(y\notin S_\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate's master-domain scope is the explicitly declared subset of admissible master assignments on which its semantic conclusion is certified for original feasible projections.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Domain Scope

children.title: Scope-Soundness Alignment
children.top_down_role: Validity boundaries arising when certificate support is narrower than its asserted coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope-Soundness Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition between a proof’s semantic scope and its encoded master cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an accepted proof \(\pi\) establish a predicate \(P_\pi(y,\theta)\) for every \(y\in S_\pi\subseteq Y\), and let \(c_\pi(y,\theta)\) be its master encoding. Scope-soundness alignment holds when \[(\forall y\in Y)(\forall\theta\in\mathbb R)\quad \mathcal M(y,\theta)\Longrightarrow c_\pi(y,\theta),\] as ensured by the two requirements \[(y\in S_\pi\wedge\mathcal M(y,\theta))\Longrightarrow P_\pi(y,\theta)\Longrightarrow c_\pi(y,\theta)\] and \[(y\notin S_\pi\wedge\mathcal M(y,\theta))\Longrightarrow c_\pi(y,\theta).\] Thus neither an overextended scope nor an incorrectly encoded guard may exclude a feasible master projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alignment requires the encoded cut to implement the certified implication inside its scope and remain harmless outside that scope.
assumptions_latex: \(S_\pi\subseteq Y\) is the exact semantic scope certified by \(\pi\).
\(\mathcal M(y,\theta)\) denotes original-model feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scoped proof and its encoding together imply global validity of \(c_\pi\) over feasible master projections.
review_flags: A source for the intended guarded-cut interface and its scope semantics is required.
standard_field_rationale: conditional validity requires both in-scope correctness and out-of-scope harmlessness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the intended in-scope correctness plus out-of-scope harmlessness criterion is mathematically appropriate. The chained implication should ultimately be separated into explicit implications, but the architecture-specific guarded-cut semantics first require an authoritative source.

children.title: Cut Strengthening Calculus
children.top_down_role: Strengthening and comparison of refinements derived from a tested master state.

children.title: Cut Generalization
children.top_down_role: Broader refinements derived from a tested master state.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Generalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakening a cut’s triggering conditions while retaining a valid inference certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sound certificate proving \(P(y,\theta)\) under the conjunction \(A_S(y)=\bigwedge_{i\in S}\ell_i(y)\), where each \(\ell_i\) is a master literal. Initialize \(T\leftarrow S\). For each candidate \(i\in T\), use the inference verifier to test whether \(A_{T\setminus\{i\}}(y)\Rightarrow P(y,\theta)\) remains valid over the master domain; if accepted, set \(T\leftarrow T\setminus\{i\}\). Stop when no tested literal can be removed and output the guarded cut \[A_T(y)\Longrightarrow P(y,\theta).\] Since \(A_S\Rightarrow A_T\), the output applies to at least as many master assignments as the input cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut generalization removes unnecessary triggering literals, using a sound verifier after each removal, and returns a valid cut with a larger scope.
assumptions_latex: The initial implication \(A_S\Rightarrow P\) has a sound certificate.
Every literal-removal test is decided by a sound inference verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output implication \(A_T\Rightarrow P\) is valid and has scope containing that of \(A_S\Rightarrow P\).

notation.meaning: Conjunction of the input cut’s triggering literals.

review_flags: A source is required for this deletion-based formulation of logic-cut generalization.
The procedure guarantees deletion-minimality only relative to the literals actually tested.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits deletion-based cut generalization, and sound verification preserves validity. No source supports this exact procedure, and 'no tested literal' should be tied explicitly to a complete pass over the current retained set.

children.title: Cut Lifting
children.top_down_role: Enhanced refinements incorporating additional master structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) is valid on \(X\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\).
\(X\cap\{x:x_j=1\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha^*x_j\leq b\) is valid on \(X\), and \(\alpha^*\) is the largest valid coefficient on \(x_j\) with all other coefficients fixed.

notation.meaning: Index of the variable being lifted.
Coefficient vector of the inequality valid on the initial face.

review_flags: The specific section and page locator provisionally match the standard binary single-variable lifting construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-variable lifting of a valid inequality from a binary face to the full discrete set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), an index \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) with \(a_j=0\) that is valid for \(X\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\). If \(X\cap\{x:x_j=1\}\neq\varnothing\), compute \[\alpha^*=b-\max\{a^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ x_j=1\}\] and output \[a^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha^*x_j\leq b.\] The output is valid for every \(x\in X\), and \(\alpha^*\) is the largest coefficient on \(x_j\) that preserves validity while the other coefficients remain fixed. Sequential lifting applies the same construction successively to additional fixed binary variables, using the current lifted inequality and face at each step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-variable lifting computes the largest coefficient for an omitted binary variable that extends an inequality valid on one face to the full feasible set; sequential lifting repeats this operation for further variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Lifting

children.title: Cut Dominance
children.top_down_role: Relative strength among refinements covering comparable master states.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\)
\(H_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_k^\top x\ge b_k\}\) and \(F\subseteq H_k\) for \(k\in\{1,2\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cap H_1\subseteq R\cap H_2\)

notation.meaning: Feasible master assignments and their current relaxation, respectively.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance is relative to the current master relaxation; strict dominance uses proper inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of master assignments and \(R\) a relaxation containing \(F\). For valid cuts \(a_1^\top x\ge b_1\) and \(a_2^\top x\ge b_2\), the first cut dominates the second relative to \(R\) precisely when every point of \(R\) satisfying the first also satisfies the second: \[R\cap\{x:a_1^\top x\ge b_1\}\subseteq R\cap\{x:a_2^\top x\ge b_2\}.\] Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper. Thus replacing the second cut by the first cannot weaken the relaxation over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut dominates another when, within the current relaxation, satisfying the first always implies satisfying the second; dominance is strict when the implication is not reversible.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-set-inclusion definition is mathematically coherent and fits Cut Dominance, but the cited integer-programming-models page does not inspectably support this exact dominance definition. A source specifically treating cut or inequality dominance is required.

children.title: Logic-Cut Scope Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Validity distinctions based on search context and retained master conditions.

children.title: Local Logic Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements restricted to a search node or local master region.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the globally feasible master set
\(D_v\subseteq X\) is the domain imposed at search node \(v\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap D_v\subseteq\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}\)

notation.meaning: Assignments compatible with the restrictions at node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local validity is restricted to a search-node domain and need not survive outside that domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the globally feasible master set and let \(D_v\subseteq X\) contain exactly the assignments compatible with the branching and propagation restrictions active at node \(v\). An inequality \(g(x)\le0\) is a local logic cut at \(v\) if \[F\cap D_v\subseteq\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}.\] It may be installed for node \(v\) and its descendants only while their domains remain subsets of \(D_v\); validity outside \(D_v\) is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local logic cut is valid for feasible assignments satisfying a search node's active restrictions and may be inherited only by descendants whose domains remain inside that node domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Logic Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and fits Local Logic Cuts, including the descendant-domain qualification. The generic constraint-programming locator does not inspectably support node-local validity or inheritance, so a source on local cuts or search-node validity is required.

children.title: Global Logic Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements valid throughout the maintained master domain.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible master set
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global validity is independent of the node or inference context in which the cut was derived.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) denote all master assignments admitting a feasible completion in the original hybrid model. An inequality \(g(x)\le0\) is a global logic cut if \[F\subseteq\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}.\] Its validity depends only on the original model, not on branching restrictions, temporary bounds, or assumptions used by a particular subproblem invocation. Consequently it may be imposed at the root and retained at every search node without an additional guard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global logic cut is satisfied by every feasible master assignment, independently of temporary search restrictions, so it can be enforced throughout the search tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Logic Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement gives a coherent definition of a globally valid logic cut, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not inspectably support the asserted root-to-node reuse semantics. A source addressing global cut validity is required.

children.title: Context-Dependent Logic Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements whose validity depends on retained contextual conditions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the globally feasible master set
\(\Gamma:X\to\{0,1\}\) represents a stated inference context
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap\{x:\Gamma(x)=1\}\subseteq\{x:g(x)\le0\}\)

notation.meaning: Predicate identifying the context under which the inference is sound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The cut is represented as a guarded implication rather than an unguarded global inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the globally feasible master set, and let \(\Gamma:X\to\{0,1\}\) encode the explicit assumptions under which a subproblem inference was obtained. A context-dependent logic cut is the guarded implication \[\Gamma(x)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ g(x)\le0,\] valid when \[F\cap\{x\in X:\Gamma(x)=1\}\subseteq\{x\in X:g(x)\le0\}.\] The consequent \(g(x)\le0\) may fail to be globally valid when detached from its guard, so storage and reuse must preserve \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A context-dependent cut is valid only when an explicit guard describing its derivation assumptions holds; reusing the cut requires preserving that guard.
knowledge_statements.title: Context-Dependent Logic Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded implication matches the intended context-dependent scope and is mathematically coherent. The cited general constraint-programming page does not inspectably support guarded logic cuts or their reuse conditions, so a more specific source is required.

children.title: Subproblem Infeasibility-Proof Interface
children.top_down_role: Certificate families used to translate failed subproblems into master exclusions.

children.title: Assignment-Scope Nogood Family
children.top_down_role: Exclusions associated with complete or reduced master assignments.

children.title: Complete-Assignment Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Exclusions tied to fully specified master candidates.

assumptions_latex: The subproblem induced by \(x=\bar x\) is infeasible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary complete-assignment form; every component of the incumbent assignment is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) be the binary master vector. If the subproblem obtained from the complete assignment \(x=\bar x\) is infeasible, then the complete-assignment nogood is \[\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1.\] Its left-hand side counts components on which \(x\) differs from \(\bar x\). Hence the inequality excludes exactly \(\bar x\) from the binary master space and leaves every other binary assignment admissible unless excluded by another constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When one complete binary assignment yields an infeasible subproblem, its nogood requires every future assignment to differ from it in at least one component.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Assignment Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary nogood formula correctly excludes exactly the complete assignment and the certificate kind is defensible in the infeasibility-proof interface. Neither cited locator inspectably supports this complete-assignment nogood construction; a source on no-good cuts or logic-based Benders infeasibility cuts is required.

children.title: Partial-Assignment Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Exclusions tied to reduced sets of master decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
Every completion satisfying \(x_j=\bar x_j\) for all \(j\in J\) induces infeasibility
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in J:\bar x_j=0}x_j+\sum_{j\in J:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)\ge1\)

notation.meaning: Indices fixed by the infeasible partial assignment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary partial-assignment form; omitted variables may take arbitrary values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), let \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and suppose every completion of the partial assignment \(x_j=\bar x_j\) for \(j\in J\) induces an infeasible subproblem. The partial-assignment nogood is \[\sum_{j\in J:\bar x_j=0}x_j+\sum_{j\in J:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)\ge1.\] It excludes all binary assignments agreeing with \(\bar x\) throughout \(J\), while making no direct restriction on components outside \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If fixing only a subset of binary variables already guarantees infeasibility, the partial nogood forces a future assignment to change at least one of those fixed values.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula correctly excludes every completion agreeing with the infeasible partial assignment. The supplied generic CP and integer-programming-model locators do not inspectably establish the partial-assignment premise or nogood formula, so a specific source is required.

children.title: Nogood Scope Comparison
children.top_down_role: Coverage differences between complete-candidate exclusions and generalized exclusions.

assumptions_latex: \(J\subseteq K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
The partial assignments \(\bar x_J\) and \(\bar x_K\) are consistent and both guarantee infeasibility

notation.meaning: Nogood mismatch count over index set S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison assumes consistent binary assignments on nested scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define the nogood mismatch count \(N_S(x)\) relative to \(\bar x_S\). If \(J\subseteq K\) and the assignments agree on \(J\), then \[\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:N_J(x)\ge1\}\subseteq\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:N_K(x)\ge1\}.\] Thus the valid nogood on the smaller scope \(J\) dominates the one on \(K\): it excludes every completion matching \(\bar x_J\), whereas the larger-scope nogood excludes only assignments matching all values in \(K\). The dominance is strict when \(J\subsetneq K\) and both kinds of completion exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For consistent nested infeasible assignments, the nogood using fewer fixed variables is stronger because it excludes all completions matching that smaller scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Nogood Scope Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated inclusion and dominance direction are correct for consistent nested binary scopes, and property is the appropriate knowledge kind. The cited modeling chapter does not inspectably support this scope-comparison result; a source specifically covering generalized or partial nogoods is required.

children.title: Reduced Infeasibility Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Reduced causes of infeasibility used to broaden master refinement.

children.title: Minimal Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Reduced conflicting decision sets used for broader exclusion.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) indexes a finite family of assignment literals or constraints
The subsystem indexed by \(C\subseteq I\) is infeasible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is minimal exactly when every \(i\in C\) makes \(C\setminus\{i\}\) feasible

notation.meaning: Index set of the conflict subsystem.
Constraint or literal indexed by i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimality is used; it does not mean minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{q_i:i\in I\}\) be a finite family of assignment literals or constraints interpreted together with the permanent subproblem constraints. A set \(C\subseteq I\) is a minimal conflict if the subsystem containing \(q_i\) for all \(i\in C\) is infeasible and, for every \(i\in C\), the subsystem indexed by \(C\setminus\{i\}\) is feasible. Equivalently, no proper subset of \(C\) is itself an infeasible conflict. Minimality is by inclusion and does not assert that \(C\) has minimum cardinality among all conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal conflict is an infeasible set of literals or constraints for which deleting any member restores feasibility; it need not be a smallest-cardinality conflict.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Conflicts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly distinguishes inclusion-minimal conflicts from minimum-cardinality conflicts and fits a definition container. The generic constraint-programming locator does not inspectably support conflict minimality, so a source on conflict analysis or irreducible infeasible subsystems is required.

children.title: Unsatisfiable Cores
children.top_down_role: Inconsistent constraint subsets retained as infeasibility explanations.

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi=\bigwedge_{i\in I}\phi_i\) is a finite conjunction
\(U\subseteq I\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigwedge_{i\in U}\phi_i\) is unsatisfiable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The core certifies infeasibility but is not required to be inclusion-minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=\bigwedge_{i\in I}\phi_i\) be a finite conjunction of subproblem constraints and assumption literals. A subset \(U\subseteq I\) is an unsatisfiable core if \[\bigwedge_{i\in U}\phi_i\] has no satisfying assignment. Checking the core with a sound satisfiability or feasibility procedure certifies infeasibility of \(\Phi\), because the core is a subsystem of \(\Phi\). The definition does not require minimality; an irreducible core additionally satisfies that deleting any one indexed formula makes the remaining conjunction satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsatisfiable core is any infeasible subset of the active formulas. It certifies infeasibility of the full system but need not be minimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiable Cores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly defines a not-necessarily-minimal unsatisfiable core and treats it as an infeasibility certificate. The cited general CP page does not inspectably support unsatisfiable-core terminology or the irreducibility distinction; a specific SAT, SMT, CP, or infeasibility-certificate source is required.

children.title: Core-to-Conflict Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between subproblem cores and master-level conflicts.

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is an unsatisfiable core containing permanent constraints and assumption literals \(\ell_j(x)\) for \(j\in J\)
Every master assignment satisfying all \(\ell_j\) activates the certified core
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigvee_{j\in J}\neg\ell_j(x)\) is valid for every feasible master assignment

notation.meaning: Indices of master-assignment assumptions occurring in the core.
Master literal associated with index j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation applies when core assumptions correspond explicitly to master literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an unsatisfiable core consists of permanent subproblem constraints together with master-assumption literals \(\ell_j(x)\) indexed by \(J\). If every master assignment satisfying \(\bigwedge_{j\in J}\ell_j(x)\) activates that core, then no feasible master assignment can satisfy all those literals. The translated conflict is therefore \[\bigvee_{j\in J}\neg\ell_j(x).\] For binary equality literals \(\ell_j(x)\equiv(x_j=\bar x_j)\), this disjunction is equivalently the partial-assignment nogood \[\sum_{j:\bar x_j=0}x_j+\sum_{j:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)\ge1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating the assignment assumptions contained in an unsatisfiable core yields a valid master conflict, and binary equality assumptions translate directly into a partial nogood.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-to-Conflict Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical translation from activated core assumptions to their negated disjunction is coherent, but the generic CP citation does not inspectably support it. A source on assumption-based cores or conflict extraction is required; that source should also clarify whether this terminal is best classified as a principle or algorithm rather than as the resulting certificate.

children.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Certificate Synthesis
children.top_down_role: Hybrid infeasibility explanations combining CP and mathematical-relaxation information.

children.title: Propagation-Assisted Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility explanations supported by domain inference.

assumptions_latex: A sound propagator derives a contradiction from assumption literals \(A_0\)
Every propagated literal is accompanied by a sound reason implication
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigvee_{\ell\in A_C}\neg\ell\) is valid, where \(A_C\subseteq A_0\) are the assumptions reached by backward reason traversal

notation.meaning: Reason set for propagated literal p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The certificate is a reason graph terminating in a propagation contradiction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sound propagator start from master-assumption literals \(A_0\). For each derived literal \(p\), let \(R(p)\) be a reason set satisfying the valid implication \(\bigwedge_{q\in R(p)}q\Rightarrow p\). If propagation derives contradictory literals \(r\) and \(\neg r\), recursively traverse their reason sets until reaching assumptions \(A_C\subseteq A_0\). The reason implications certify \(\bigwedge_{\ell\in A_C}\ell\Rightarrow\bot\); hence the master conflict \[\bigvee_{\ell\in A_C}\neg\ell\] is valid. Verification consists of checking each reason implication and the final contradictory pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation certificate traces a contradiction backward through sound reason implications to master assumptions; negating those assumptions gives a verifiable conflict cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Assisted Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reason-graph construction is plausible and fits a certificate container, but its soundness depends on the precise semantics under which every reason implication is valid. The cited introductory CP section does not inspectably support reason traversal or certificate verification, so a source on explanation-based propagation or conflict analysis is required.

children.title: Relaxation-Assisted Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility explanations supported by mathematical relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The assignment-dependent relaxation is \(Ay\ge b-Bx\)
\(\lambda\ge0\), \(\lambda^\top A=0\), and \(\lambda^\top(b-B\bar x)>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^\top Bx\ge\lambda^\top b\) is necessary for relaxation feasibility and excludes \(\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-relaxation certificate using a Farkas multiplier for an assignment-dependent right-hand side.

source_refs.locator: 5.4 Duality results and convex relaxation p. 60
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the assignment-dependent linear relaxation \(Ay\ge b-Bx\), with \(y\) unrestricted except through these inequalities. If, at \(x=\bar x\), there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \[\lambda^\top A=0,\qquad \lambda^\top(b-B\bar x)>0,\] then \(\lambda\) is a Farkas infeasibility certificate. Indeed, every assignment whose relaxation is feasible must satisfy the master inequality \[\lambda^\top Bx\ge\lambda^\top b.\] The strict certificate inequality shows that \(\bar x\) violates this cut. Verification requires only the displayed sign, orthogonality, and scalar-product checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Farkas multiplier proving an assignment's linear relaxation infeasible also yields a master inequality necessary for relaxation feasibility and violated by that assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Assisted Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4 Duality results and convex relaxation p. 60
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Explanations combining discrete inference with relaxation information.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite set of master assignments.
For each \(x\in X\), the subordinate constraint problem has feasible set \(Y(x)\).
\(P\subseteq X\) is the master condition covered by the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\in P\), so the master cut \(x\notin P\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Subproblem feasible set at master assignment x.
Master assignments covered by the certificate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain hybrid certificate combining relaxation deductions and constraint-propagation explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid infeasibility certificate for \(P\) is a finite, independently checkable derivation \(\mathcal C\) whose leaves are constraints valid for every \(x\in P\), relaxation-valid inequalities, or sound propagation inferences, and whose terminal conclusion is a contradiction such as \(0\geq 1\). Every inference in \(\mathcal C\) must preserve validity for all completions \(y\in Y(x)\). Consequently, existence of \(\mathcal C\) establishes \(Y(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\in P\), and the logic cut excluding \(P\), written \(x\notin P\), is valid for the master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkable combination of relaxation inequalities and propagation inferences proves every subproblem covered by a master condition infeasible, thereby validating a cut that excludes that condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and mathematical claim fit the terminal container, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not specifically support hybrid infeasibility certificates combining relaxation inequalities, propagation explanations, and a logic-cut proof interface. A source on logic-based Benders or independently checkable hybrid infeasibility proofs is required.

children.title: Subproblem Optimality-Proof Interface
children.top_down_role: Proof and bound families used to refine conditional objective estimates.

children.title: Value-Inference Cut Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Master refinements organized around conditional subproblem values.

children.title: Value-Function Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master refinements organized around conditional subproblem values.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain and \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the subproblem value function.
\(L:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(L(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master inequality \(\theta\geq L(x)\) is valid, and it is exact at any \(\bar x\) satisfying \(L(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Optimal subproblem value at master assignment x.
A lower estimator of the value function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph cuts formed from globally valid lower estimators of the subproblem value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A value-function cut is an inequality \(\theta\geq L(x)\), where \(L\) is a lower estimator of the recourse value function \(Q\): \(L(x)\leq Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Thus every epigraph point satisfying \(\theta\geq Q(x)\) also satisfies the cut. The cut is tight at a sampled assignment \(\bar x\) when \(L(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\). A collection \(\{L_k\}_{k\in K}\) yields the master estimator \(\theta\geq\max_{k\in K}L_k(x)\), which remains a valid lower approximation of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any global lower estimator of the subproblem value yields a valid master epigraph cut; equality at a sampled assignment makes the cut locally exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Cuts

children.title: Inference-Based Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master refinements organized around subproblem inference objects.

assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\) is the optimal subproblem value for each master assignment \(x\in X\).
The inference \(P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\geq\alpha\) is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(P(x)\Rightarrow\theta\geq\alpha\) is valid for every master point satisfying \(\theta\geq Q(x)\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound under the predicate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional optimality cuts obtained from sound lower-bound inferences about a subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inference-based optimality cut is the conditional inequality \(P(x)\Rightarrow\theta\geq\alpha\), derived from a sound subproblem inference \(P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\geq\alpha\). Here \(P\) may encode a conjunction of master literals, domains, or structural conditions rather than an algebraic neighborhood. Because \(Q(x)\geq\alpha\) whenever \(P(x)\) holds, every valid recourse epigraph point obeys the implication. For binary master variables, the implication may be represented by an indicator constraint or by a valid big-\(M\) inequality when a justified finite \(M\) is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound conditional lower bound on the subproblem value becomes a master implication requiring the recourse variable to exceed that bound whenever the condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Inference-Based Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional cut is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but the cited general section on optimality via bounds does not establish the logic-based inference interface, indicator representation, or big-M qualification stated here. A specific logic-based Benders or inference-dual source is required.

children.title: Value-to-Inference Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between conditional value information and inference-supported refinements.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite nonempty set and \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the subproblem value function.
\(A\subset\mathbb R\) is finite, \(\ell\in\mathbb R\) satisfies \(\ell\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\) is the master recourse variable.
For every \(a\in A\), \(P_a\) is a predicate on \(X\) satisfying \(P_a(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\geq a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(L(x)=\max(\{a\in A:P_a(x)\}\cup\{\ell\})\), the family \(\theta\geq\ell\) and \(P_a(x)\Rightarrow\theta\geq a\) for all \(a\in A\) is equivalent to \(\theta\geq L(x)\).

notation.meaning: Lower estimator induced by the inferences.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:finite threshold implications and their pointwise maximum have identical epigraph constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-threshold correspondence between conditional value inferences and a pointwise lower estimator.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:X\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(L(x)=\max(\{a\in A:P_a(x)\}\cup\{\ell\})\). For each \(x\in X\), the constraints \(\theta\geq\ell\) and \(P_a(x)\Rightarrow\theta\geq a\) for every \(a\in A\) hold exactly when \(\theta\geq L(x)\) holds. Conversely, any lower estimator \(L:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L(x)\leq Q(x)\) induces sound threshold predicates \(P_a(x)\equiv[L(x)\geq a]\) for every \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite conditional lower-bound inferences are equivalent to a value cut whose estimator is their pointwise maximum; a valid lower estimator conversely generates sound threshold inferences.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-to-Inference Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Structure-Specific Optimality Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Refinements derived from recognizable scheduling, routing, or combinatorial structure.

children.title: Analytic Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements obtained from recognizable analytic subproblem structure.

assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}\{f(y):g(y,x)\leq0\}\).
A parameter \(\lambda\) defines a tractable analytic lower bound \(L_\lambda(x)\leq Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\theta\geq L_\lambda(x)\) is a valid analytic optimality cut.

notation.meaning: Analytic lower-bound function parameterized by lambda.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts obtained by symbolic evaluation of a dual, relaxation, or valid inequality family.

source_refs.locator: 5.4 Generalized Nonlinear Lagrangian Theory for Singly-Constrained Nonlinear Integer Programming Problems p. 137

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An analytic optimality cut is a master inequality \(\theta\geq L_\lambda(x)\) whose right-hand side is obtained in closed form from a valid analytic lower-bounding construction for the subproblem, such as a dual-feasible multiplier, Lagrangian relaxation, or support inequality. The defining requirement is global validity: \(L_\lambda(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If \(\lambda\) is generated at \(\bar x\) and \(L_\lambda(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\), the cut is exact at \(\bar x\); otherwise it remains valid but may underestimate there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-form lower bound derived from duality, relaxation, or a support inequality yields a valid recourse cut, possibly exact at the generating assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Optimality Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4 Generalized Nonlinear Lagrangian Theory for Singly-Constrained Nonlinear Integer Programming Problems p. 137

children.title: Scheduling-Specific Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements exploiting scheduling structure.

assumptions_latex: \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) selects job \(j\) with processing time \(p_j\geq0\).
Selected jobs are scheduled nonpreemptively on \(m\geq1\) identical parallel machines.
\(Q(x)\) is the minimum makespan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheduling cut \(\theta\geq m^{-1}\sum_j p_jx_j\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Minimum makespan for the selected jobs.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:makespan is at least total selected processing load divided by machine count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Load-based logic cut for identical-machine makespan recourse with master-selected jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any schedule of the selected jobs, the total occupied machine time is \(\sum_j p_jx_j\), while \(m\) machines operating until makespan \(Q(x)\) provide at most \(mQ(x)\) units of processing capacity. Hence \(Q(x)\geq m^{-1}\sum_jp_jx_j\), and the master inequality \(\theta\geq m^{-1}\sum_jp_jx_j\) is a valid scheduling-specific optimality cut. The additional inequality \(\theta\geq p_jx_j\) is valid for every job \(j\), so their maximum may strengthen the load cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical-machine makespan recourse, makespan is at least average selected workload and each selected job length, giving explicit scheduling-specific master cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling-Specific Optimality Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The average-load and longest-job bounds are standard and mathematically correct under the stated identical-machine, nonpreemptive assumptions, but no inspectable citation is supplied. The statement also contains a proof-style capacity argument. A scheduling source with a specific locator is required before deciding whether the resulting cut should remain a property or be classified as a theorem/cut representation.

children.title: Routing-Specific Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements exploiting routing structure.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a connected undirected graph with nonnegative edge costs.
\(S(x)\subseteq V\) contains the depot and all vertices required by master assignment \(x\).
\(Q(x)\) is the minimum cost of a closed walk visiting \(S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The routing cut \(\theta\geq\operatorname{MST}(S(x))\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Vertices required under master assignment x.
Minimum spanning-tree cost on the required vertices in the metric closure.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:deleting an edge from a visiting tour leaves a connected spanning subgraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spanning-tree lower-bound cut for a master-selected required-vertex routing subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every closed walk visiting all vertices in \(S(x)\) contains, after removing cycles and repeated traversal as needed in the metric closure, a connected subgraph spanning \(S(x)\). Its cost is therefore at least \(\operatorname{MST}(S(x))\). Consequently \(Q(x)\geq\operatorname{MST}(S(x))\), and \(\theta\geq\operatorname{MST}(S(x))\) is a valid routing-specific optimality cut. The right-hand side may be imposed through a spanning-tree formulation, separated combinatorially, or replaced by any computable lower estimator dominated by the spanning-tree value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any route visiting the master-selected vertices costs at least a spanning tree on them, so the spanning-tree value supplies a valid routing cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Routing-Specific Optimality Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spanning-tree lower bound is standard for nonnegative routing costs when MST is explicitly taken in the graph metric closure, but no citation is supplied and the statement contains proof text. The relationship between the original graph costs, shortest-path metric closure, and the declared MST value should be sourced explicitly.

children.title: Combinatorial Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Refinements exploiting other discrete application structure.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(\bar x\in X\), and \(Q(\bar x)<+\infty\).
A global lower bound \(\ell\leq Q(x)\) is known for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\theta\geq Q(\bar x)-(Q(\bar x)-\ell)d_H(x,\bar x)\) is valid and exact at \(\bar x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:Hamming distance is zero at the sampled assignment and at least one elsewhere
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary no-good optimality cut using one evaluated recourse value and a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(d_H(x,\bar x)=\sum_{j:\bar x_j=0}x_j+\sum_{j:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)\). The combinatorial optimality cut \(\theta\geq Q(\bar x)-(Q(\bar x)-\ell)d_H(x,\bar x)\) is valid. At \(x=\bar x\), its right-hand side equals \(Q(\bar x)\). At every other binary assignment, \(d_H(x,ar x)\geq1\), so the right-hand side is at most \(\ell\leq Q(x)\). Thus the cut records the evaluated value at \(\bar x\) without requiring an analytic model of nearby subproblem values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary no-good optimality cut enforces the evaluated recourse value at one assignment and falls to a known global lower bound elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Optimality Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary Hamming-distance cut is mathematically valid under the stated global lower bound, but it has no inspectable source. In addition, the statement contains the malformed expression \(d_H(x,ar x)\), which must be \(d_H(x,\bar x)\), and includes proof text. A specific logic-based Benders source is required before revision can be accepted.

children.title: Relaxation-Supported Optimality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Logic cuts supported by mathematical lower bounds on the subproblem.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain, \(\mathcal Y\) is a decision space, and \(f:\mathcal Y\times X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
For every \(x\in X\), the original and relaxed feasible sets satisfy \(Y(x)\subseteq R(x)\subseteq\mathcal Y\).
The functions \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(y,x)\) and \(Q_R(x)=\inf_{y\in R(x)}f(y,x)\) are well defined, \(Q_R\) is master-representable, and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\) is the master recourse variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(Q_R(x)\leq Q(x)\) holds for every \(x\in X\), so \(\theta\geq Q_R(x)\) is a valid relaxation-supported optimality cut.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality cuts obtained from minimization relaxations of the subordinate problem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in X\), a minimization relaxation with \(Y(x)\subseteq R(x)\) satisfies \(Q_R(x)\leq Q(x)\). When \(Q_R\) is master-representable, \(\theta\geq Q_R(x)\) is a valid relaxation-supported optimality cut. More generally, any master-representable function \(L_R:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L_R(x)\leq Q_R(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) yields the valid cut \(\theta\geq L_R(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master-representable lower value obtained from a minimization relaxation gives a valid lower-bound cut on recourse.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Supported Optimality Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.top_down_role: Master-side approximations of unresolved subproblem contributions.

children.title: Master Recourse Estimators
children.top_down_role: Master-side representations of unresolved subproblem contributions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain and \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the recourse value function.
\(E_0:X\to\mathbb R\) is master-representable and satisfies \(E_0(x)\leq Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized master constraint \(\theta\geq E_0(x)\) is a valid outer approximation of the recourse epigraph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initial master-representable lower approximations of the recourse value function.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A master recourse estimator is a function \(E_0\) representable in the master model and satisfying \(E_0(x)\leq Q(x)\) throughout \(X\). The initialization constraint \(\theta\geq E_0(x)\) therefore contains the true recourse epigraph \(\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\theta\geq Q(x)\}\). Constant lower bounds, relaxation values, and maxima of previously known valid cuts are admissible estimators. Subsequent optimality cuts may replace \(E_0\) by \(E_k(x)=\max\{E_0(x),L_1(x),\ldots,L_k(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master recourse estimator is any representable global lower approximation of recourse; imposing it initializes a valid outer approximation of the true epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Master Recourse Estimators

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Initial Recourse Bounds
children.top_down_role: Starting bounds assigned to unresolved recourse terms.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty master domain and \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is bounded below on \(X\).
\(\ell_0\in\mathbb R\), and \(\theta\in\mathbb R\) is the master recourse variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initial master bound \(\theta\geq\ell_0\) is valid exactly when \(\ell_0\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), equivalently when \(\ell_0\leq\inf_{x\in X}Q(x)\).

notation.meaning: Recourse value at master assignment x.
Initial scalar lower bound on all recourse values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar lower-bound initialization for a minimization recourse variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite scalar \(\ell_0\in\mathbb R\) is a valid initial recourse bound exactly when \(\ell_0\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), equivalently when \(\ell_0\leq\inf_{x\in X}Q(x)\). Under this condition, \(\theta\geq\ell_0\) is valid for the true recourse epigraph. Any scalar larger than \(\inf_{x\in X}Q(x)\) is not a valid global initialization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite initial scalar recourse bound is valid exactly when it does not exceed any recourse value on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial Recourse Bounds

children.title: Estimator Initialization Quality
children.top_down_role: Structural effects of initial estimator strength on the master representation.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty master domain and \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\) is the finite recourse value function.
For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), \(E_i:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(E_i(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(E_1(x)\geq E_0(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(E_1\) dominates \(E_0\) and \(\Delta_\infty(E_1)\leq\Delta_\infty(E_0)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:pointwise dominance directly reduces every nonnegative underestimation gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance and worst-case underestimation criteria for valid initial recourse estimators.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid estimator \(E:X\to\mathbb R\), define \(\Delta_\infty(E)=\sup_{x\in X}(Q(x)-E(x))\). If \(E_1(x)\geq E_0(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(E_1\) pointwise dominates \(E_0\), the master region defined by \(\theta\geq E_1(x)\) is contained in the region defined by \(\theta\geq E_0(x)\), and \(\Delta_\infty(E_1)\leq\Delta_\infty(E_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise larger valid initializer defines a tighter master relaxation and has no greater worst-case underestimation gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Initialization Quality

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Subproblem Bound Aggregation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Transfer and combination of bounds from exact, relaxed, or disaggregated subproblems.

children.title: Subproblem Lower-Bound Transfer
children.top_down_role: Movement of certified or relaxed lower bounds into the master.

assumptions_latex: \(D\ne\varnothing\) and the original problem is a minimization problem.
\(L_t(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in D\).
\(\ell_{t+1}(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_t\le \inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\) and \(B_{t+1}\ge B_t\).

notation.meaning: Optimal subproblem value at master state x.
Current pointwise lower estimator of recourse.
Lower bound obtained from the master estimator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise minorization and monotonicity of infima are standard order properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a valid recourse lower bound into a minimization master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original objective be \(\min_{x\in D}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\), where \(Q(x)\) is the optimal value of the subproblem induced by \(x\). If \(L_t:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfies \(L_t(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), then \[B_t:=\inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+L_t(x)\}\le \inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}.\] Hence \(B_t\) is a valid global lower bound. Adding a further valid estimator by \(L_{t+1}(x)=\max\{L_t(x),\ell_{t+1}(x)\}\) preserves validity and gives \(B_{t+1}\ge B_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise lower estimator of subproblem value yields a global master lower bound; taking maxima with additional valid estimators preserves validity and cannot weaken that bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Lower-Bound Transfer

children.title: Disaggregated Bound Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combination of lower bounds from separable subproblem components.

assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(Q(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}Q_k(x)\) on \(D\).
\(L_{k,t}(x)\le Q_k(x)\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=1}^{m}L_{k,t}(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite sums preserve componentwise lower-bound inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive aggregation of independently bounded recourse components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the recourse function decomposes as \(Q(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}Q_k(x)\) on \(D\). For each component \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(L_{k,t}(x)\le Q_k(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Then the disaggregated estimator \[L_t^{\mathrm{agg}}(x):=\sum_{k=1}^{m}L_{k,t}(x)\] satisfies \(L_t^{\mathrm{agg}}(x)\le Q(x)\) throughout \(D\). Consequently, \(\inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+L_t^{\mathrm{agg}}(x)\}\) is a valid lower bound on the original minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When recourse is additive, summing valid componentwise lower estimators gives a valid aggregate estimator and therefore a valid master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated Bound Aggregation

children.title: Heterogeneous Bound Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combination of exact, relaxed, or surrogate subproblem bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(Q(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}w_kQ_k(x)\) on \(D\).
\(w_k\ge0\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(b_{k,t}(x)\le Q_k(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) whenever \(w_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_t(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}w_kb_{k,t}(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in D\).

notation.meaning: Certified bound supplied by solver k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative linear combinations preserve lower-bound inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient validity condition for combining bounds produced by heterogeneous subproblem solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}w_kQ_k(x)\) on \(D\), where \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(w_k\ge0\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Solver \(k\) may return an exact value, a relaxation bound, or a certified dual bound \(b_{k,t}(x)\). If every positively weighted contribution satisfies \(b_{k,t}(x)\le Q_k(x)\) for all \(x\in D\), then the heterogeneous aggregate \[L_t(x):=\sum_{k=1}^{m}w_k b_{k,t}(x)\] satisfies \(L_t(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(D\), irrespective of how the individual certificates were computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds from different solver types may be combined when every positively weighted component is a certified lower bound and all aggregation weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Bound Aggregation

children.title: Primal Bound Coordination Calculus
children.top_down_role: Use of feasible subproblem completions to maintain global primal information.

children.title: Incumbent Completion
children.top_down_role: Construction of complete feasible solutions from master candidates.

assumptions_latex: \(x^t\in D\) is a master state.
The objective is \(c(x)+q(x,y)\).
Feasibility of the returned full pair is checked against the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful completion returns a feasible pair \((x^t,y^t)\) with upper bound \(U^t=c(x^t)+q(x^t,y^t)\); failure returns no upper bound.

notation.meaning: Feasible completion set induced by master state x.
Objective value of the completed feasible solution.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: any feasible solution to a minimization problem supplies an upper bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of a master assignment into a feasible full solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master state \(x^t\in D\), solve the induced completion problem \[Q(x^t):=\inf\{q(x^t,y):y\in Y(x^t)\}.\] If the solver returns \(y^t\in Y(x^t)\) and the full pair \((x^t,y^t)\) satisfies every original constraint, compute \(U^t=c(x^t)+q(x^t,y^t)\) and return the feasible incumbent candidate \((x^t,y^t)\) with value \(U^t\). If \(Y(x^t)=\varnothing\) or feasibility cannot be certified, return failure and no primal bound. Approximate completion may update the incumbent only when the returned pair is independently certified feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the subproblem at a master state. A certified feasible completion supplies an incumbent value; infeasibility or uncertified completion supplies no primal bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Completion

children.title: Upper-Bound Coordination
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of global primal bounds across master and subproblem solves.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
Every accepted \(U_j^t\) is the objective value of a certified feasible full solution.
Each feasibility certificate and objective value identify the same solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline U_t\) is a valid upper bound and \(\overline U_t\le\overline U_{t-1}\).

notation.meaning: Set of workers returning certified candidates at iteration t.
Certified candidate objective from worker j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the minimum of feasible minimization objective values is a valid monotone upper bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone coordination of certified incumbent values from multiple completion attempts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(J_t\) be the set of completion workers returning certified feasible full solutions at iteration \(t\), and let \(U_j^t\) be the objective value reported by worker \(j\in J_t\). Define \[\overline U_t:=\min\bigl(\{\overline U_{t-1}\}\cup\{U_j^t:j\in J_t\}\bigr),\] with \(\overline U_0=+\infty\) if no incumbent is known and \(\min\varnothing:=+\infty\). Then \(\overline U_t\) is a valid global upper bound and \(\overline U_t\le\overline U_{t-1}\). Duplicate, delayed, or dominated candidates do not affect correctness provided their reported objective and feasibility certificate refer to the same full solution and the solution remains feasible for the current problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinated primal bound is the minimum certified feasible objective received so far; it remains valid and decreases monotonically.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Coordination

children.title: Completion Failure Handling
children.top_down_role: Structural treatment of master candidates lacking feasible subproblem completions.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
Completion status distinguishes feasible, certified infeasible, and unknown outcomes.
Cuts are admitted only after validity checking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncertified failure changes neither the upper bound nor the feasible master domain; certified infeasibility may exclude \(x^t\) by a valid feasibility cut.

notation.meaning: Completion set at the attempted master state.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: primal bounds require feasible solutions and state exclusion requires a validity certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates certified completion failure from admissible primal-bound and cut updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the declared master domain. If completion at \(x^t\in D\) returns no certified feasible full solution, its output must not update the primal upper bound. A declaration \(Y(x^t)=\varnothing\) may generate a feasibility cut \(g_t(x)\le0\) only when a certificate establishes both \(g_t(x^t)>0\) and \(g_t(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in D\) admitting a feasible completion. A timeout, numerical error, or unknown solver status establishes neither infeasibility nor a valid objective bound; absent an independent certificate, it permits only deferral, retry, or a conservative solver-status update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failed completion cannot improve the incumbent. Only certified infeasibility may yield a feasibility cut; timeout or unknown status justifies neither exclusion nor a bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion Failure Handling

children.title: Master Information Consistency System
children.top_down_role: Consistency of retained refinements and estimates as the master domain changes.

children.title: Cut-Pool Consistency
children.top_down_role: Validity of retained refinements under evolving master state.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\).
\(Q(x)\) denotes the true optimal completion value.
The master uses \(\eta\) as a recourse epigraph variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All original feasible solutions remain represented, and each retained optimality cut is a valid recourse lower estimator.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid inequalities preserve feasible solutions and pointwise recourse minorants preserve lower bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global validity invariant for cuts retained in a logic-based master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the declared master domain, let \(F:=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) be the set of master states admitting a feasible completion, and let the active cut pool be \(\mathcal C_t\). Cut-pool consistency holds when every feasibility cut \(g(x)\le0\) in \(\mathcal C_t\) satisfies \(g(x)\le0\) for all \(x\in F\), and every optimality cut \(\eta\ge\ell(x)\) in \(\mathcal C_t\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Under this invariant, imposing all active cuts neither removes a feasible original solution nor overestimates its recourse value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent cut pool contains only feasibility cuts valid for every completable state and optimality cuts that never exceed true recourse.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Consistency

children.title: Recourse-Estimator Consistency
children.top_down_role: Alignment of stored recourse estimates with current subproblem information.

assumptions_latex: \(F:=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) is the set of completable master states.
Every \(\ell\in\mathcal L_t\) satisfies \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
The master enforces every active estimator through \(\eta\), and \(\mathcal L_t\subseteq\mathcal L_{t+1}\) for monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q_t(x)\le Q(x)\) and \(\widehat Q_{t+1}(x)\ge\widehat Q_t(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a supremum of pointwise minorants is a minorant, and enlarging its index set is monotone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant linking the master recourse variable to accumulated optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) be the set of completable master states, let \(\mathcal L_t\) be the active family of recourse lower estimators on \(F\), and define \(\widehat Q_t(x):=\sup_{\ell\in\mathcal L_t}\ell(x)\), with the empty supremum equal to \(-\infty\). Recourse-estimator consistency requires \(\ell(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(\ell\in\mathcal L_t\) and every \(x\in F\), and requires the master constraints \(\eta\ge\ell(x)\) for every \(\ell\in\mathcal L_t\), equivalently \(\eta\ge\widehat Q_t(x)\). Consequently, \(\widehat Q_t(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in F\); if \(\mathcal L_t\subseteq\mathcal L_{t+1}\), then \(\widehat Q_{t+1}(x)\ge\widehat Q_t(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master estimator is the supremum of active valid recourse lower bounds. It remains below true recourse and strengthens monotonically as cuts are added.
knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Estimator Consistency

children.title: Master-Domain Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of retained information with domain changes.

assumptions_latex: \(D_0\) is the original declared master domain.
\(F=\{x\in D_0:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\).
\(D_t\) is the set of master states retained at iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq D_t\subseteq D_0\), so no feasible original solution is lost through master-domain restriction.

notation.meaning: Projection of the original feasible set onto master variables.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricting a search domain is exact when the projection of every feasible solution is retained
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant ensuring that master-domain restrictions preserve all completable states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0\) be the declared master domain and let \(F:=\{x\in D_0:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) be the projection of the original feasible set. If \(D_t\) is the active master domain at iteration \(t\), master-domain consistency is the inclusion \(F\subseteq D_t\subseteq D_0\). Thus every domain restriction or feasibility cut added through iteration \(t\) must retain every point of \(F\). Under this condition, no globally feasible original solution is discarded, although \(D_t\) may still contain states with infeasible completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active master domain must contain every master state that admits a feasible completion while remaining inside the declared original master domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Domain Consistency

children.title: Stale-Information Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where retained cuts or estimates lose their intended scope.

assumptions_latex: Iterations \(s<t\) may use different domains or model data.
Stored information carries its generating domain, objective, constraints, and certificate.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unrevalidated stale information must not restrict the master or update global bounds when its generating validity predicate no longer implies current validity.

notation.meaning: Master domain when the information was generated.
Objective function shared by the old and current minimization problems.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificates remain valid only under transformations that preserve their defining implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity limits for reusing cuts and bounds after master information changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Information generated at iteration \(s<t\) may be reused at iteration \(t\) only if its original validity predicate remains true for the current problem. A stale cut is safe only when it is valid on the current feasible projection. A stale upper bound is safe only when it is tied to a solution feasible for the current problem and evaluated under the current objective. If the objective function \(f\) is unchanged, \(D_t\subseteq D_s\), and \(L_s\le\inf_{x\in D_s}f(x)\), then \(L_s\le\inf_{x\in D_t}f(x)\), so the stale lower bound remains valid after domain contraction. Domain expansion, changed objective coefficients, changed constraints, or altered subproblem semantics requires revalidation and may invalidate the corresponding information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Old cuts and bounds remain usable only while their validity conditions survive. An unchanged-objective lower bound survives domain contraction, whereas domain expansion or changed model data requires revalidation.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Information Boundaries

children.top_down_role: Termination mechanisms, complexity regimes, and guarantee boundaries for exact logic-based decomposition.
