children.title: Finite Master-Domain Regime
children.top_down_role: Termination structure associated with finitely many distinguishable master states.

assumptions_latex: Every processed state receives a certified exact completion status and, when feasible, its exact completed objective value.
Each iteration permanently resolves one previously unresolved state, and stopping occurs only after every unresolved state is certified unable to improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination occurs after at most \(|D|\) state-processing iterations with a global optimality or infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Finite set of distinguishable master states.
Master state processed at iteration t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a finite set cannot supply more than its cardinality of distinct permanently resolved states
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination under exact state processing and permanent resolution of unresolved master states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the distinguishable master-state set \(D\) be finite and nonempty. Suppose each state-processing iteration selects a previously unresolved state \(x^t\in D\), solves its completion problem to a certified terminal status, and permanently records either that the state is infeasible or, when it is feasible, its exact completed objective value and a corresponding feasible completion. Suppose further that a resolved state is never processed again and that the algorithm stops only when every unresolved state is certified unable to improve the incumbent. Then the algorithm terminates after at most \(|D|\) state-processing iterations and returns either a globally optimal feasible solution or a certificate that the original problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite master domain, exact processing and permanent resolution of one new state per iteration imply termination within the number of states, provided stopping certifies that no unresolved state can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Master-Domain Regime

children.title: Master-State Progress Certificate
children.top_down_role: Progress mechanisms preventing unresolved repetition of master states.

children.title: Valid-Cut Progress
children.top_down_role: Master refinement through cuts valid for the maintained search domain.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\).
\(x^t\in D\setminus F\) is the current master state.
The master permanently enforces \(g_t(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All \(x\in F\) remain admissible and \(x^t\) is excluded from every subsequent master solution.

notation.meaning: Set of master states with feasible completion.
Progress-cut function generated at iteration t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a valid inequality violated at the current point preserves the feasible set and excludes that point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasibility-cut certificate that preserves completable states while eliminating the current infeasible master state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the declared master domain, let \(F:=\{x\in D:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\) be the set of master states admitting feasible completion, and let \(x^t\in D\setminus F\) be the current master state. A feasibility cut \(g_t(x)\le0\) is a valid-cut progress certificate when \[g_t(x)\le0\quad\text{for every }x\in F,\qquad g_t(x^t)>0.\] The first condition certifies global validity on completable states, while the second certifies strict exclusion of the current infeasible state. After adding the cut, every feasible original solution remains represented and \(x^t\) cannot recur. On a finite master domain, permanently adding one such certificate for each selected unresolved infeasible state yields strict progress on those states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility progress cut is valid for every completable state and violated by the current infeasible state, so it preserves feasibility while preventing that state's recurrence.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Cut Progress

children.title: Master-State Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Removal of resolved or disproven master states from future consideration.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-State Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that a valid refinement removes the evaluated master state from subsequent consideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the current master domain and let \(\bar x\in D\) be evaluated by an exact subproblem. A refinement predicate \(C_{\bar x}:D\to\{0,1\}\) is a master-state exclusion certificate when every globally admissible solution satisfies \(C_{\bar x}(x)=1\), while \(C_{\bar x}(\bar x)=0\). Adding \(C_{\bar x}(x)=1\) to the master is therefore valid and changes its domain to \(D^+=\{x\in D:C_{\bar x}(x)=1\}\), with \(\bar x\notin D^+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid refinement certifies exclusion when all globally admissible solutions satisfy it but the evaluated master state violates it.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) has been evaluated by an exact subproblem.
\(C_{\bar x}\) is valid for every globally admissible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\notin D^+\), and no globally admissible solution is removed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from validity and violation of the added refinement predicate

children.title: Repeated-State Prevention
children.top_down_role: Structural safeguards against unresolved recurrence of equivalent master states.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-State Prevention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonrepetition property induced by retaining an exclusion certificate after every evaluated state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an iterative master procedure produces states \(x^0,x^1,\ldots\) and permanently retains, after evaluating \(x^k\), a valid constraint \(C_k(x)=1\) satisfying \(C_k(x^k)=0\). If every later state \(x^j\), with \(j>k\), is feasible for every retained constraint, then \(C_k(x^j)=1\). Consequently \(x^j\ne x^k\), so all evaluated master states are pairwise distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanently retaining a constraint violated by each evaluated state prevents that state from being selected again.
assumptions_latex: Each evaluated state receives a valid excluding constraint.
All exclusion constraints remain in every later master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(0\le k<j\), \(x^j\ne x^k\).

notation.meaning: master state evaluated at iteration k
constraint excluding the kth evaluated state

children.title: Termination Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Termination route based on certified feasibility, conditional values, and global bounds.

children.title: Exact Subproblem Certification
children.top_down_role: Certified feasibility or conditional value information from exact subproblem reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Subproblem Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–lower-bound certificate for exact evaluation of a fixed-master subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed master state \(x\), let \(Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\). An exact subproblem certificate is either: (i) a feasible \(\hat y\in Y(x)\) and a certified lower bound \(\ell\) with \(\ell=f(x,\hat y)\), which establishes \(Q(x)=f(x,\hat y)\); or (ii) a valid infeasibility certificate establishing \(Y(x)=\varnothing\), hence \(Q(x)=+\infty\). The certificate must be independently checkable under the stated subproblem model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact evaluation is certified by matching feasible and lower-bound values, or by a valid proof that the fixed-master subproblem is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-master subproblem and its feasibility conventions are specified exactly.
The reported lower bound or infeasibility certificate is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate determines the exact value \(Q(x)\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).

notation.meaning: subproblem feasible set at master state x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two stated certificate forms correctly establish exact finite value or infeasibility and the content kind fits, but an authoritative source for exact logic-based Benders subproblem certification is required.

children.title: Lower-Bound Certification
children.top_down_role: Certified global or conditional lower-bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-relaxation certificate of a global lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq D_M\), let \(c:D_M\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and let \(Q:D\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). Define \(v^*=\inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\). If \(q_M:D_M\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) satisfies \(q_M(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\), and the master is solved globally with value \(L=\inf_{x\in D_M}\{c(x)+q_M(x)\}\), then \(L\le v^*\). A lower-bound certificate consists of checkable validity of the domain relaxation and underestimator together with certification of the global master value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally solved relaxed master certifies a lower bound when its domain contains the original domain and its recourse approximation does not exceed true recourse on the original domain.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq D_M\).
\(c:D_M\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \(Q:D\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and \(q_M:D_M\to\overline{\mathbb R}\).
\(q_M(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
The master value \(L\) is certified globally.

notation.meaning: exact recourse-value function on the original domain

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Continuous bound versus Lagrangian bound p. 26

children.title: Upper-Bound Certification
children.top_down_role: Certified primal information from feasible completed solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-solution certificate of a global upper bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v^*=\inf\{c(x)+f(x,y):x\in D,\ y\in Y(x)\}\), let \((\hat x,\hat y)\) satisfy \(\hat x\in D\) and \(\hat y\in Y(\hat x)\). If its objective value is evaluated exactly as \(U=c(\hat x)+f(\hat x,\hat y)\), then the feasibility witness \((\hat x,\hat y)\), together with the objective calculation, certifies the global upper bound \(v^*\le U\). The smallest certified incumbent value remains a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any exactly evaluated feasible master–subproblem solution certifies an upper bound for a minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
\((\hat x,\hat y)\) is feasible for the complete model.
Its objective value \(U\) is evaluated exactly.
review_flags: locator supports incumbent bounds generally; logic-based Benders specialization pending

children.title: Termination Certificate Alignment
children.top_down_role: Compatibility among subproblem status, lower bounds, and primal bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Termination Certificate Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alignment of exact subproblem, lower-bound, and incumbent certificates at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a certified lower bound and \(U\) a certified feasible upper bound for a minimization problem with value \(v^*\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), termination is certified when all subproblem results used to justify the active bounds are exact and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\). Then \(L\le v^*\le U\), and the incumbent has absolute optimality gap at most \(\varepsilon\). When \(\varepsilon=0\), the incumbent is globally optimal and \(L=U=v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible exact subproblem, lower-bound, and feasible-incumbent certificates justify termination once the certified bound gap meets the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le v^*\le U\) is certified.
Subproblem conclusions supporting the active certificates are exact.
\(U-L\le\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-v^*\le\varepsilon\); if \(\varepsilon=0\), then \(L=U=v^*\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bound sandwich directly yields the absolute-gap certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Master-State Enumeration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case dependence on the number of distinguishable master states and cut strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-State Enumeration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case subproblem-call bound from finite-state exclusion and quantified cut strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the initial master domain contain \(M<\infty\) distinguishable states. Suppose every nonterminal exact subproblem call adds a permanently retained valid refinement that excludes the evaluated state. Then at most \(M\) subproblem calls occur. More strongly, if every nonterminal refinement makes at least \(r\ge1\) previously admissible states permanently inadmissible, while preserving an optimal state, then there are at most \(\lceil(M-1)/r\rceil\) nonterminal calls and at most \(\lceil(M-1)/r\rceil+1\) calls including final certification. The \(M\) bound is attained when cuts exclude only their generating states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-state exclusion permits at most one evaluation per state; cuts eliminating at least r states reduce the worst-case call count proportionally.
assumptions_latex: The initial master domain has \(M<\infty\) distinguishable states.
Every nonterminal refinement is valid, permanent, and excludes its evaluated state.
For the strengthened bound, each refinement removes at least \(r\) admissible states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{calls}}\le M\), and under the strength condition \(N_{\mathrm{calls}}\le\lceil(M-1)/r\rceil+1\).

notation.meaning: number of initial distinguishable master states
minimum states removed per nonterminal refinement

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite counting argument under explicit permanent-exclusion assumptions
tightness and cut-strength formulation need specialized source

children.title: Weakened Convergence Guarantee Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes requiring additional analysis or yielding weakened termination guarantees.

children.title: Continuous-Domain Convergence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Termination limitations arising from nonfinite master domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Domain Convergence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-state convergence reasoning on an infinite or continuous master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite convergence does not follow from point exclusion when the master domain is infinite. For example, take \(D=[0,1]\) and let iteration \(k\) evaluate \(x^k=1/(k+1)\). If its refinement excludes only \(x^k\), then every later \(x^j\) remains admissible and differs from all earlier states. Thus nonrepetition holds but the sequence is infinite. Finite termination on continuous domains therefore requires an additional mechanism, such as finitely many relevant equivalence classes, uniform region elimination, or a separate compactness-and-progress argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a continuous domain, excluding one evaluated point per iteration prevents repetition but does not imply finite termination.
assumptions_latex: The master domain may contain infinitely many distinguishable states.
Each refinement is permitted to exclude only its generating state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise exclusion and nonrepetition alone do not imply finite convergence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit infinite nonrepeating sequence is a direct counterexample
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit infinite nonrepeating sequence correctly shows that point exclusion alone does not imply finite termination on a continuous domain, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. No inspectable convergence source is supplied.

children.title: Inexact-Subproblem Convergence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee limitations arising from approximate subproblem resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Subproblem Convergence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of finite convergence when approximate subproblem information neither closes bounds nor enforces progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the singleton master domain \(D=\{0\}\) and a fixed-state subproblem whose exact value \(Q(0)=0\) is attained by a known feasible solution, thereby certifying \(U=0\). Let the master recourse underestimator remain \(q(0)=-1\), so its certified lower bound is \(L=-1\). Suppose that at every iteration an inexact subproblem oracle returns only the same valid lower estimate \(-1\) and produces no refinement that tightens the estimate or excludes state \(0\). The singleton master then selects state \(0\) again, and the certified gap remains \(U-L=1\). Thus, for every tolerance \(0\le\varepsilon<1\), the stopping test is never certified and the procedure can continue indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a singleton master domain, an inexact oracle can stall indefinitely when it repeatedly returns the same loose valid bound and supplies no excluding or tightening refinement.
assumptions_latex: \(D=\{0\}\), and \(Q(0)=0\) is attained by a certified feasible solution.
The master underestimator remains \(q(0)=-1\).
Every inexact call returns only the same valid estimate and no strict master refinement.
\(0\le\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gap remains \(U-L=1>\varepsilon\), so finite convergence is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: exact recourse value at the sole master state

children.title: Heuristic-Refinement Convergence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee limitations arising from refinements lacking complete certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-Refinement Convergence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-convergence boundary for valid but nonseparating heuristic refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{0\}\), and suppose the exact recourse value \(Q(0)=0\) is attained by a known feasible solution, certifying \(U=0\). Let the master minimize a recourse variable \(\theta\) subject to the permanent valid inequality \(\theta\ge-1\). Its lower bound is then \(L=-1\), and its only master state is \(0\). If a heuristic refinement procedure repeatedly returns this same inequality, it neither excludes state \(0\) nor improves the lower bound. Hence the certified gap remains \(U-L=1\), and for every tolerance \(0\le\varepsilon<1\) the state can recur indefinitely without certified termination. Validity alone therefore does not guarantee finite convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid heuristic inequality can be repeatedly returned without separating the sole master state or improving its bound, so validity alone does not ensure finite convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(D=\{0\}\), and \(Q(0)=0\) is attained by a certified feasible solution.
The master minimizes \(\theta\) subject to \(\theta\ge-1\).
The heuristic procedure may repeatedly return the same valid inequality.
\(0\le\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounds remain \(L=-1\) and \(U=0\), so finite convergence is not guaranteed.

children.title: Repeated-Master Logic-Based Benders
children.top_down_role: Iterative organizations with aggregated or disaggregated subproblem refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Master Logic-Based Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative logic-based Benders organization with aggregated or disaggregated refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a master domain \(D\), cost \(c\), subproblem value function \(Q\), initial valid underestimator \(q_0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Initialize \(U=+\infty\) and \(k=0\). Solve \(x^k\in\arg\min_{x\in D}\{c(x)+q_k(x)\}\), obtaining lower bound \(L_k\). Solve the subproblem at \(x^k\); update \(U\) from any complete feasible solution. If \(U-L_k\le\varepsilon\), return the incumbent. Otherwise add valid aggregated or componentwise disaggregated refinements to form \(q_{k+1}\), increment \(k\), and repeat. Exact finite convergence additionally requires a finite progress mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated-master logic-based Benders alternates global master solves, fixed-state subproblem checks, bound updates, and aggregated or disaggregated valid refinements.
assumptions_latex: Each master is solved globally.
Every added refinement is valid for the original problem.
Termination uses certified lower and feasible upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal whenever the stopping test is reached with valid certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the repeated-master leaf and its stopping conclusion is appropriately conditional. An authoritative source is required to validate the stated logic-based Benders workflow and the aggregation/disaggregation variants.

children.title: Embedded Branch-Check Architecture
children.top_down_role: Single-tree master search with embedded subproblem checking and cut enforcement.

children.title: Incumbent-Triggered Branch-Check
children.top_down_role: Subproblem invocation at complete feasible master candidates.

children.title: Complete Master Candidates
children.top_down_role: Master incumbents eligible for embedded subproblem evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Master Candidates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete integer master assignments eligible for incumbent-triggered subproblem checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-check node, let \(X_M^k\) denote the feasible set of the current master formulation over master variables \(x\), including all retained refinements. A complete master candidate is a vector \(\bar x\in X_M^k\) that assigns every master variable, satisfies every required integrality and logical-domain restriction, and has finite master objective value. It is complete only relative to the master: acceptance as a full incumbent additionally requires feasibility of the associated subproblem and completion variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete master candidate assigns all master variables integrally and satisfies the current master, but still requires a subproblem check before becoming a full incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The current master variable set and all domain restrictions are specified.
All retained master constraints are included in \(X_M^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is eligible for an incumbent-triggered subproblem check but is not thereby a complete feasible solution.

notation.meaning: current feasible master set at iteration or node k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes a complete master assignment from a full feasible incumbent and fits the leaf. The cited generic branch-and-bound section does not adequately support branch-and-check-specific terminology without full-text or specialized evidence.

children.title: Incumbent Subproblem Checks
children.top_down_role: Subproblem evaluation initiated from complete feasible master candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Subproblem Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subproblem validation triggered by an integral master incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an integral master incumbent \(\bar y\), solve the conditional subproblem \(Q(\bar y)=\inf\{f(\bar y,x):x\in X(\bar y)\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when \(X(\bar y)=\varnothing\). If \(Q(\bar y)=+\infty\), return an infeasibility explanation and reject \(\bar y\). Otherwise obtain an optimizer \(\bar x\), compute \(z=f(\bar y,\bar x)\), and compare \(z\) with the incumbent bound. Return the feasible completion \((\bar y,\bar x)\), updating the incumbent when \(z\) improves it. Exactness requires the subproblem solver to certify infeasibility or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an integral master candidate, solve its exact conditional subproblem; reject infeasible candidates and use feasible completions to update the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar y\) satisfies all current master constraints and required integrality conditions.
The conditional subproblem is solved with a valid infeasibility or global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\bar y)=+\infty\) certifies rejection; otherwise \((\bar y,\bar x)\) is a feasible completed candidate of value \(Q(\bar y)\).
review_flags: Exact logic-based Benders branch-check locator is unavailable.
standard_field_rationale: exact conditional optimization gives the stated feasibility and completion outcomes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but no cited source supports this embedded branch-check specification. Boundedness or attainment is also needed because a nonempty conditional problem may have value minus infinity or an unattained infimum.

children.title: Incumbent Rejection Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master refinements generated when a candidate fails subproblem validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Rejection Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity criterion for a cut generated from a rejected master incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_F=\{y:\exists x\in X(y)\}\) be the projection of feasible full solutions onto the master space. After a check proves \(X(\bar y)=\varnothing\), an incumbent rejection cut is an inequality \(g(y)\le 0\) satisfying \(g(y)\le0\) for every \(y\in Y_F\) and \(g(\bar y)>0\). Adding this inequality to the master removes \(\bar y\), and possibly other infeasible assignments, without excluding any master assignment admitting a feasible completion. The subproblem explanation must certify both global validity over \(Y_F\) and violation at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejection cut is valid for every completable master assignment but violated by the rejected incumbent, so it removes no feasible full solution.
assumptions_latex: The checked master incumbent \(\bar y\) has no feasible subproblem completion.
The subproblem explanation implies the displayed inequality for every feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_F\subseteq\{y:g(y)\le0\}\) and \(g(\bar y)>0\).

notation.meaning: projection of full feasibility onto master variables

review_flags: A source specific to logic-based Benders rejection cuts is required.
standard_field_rationale: validity plus strict violation is the standard cut certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity-and-violation criterion is mathematically coherent and the certificate role fits the leaf, but the record has no inspectable citation specific to logic-based Benders rejection cuts.

children.title: Incumbent Completion Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Feasible completions contributing primal information.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Completion Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive outcomes of an exact incumbent-triggered conditional solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integral master candidate \(\bar y\), an exact conditional solve has two principal outcomes. If \(X(\bar y)=\varnothing\), then \(\bar y\) admits no full feasible completion and may be rejected using a valid explanation cut. If \(X(\bar y)\ne\varnothing\) and an optimizer \(\bar x\) is returned, then \((\bar y,\bar x)\) is feasible for the undecomposed problem and has objective \(f(\bar y,\bar x)=Q(\bar y)\). For minimization, this value supplies a primal bound and replaces the incumbent exactly when it is smaller than the current incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact check either certifies that the master candidate is uncompletable or returns a full feasible solution and a possible incumbent improvement.
assumptions_latex: The master candidate \(\bar y\) is integral and master-feasible.
The conditional subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X(\bar y)=\varnothing\), or there exists \(\bar x\in X(\bar y)\) with \(f(\bar y,\bar x)=Q(\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: feasible completions of the master candidate

review_flags: A source specific to incumbent completion in embedded logic-based Benders is required.
standard_field_rationale: the alternatives follow from exact conditional optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but no source is cited. The claimed two-outcome exhaustiveness additionally requires attainment and exclusion of an unbounded-below conditional problem.

children.title: Relaxation-Enhanced Branch-Check
children.top_down_role: Earlier subproblem bounds or checks integrated into master node processing.

children.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Subproblem-derived estimates used during master node processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained from relaxations at branch-and-bound nodes for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\), let \(F_v\) be its feasible set and let \(R_v\supseteq F_v\) be a relaxation. Define \(L_v=\inf\{f(z):z\in R_v\}\), with \(L_v=+\infty\) when \(R_v=\varnothing\). Then \(L_v\le\inf\{f(z):z\in F_v\}\). If additional inequalities valid for every point of \(F_v\) are imposed on \(R_v\), the resulting relaxation value cannot decrease and remains a valid node lower bound. An empty relaxation certifies that the node contains no feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over a node relaxation gives a valid lower bound; valid added cuts can only improve that bound in minimization.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The relaxed feasible region satisfies \(F_v\subseteq R_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\le\inf_{z\in F_v}f(z)\), and tightening \(R_v\) by valid inequalities cannot decrease \(L_v\).

notation.meaning: original feasible set remaining at node v
node relaxation containing the original node set

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Relaxation-Based Node Pruning
children.top_down_role: Master node removal supported by relaxation information.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Based Node Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning tests based on node relaxations and a global incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(R_v\) be a relaxation of the feasible region remaining at node \(v\), let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound on every feasible objective value in that node, and let \(U\) be the value of a known feasible incumbent. The node may be pruned when \(R_v=\varnothing\) or when \(L_v\ge U\). In the first case the node contains no feasible solution. In the second case every feasible solution in the node has value at least \(U\), so the node cannot produce a strictly better incumbent. With an absolute improvement tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), pruning at \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon\) certifies absence of an improvement exceeding \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node when its relaxation is infeasible or its valid lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and \(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
The set \(R_v\) is a valid relaxation of the node feasible region, and \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for every feasible solution remaining at the node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v=\varnothing\) or \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon\) implies that no solution in node \(v\) improves \(U\) by more than \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: relaxation of the feasible region at node v
valid lower bound at node v

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Early Subproblem Checks
children.top_down_role: Subproblem evaluation before a complete master incumbent is available.

knowledge_statements.title: Early Subproblem Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional checks performed before a complete integral master assignment is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let \(D_v\) denote the master assignments consistent with its branching decisions. Construct a subproblem relaxation \(S_v\) whose feasible set contains every subproblem completion induced by every \(y\in D_v\). Solve or propagate \(S_v\) before master integrality is complete. If \(S_v\) is infeasible, prune \(v\). Otherwise, use only certified consequences valid for all \(y\in D_v\), such as a node lower bound or a locally valid inequality, and continue branching. A conclusion valid only for one fractional representative must not be used to reject the entire node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check a relaxation covering all completions below a node; prune only on certified infeasibility and retain only consequences valid throughout that node.
assumptions_latex: \(D_v\) contains exactly the master assignments permitted below node \(v\).
The early subproblem relaxation contains every completion induced by \(D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_v=\varnothing\) certifies node infeasibility; otherwise only consequences valid for every \(y\in D_v\) may be retained.

notation.meaning: early subproblem relaxation covering node completions

review_flags: The precise early-check architecture requires a logic-based Benders source.
standard_field_rationale: node pruning is safe only when the checked relaxation covers all node completions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and node-wide validity safeguard are coherent, but the precise early-check architecture has no inspectable logic-based Benders source.

children.title: Local Relaxation Cuts
children.top_down_role: Relaxation-supported refinements restricted to covered search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Relaxation Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and scope of relaxation cuts generated at a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) be the set of full solutions compatible with node \(v\), and let \(a^{\mathsf T}y\le b\) be derived from a node-specific subproblem relaxation. It is a valid local relaxation cut precisely when \(a^{\mathsf T}y\le b\) holds for the master projection of every point in \(F_v\). The cut may then be imposed at \(v\) and its descendants. It may be promoted to a global cut only if validity is established for the projection of every globally feasible solution, independently of the branching restrictions defining \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut must hold for every feasible solution below its node and may become global only after global validity is certified.
assumptions_latex: The node domain and the master projection of its feasible completions are well defined.
The cut derivation supplies a validity certificate over the stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_y(F_v)\subseteq\{y:a^{\mathsf T}y\le b\}\) permits local use; global use requires the analogous inclusion for the global feasible set.

notation.meaning: full feasible solutions compatible with node v

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83

children.title: Multilevel Logic-Based Benders Family
children.top_down_role: Variants with multiple refinement streams or more than one decomposition level.

children.title: Nested Logic-Based Benders
children.top_down_role: Decomposition structures containing subordinate decomposition processes.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Logic-Based Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive decomposition in which a subproblem is itself solved by logic-based Benders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition variables into ordered levels \(y^1,\ldots,y^K\). At level \(k<K\), solve a master over \(y^k\); for each candidate \(\bar y^k\), invoke the level-\(k+1\) logic-based Benders procedure with \(y^1,\ldots,y^k\) fixed. If the nested solve proves infeasibility, add to level \(k\) a valid feasibility cut excluding the certified incompatible assignments. If it returns optimal downstream value \(Q_{k+1}\), add a valid optimality cut bounding that value. Iterate until no violated cut remains. At level \(K\), solve the terminal conditional problem exactly, and propagate its certificate and value upward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each subproblem is recursively decomposed; its feasibility or value certificate generates a cut for the immediately preceding master level.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many levels and each master candidate domain is finite or otherwise finitely convergent.
Every propagated feasibility or optimality cut is valid for its receiving master.
Terminal conditional problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the level-one solution and recursively returned completions solve the full multilevel problem.

notation.meaning: decision variables controlled at level k
optimal downstream value returned to level k

review_flags: A source establishing this exact recursive logic-based Benders formulation and convergence conditions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive algorithm fits the title, but no source supports this exact nested formulation or the stated finite-convergence and global-solution conclusion.

children.title: Multi-Cut Logic-Based Benders
children.top_down_role: Variants retaining multiple refinement streams from subproblem components.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut Logic-Based Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate logic-based Benders cuts for decomposable subproblem components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the conditional value separates as \(Q(y)=\sum_{j=1}^m Q_j(y)\). Introduce master variables \(\theta_j\) representing component values. At a master candidate \(\bar y\), solve every component subproblem. For each feasible component, generate a valid cut \(\theta_j\ge\phi_j(y;\bar y)\) satisfying \(\phi_j(y;\bar y)\le Q_j(y)\); for each infeasible component, generate a valid feasibility cut. Add the component cuts separately rather than aggregating them into one inequality, re-solve the master, and stop when all components are feasible and no component optimality cut is violated. Return the completed solution with objective contribution \(\sum_jQ_j(\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve separable subproblems independently and add one valid feasibility or optimality cut per component at each checked master candidate.
assumptions_latex: The conditional objective and constraints decompose into independent components indexed by \(j\).
Every generated component cut is globally valid for its component value function.
The master and component subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(\theta_j=Q_j(\bar y)\) for all \(j\), and \(\sum_{j=1}^m\theta_j=Q(\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: master surrogate for component j value

review_flags: A source specific to multi-cut logic-based Benders is required.
standard_field_rationale: separability permits componentwise value cuts whose sum bounds the total value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise algorithm fits a multi-cut leaf, but it lacks a citation. The stated stopping test does not by itself establish theta_j=Q_j without a sourced master objective and convergence framework.

children.title: Hierarchical Logic-Based Benders
children.top_down_role: Variants organized across multiple decision or inference levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Logic-Based Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Levelwise coordination with cuts passed through a prescribed decision hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a rooted hierarchy have decision blocks \(y^v\) at nodes \(v\). A parent master proposes decisions for its block and inherited ancestor decisions; each child solves its conditional descendant problem. A child returns either an infeasibility cut valid for all parent assignments represented by the certificate or a lower-bounding function for its descendant value. The parent adds all returned cuts, reoptimizes, and passes revised decisions downward. Leaves solve their conditional problems exactly. Stop when every child accepts the inherited assignment and every returned value bound is tight at the selected parent solution; concatenate the compatible decisions from all hierarchy nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parent masters coordinate descendant subproblems, receiving valid feasibility or value cuts upward until all hierarchical decisions are compatible and bounds are tight.
assumptions_latex: The decision hierarchy is finite and acyclic.
Sibling descendant problems are conditionally independent given their ancestor decisions.
All returned cuts are valid and all leaf problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the concatenated hierarchical decisions are feasible and globally optimal for the represented hierarchical model.

notation.meaning: decision block at hierarchy node v
a node of the rooted decision hierarchy

review_flags: The term has multiple architectural meanings; a source is needed to confirm this rooted-hierarchy version and its convergence assumptions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The term is architecturally ambiguous and no citation identifies this rooted-hierarchy interpretation. The listed assumptions are also insufficient on their own for the asserted global-optimality conclusion.

children.title: Cut-Pool Management Calculus
children.top_down_role: Management of cut dominance, relevance, redundancy, and master growth.

children.title: Cut Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Improvement of refinement coverage or tightness.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance-based replacement of a valid cut by a tighter valid inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be the master domain, and let two valid cuts define retained sets \(H=\{y\in Y:g(y)\le0\}\) and \(H'=\{y\in Y:g'(y)\le0\}\). The cut \(g'(y)\le0\) strengthens \(g(y)\le0\) on \(Y\) when \(H'\subseteq H\); the strengthening is strict when \(H'\subsetneq H\). Replacing the original cut by its strengthening preserves every feasible master projection provided all such projections lie in \(H'\). For minimization, adding the stronger cut to a relaxation cannot decrease its lower bound and may remove relaxation points retained by the weaker cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strengthened cut retains a subset of the points retained by the original while remaining valid for every feasible master projection.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities are considered over the same master domain \(Y\).
The strengthened inequality is valid for every feasible master projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H'\subseteq H\) implies dominance, feasibility preservation, and a nondecreasing minimization relaxation bound.

notation.meaning: sets retained by the original and strengthened cuts

children.title: Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of refinements admitted to the active master.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted selection of valid cuts from a generated candidate pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \(\bar y\), a finite pool \(\mathcal C\) of certified valid cuts, a scoring map \(s:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\), and a budget \(B\), discard cuts not violated beyond tolerance \(\tau\). Order the remaining cuts by nonincreasing score, then scan this order and accept a cut only if it satisfies the prescribed numerical-stability test and is not redundant with already accepted cuts. Stop after accepting \(B\) cuts or exhausting the pool. Add the accepted set to the relaxation; validity is inherited from the candidate certificates and is independent of the ranking score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter for meaningful violation, rank valid cuts, reject unstable or redundant candidates, and add at most the specified budget.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal C\) has an independently verified validity certificate.
The score, violation tolerance, stability test, redundancy test, and budget are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathcal C\), \(|S|\le B\), and every selected cut is valid and violated by \(\bar y\) beyond \(\tau\).
review_flags: Cut-selection rules vary by implementation; a source is needed for this budgeted score-and-filter specification.
standard_field_rationale: selection preserves correctness when validity is certified before heuristic ranking.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally coherent, but Cut Selection is a broad leaf and this particular budgeted score-filter-stability procedure has no citation establishing it as the intended specification.

children.title: Cut Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal of inactive, redundant, or low-value refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of inactive logic-based Benders cuts while preserving master validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master at round \(t\) contain a valid cut pool \(P_t\). For each cut \(c\in P_t\), maintain an age \(a_t(c)\), resetting it to zero whenever \(c\) is active at an accepted master solution and otherwise incrementing it. Given an age threshold \(A\) and protected set \(E_t\), set \(D_t=\{c\in P_t\setminus E_t:a_t(c)>A\}\) and update \(P_{t+1}=P_t\setminus D_t\). The protected set must contain every cut required to certify the current lower bound or incumbent rejection. Deleted cuts may be regenerated when their associated subproblem is solved again.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete sufficiently old inactive cuts, except cuts needed for current certificates; permit later regeneration of deleted cuts.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in \(P_t\) is valid for the original master domain.
The protected set \(E_t\) contains all cuts used by retained certificates.
Deleted cuts can be regenerated or are unnecessary for correctness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced master remains a valid relaxation, although its bound may weaken.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this cut-deletion rule or its certificate-protection boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Cut Deletion leaf, and the validity-versus-bound-weakening distinction is plausible. children.title: Cut-Pool Growth Control

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Growth Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted admission and deletion for a logic-based Benders cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), let \(P_t\) be the retained pool, \(G_t\) newly generated valid cuts, and \(B_t\) a pool-size budget. Assign each candidate \(c\in P_t\cup G_t\) a score \(s_t(c)\) based on violation, efficacy, activity, or diversity. Preserve a mandatory set \(E_t\), then choose \(P_{t+1}\) maximizing \(\sum_{c\in P}s_t(c)\) over subsets \(P\) satisfying \(E_t\subseteq P\subseteq P_t\cup G_t\) and \(|P|\le B_t\). If \(|E_t|>B_t\), enlarge the budget to at least \(|E_t|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admit and retain the highest-scoring cuts under a pool budget while preserving all mandatory certificate cuts.
assumptions_latex: All candidates in \(P_t\cup G_t\) are valid inequalities.
The mandatory set \(E_t\) is identified before budget enforcement.
Scores are finite and comparable within each round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update controls pool cardinality without removing mandatory cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Caching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact memoization of parameterized decomposition subproblems and their certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(y)\) denote the subproblem induced by master assignment \(y\), and let \(k(y)\) be a canonical cache key. On a query \(y\), return a stored record \(R[k(y)]\) only if its validity predicate \(V(R[k(y)],y)\) holds. Otherwise solve \(S(y)\), store its status, objective value, primal solution when available, and a reusable optimality or infeasibility certificate, then return the new record. Exact reuse requires that equal keys determine equivalent feasible regions and objectives, or that \(V\) explicitly verifies the weaker equivalence needed by the returned information.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Re-solving a changed subproblem from a compatible retained solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For successive parameters \(y^{t-1}\) and \(y^t\), retain a solver state \(z^{t-1}\) produced while solving \(S(y^{t-1})\). Construct \(S(y^t)\), discard every component of \(z^{t-1}\) invalidated by changed variables, constraints, objective coefficients, or domains, and initialize the subproblem solver with the remaining compatible state. Run the solver to its ordinary termination test and return only the newly certified status, objective value, and solution for \(S(y^t)\). Retained state may affect computational effort but must not replace feasibility, optimality, or infeasibility verification for the current parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain compatible solver state across related subproblems, invalidate stale components, and certify the new problem normally.
assumptions_latex: The solver exposes reusable state \(z^{t-1}\).
Every retained state component has a checkable compatibility condition.
The current solve applies its normal correctness tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned result is certified for \(S(y^t)\), independently of the prior state.

children.title: Cache Validity Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Cache Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions beyond which cached subproblem results cannot be reused as exact results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached record obtained for \(S(y)\) is not an exact result for \(S(y')\) whenever a change in parameters can alter the relevant feasible set, objective ordering, or certificate semantics and no validation predicate establishes invariance. In particular, equality of objective values alone does not validate reuse of a primal optimizer, and equality of feasibility status alone does not validate reuse of an optimality cut. Across such a boundary, the record may be used only as a heuristic hint; the current subproblem must be solved or its claimed result independently certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cache entry ceases to be exact when relevant feasibility, objective, or certificate semantics may change without validated invariance.
assumptions_latex: The cache record was certified for \(S(y)\), not automatically for \(S(y')\).
The requested reuse concerns status, value, solution, or certificate information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absent validated invariance, exact reuse across the boundary is unsound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock accounting for a nonoverlapping one-pass solver chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If stage \(i\) takes time \(T_i\), transfer and validation after stage \(i\) take time \(C_i\), and no stages overlap, then \(T_{\mathrm{cas}}=\sum_{i=1}^K T_i+\sum_{i=1}^{K-1}C_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonoverlapping sequential cascade takes the sum of all stage runtimes and transfer costs.
assumptions_latex: Stages execute without temporal overlap.
\(T_i\) and \(C_i\) include all work charged to their stage or transfer.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Cascade Runtime Composition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why a sound forward reduction may fail to preserve completeness or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\phi:F'\to F\) maps every reduced feasible solution to an original feasible solution and preserves objective values, then for minimization \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)\le\min_{y\in F'}f'(y)\). Without a reduced representative of at least one original optimum, equality is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction that safely maps solutions back but may discard original optima supports feasible recovery, not optimality preservation.
assumptions_latex: Both problems use minimization.
The solution map preserves objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(F')\subseteq F\ \not\Rightarrow\ \min_{x\in F}f(x)=\min_{y\in F'}f'(y).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition under which preprocessing stages preserve completeness of the final solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sequential cascade transform \(M_0\) through \(M_i=P_i(M_{i-1})\). Suppose every \(P_i\) induces an objective-preserving bijection between feasible solutions of consecutive models, and the final solver is complete for \(M_K\). Then the cascade reports infeasibility exactly when \(M_0\) is infeasible and otherwise returns an optimal solution of \(M_0\) after applying the inverse maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalence-preserving transformations followed by a complete final solver yield a complete cascade for the original problem.
assumptions_latex: Every stage supplies objective-preserving forward and inverse feasible-solution maps.
The final solver terminates with a correct infeasibility or optimality result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}(M_K)=\operatorname{opt}(M_0),\quad M_K\text{ infeasible}\iff M_0\text{ infeasible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Completeness of an Equivalence-Preserving Cascade

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass protocol with stage-specific transfer contracts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a certified result ledger \(H\). For \(i=1,\ldots,K\), translate the current artifact into \(A_i\)'s declared input type, validate every correctness-critical restriction, execute the assigned stage task, translate its output forward, and add only common-model verified incumbents, bounds, or certificates to \(H\). Stop early only when \(H\) contains a valid terminal certificate; otherwise return the strongest certified conclusions after \(A_K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run each typed stage once, validate critical transfers, and retain only original-model certified results.
assumptions_latex: Every stage contract classifies its outputs.
Translations preserve declared decision and objective semantics.
Unverified outputs do not support correctness conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ contains only conclusions valid for the original model}.
knowledge_statements.title: Typed Sequential Cascade

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions for interpreting stage results on the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be the original feasible set and \(F_i\) a stage feasible set with reconstruction map \(\phi_i:F_i\to F_0\). A stage point certifies original feasibility only after \(\phi_i(y)\in F_0\) is verified. A stage lower bound \(L_i\) transfers only when the relaxation and objective mappings imply \(L_i\le\inf_{x\in F_0}f_0(x)\). Stage infeasibility transfers only when every original feasible point has a represented stage counterpart; \(\phi_i(F_i)\subseteq F_0\) alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible points require valid reconstruction, lower bounds require a sound relaxation relation, and stage infeasibility requires representation completeness.
assumptions_latex: Original and stage objective mappings are declared.
Reconstruction and representation relations are checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_0\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow F_i\ne\varnothing\text{ is required to transfer stage infeasibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cascade Certificate Transfer Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defining invocation and ownership structure of a sequential heterogeneous solver chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-order one-pass cascade is a finite ordered list \((A_1,\ldots,A_K)\) in which \(A_i\) runs after \(A_{i-1}\), receives a forward translation of the preceding output, and is invoked at most once. Stages may preprocess, complete, repair, optimize, or validate. Revisiting an earlier stage produces iterative cooperation instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cascade invokes heterogeneous stages once in fixed order and transfers outputs only forward.
assumptions_latex: Stage order is fixed or determined by an acyclic routing rule.
Each stage has defined input and output translations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i<j\Longrightarrow A_i\text{ completes before }A_j\text{ starts},\qquad \#\operatorname{invoke}(A_i)\le1.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Order One-Pass Solver Cascade

assumptions_latex: All stages refer to a common model \(M\) or an explicitly equivalent reformulation.
Each transfer map \(T_i\) preserves the semantics of transmitted information.
Terminal certificates are independently checkable for \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cascade returns only incumbents and bounds valid for the common model.

Starting from state \(x_0\), solver \(A_i\) receives the validated projection \(T_i(x_{i-1})\), performs its assigned preprocessing, completion, repair, optimization, or validation task, and returns state \(x_i\) plus certified information \(C_i\). Information passed forward may restrict later search only when its certificate is valid for \(M\). The cascade stops at the first prescribed terminal certificate or after \(A_K\), returning the best feasible incumbent and strongest valid bound accumulated across stages.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling invariant distinguishing two-solver alternation from generic iterative cooperation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two solvers \(A_0,A_1\), a strict alternating schedule is a round sequence \((i_t)_{t\ge0}\) satisfying \(i_{t+1}=1-i_t\). Each solver is therefore invoked once in every two consecutive rounds. A schedule that may repeat the same solver is iterative cooperation but is not strict alternation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(i_{t+1}=1-i_t\), solver \(A_{i_t}\) executes round \(t\) from committed state \(H_t\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(U_{t+1}\le U_t\) and \(L_{t+1}\ge L_t\) do not imply finite termination: the constant sequences \(U_t=1\) and \(L_t=0\) satisfy both inequalities for every \(t\) while retaining a positive optimality gap indefinitely.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient termination condition for iterative cooperation over a finite certified state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a finite set of certified shared states and suppose every nonterminal cooperation round maps \(H_t\) to \(H_{t+1}\) with \(\rho(H_{t+1})>\rho(H_t)\) for a ranking function \(\rho:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\). Then the process performs at most \(|\mathcal H|-1\) nonterminal transitions before reaching a terminal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative cooperation terminates on a finite state space when every nonterminal round strictly improves a ranking function.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is finite.
Every nonterminal round makes strict ranking progress.
A transition is available from every nonterminal state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy separating control-transfer decisions from validation of transferred information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A handoff trigger policy is a map \(\pi\) from observable cooperation history \(h_t\) to either \(\operatorname{continue}\) or a pair \((j,b)\), where \(j\) is the next solver and \(b\) is its resource budget. Triggers may be periodic, resource-based, event-based, stagnation-based, or adaptive. The trigger determines when and where control moves; it does not certify transferred state.

knowledge_statements.title: Handoff Trigger Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary between scheduling decisions and semantic transfer validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing the trigger rule cannot make an invalid transferred deduction valid. If a receiver uses a set \(D\) to restrict the common feasible set \(F\), soundness requires \(F\subseteq D\), regardless of whether the handoff was periodic, event-driven, or adaptive. If \(F\nsubseteq D\), some feasible point is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No scheduling trigger can compensate for an unsound transferred restriction; semantic validity must be checked independently.
assumptions_latex: The transferred deduction is used as a mandatory restriction rather than a heuristic hint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\nsubseteq D\ \Longrightarrow\ D\text{ is not a sound certified restriction of }F.

Solver Handoff Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility conditions for transferring control and information between solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A handoff from solver \(A_i\) to solver \(A_j\) at state \(H\) is admissible precisely when the policy selects \(j\), allocates finite resources, and supplies a translation \(T_{ij}(H)\) whose accepted components satisfy their target-side validity predicates. A transferred incumbent must map to a feasible solution of the target's common model; a transferred bound must retain its direction and objective scale; and a transferred deduction must be logically implied by the common model. Any component failing its predicate must be discarded or treated solely as an uncertified search hint.

The policy distinguishes certified information from heuristic hints.
