knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Model Retention Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsound reuse after removal of the context that implied a deduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let round \(t\) solve \(M_t:\ x\in\{0,1\},\ x=0\), so \(x=0\) is valid. Let round \(t+1\) solve \(M_{t+1}:\ x\in\{0,1\}\) with objective \(\min(-x)\). Retaining \(x=0\) as a certified restriction discards the true optimum \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deduction valid under a removed round-specific constraint can cut off the next round's optimum.
assumptions_latex: The constraint \(x=0\) is absent from \(M_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_t\models(x=0)\quad\text{but}\quad M_{t+1}\not\models(x=0).
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Local-Deduction Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity checks for common retained-state classes under the next-round model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For next-round feasible set \(F'\) and objective \(f'\), an assignment is a certified incumbent only if \(x\in F'\) and its value equals \(f'(x)\); a lower bound \(L\) is certified only if \(L\le\inf_{x\in F'}f'(x)\); and a cut or deduction with satisfaction set \(D\) is certified only if \(F'\subseteq D\). Local information additionally requires containment in its recorded locality. Bases, activities, caches, and pseudocosts are heuristic unless separately given certificate semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assignments, bounds, deductions, and local information require class-specific validity tests; ordinary solver internals are heuristic warm starts.
assumptions_latex: The next-round model and objective semantics are fixed.
Local information records its validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in F',\ f'(x)=U;\qquad L\le\inf_{x\in F'}f'(x);\qquad F'\subseteq D.
knowledge_statements.title: Retention Tests by State Class

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic partition of information persisted across cooperation rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition retained state as \(H_t=H_t^{\mathrm{cert}}\uplus H_t^{\mathrm{hint}}\). An item belongs to \(H_t^{\mathrm{cert}}\) only when its claim, model identity, scope, and dependencies are valid for the next round; it may then support propagation, pruning, bounds, or termination. An unvalidated item may enter \(H_t^{\mathrm{hint}}\) to guide search, but no correctness conclusion may depend on it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified retained state may support correctness claims; heuristic retained state may only guide search.
assumptions_latex: Each retained item has identifiable semantics and scope.
Correctness-critical operations expose their state dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h\in H_t^{\mathrm{hint}}\Longrightarrow h\text{ cannot alone justify pruning, a bound, infeasibility, or optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified and Heuristic Retained State
Cross-Round State Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-filtered persistence of cooperative-solver state across rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) be the shared state after cooperation round \(t\), and let \(M_{t+1}\) be the model solved next. A state item \(h\in H_t\) may enter \(H_{t+1}\) as certified information only if its validity predicate \(V(h,M_{t+1})\) holds. Globally valid cuts, verified feasible incumbents, and sound global bounds may persist; local branching deductions, solver-specific bases, and propagation states require compatibility checks. Items that fail validation may initialize heuristics but may not justify pruning, bound updates, infeasibility, or optimality claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain certified state across rounds only after checking validity for the next model; stale state may serve only as a heuristic hint.
assumptions_latex: Every retained item has identified semantics and scope.
The next-round model \(M_{t+1}\) is known before certified reuse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified cross-round retention preserves the correctness of pruning and termination claims.

notation.meaning: model used in the next round
validity predicate for item h on model M

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports cross-round state-retention boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits Cross-Round State Retention. The certified-versus-heuristic boundary is plausible, but the persistence classes and claimed preservation of pruning and termination correctness lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Concurrent Cooperation Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Concurrent searches with selective or delayed information exchange.

children.title: Parallel Solver Cooperation
children.top_down_role: Concurrent solver searches with coordinated information sharing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronized concurrent solution of equivalent CP–MIP formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A synchronous parallel cooperation protocol for solvers \(A_1,\ldots,A_K\) consists of concurrent search epochs \(E_0,E_1,\ldots\) separated by barriers. During \(E_t\), each solver searches from the validated state available at the epoch's start; at the barrier, valid outputs are combined into \(H_{t+1}\) before epoch \(E_{t+1}\) begins. Information produced within \(E_t\) therefore cannot affect another solver before the barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous parallel cooperation runs concurrent searches in epochs and exchanges validated information at barriers.
assumptions_latex: All solvers represent equivalent feasibility and objective problems.
Every imported item is valid for its receiving formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_{t+1}\text{ contains only information valid for the common problem.}

notation.meaning: validated barrier state at epoch t

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel Cooperation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and termination conditions for concurrent solver results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common minimization problem with optimum \(z^*\), let \(X_i\) contain solver \(i\)'s verified feasible outputs and let \(L_i\le z^*\) be a certified problem-global lower bound. Then \(U=\min_i\min_{x\in X_i}f(x)\) and \(L=\max_iL_i\) satisfy \(L\le z^*\le U\). If \(L\ge U\), an incumbent attaining \(U\) is globally optimal. Exhaustion of only a solver-local search region does not certify global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified feasible values combine by minimum and global lower bounds by maximum; closing the gap certifies optimality, but local exhaustion does not certify global infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(X_i\) is verified against the common model.
Every \(L_i\) applies to the entire common feasible set.
Objective mappings preserve value and minimization sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le z^*\le U,\qquad L\ge U\Longrightarrow L=U=z^*.

notation.meaning: verified feasible outputs of solver i
certified global lower bound from solver i

knowledge_statements.title: Sound Parallel Result Aggregation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elapsed-time accounting for the locally defined barrier-synchronized variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If epoch \(t\) assigns computation time \(T_{i,t}\) to solver \(i\), followed by nonoverlapping validation and synchronization time \(C_t\), then \(R\) epochs take \(T_{\mathrm{par}}=\sum_{t=0}^{R-1}(\max_iT_{i,t}+C_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each synchronous epoch pays its slowest participating solver time plus validation and barrier overhead.
assumptions_latex: Solvers within an epoch execute concurrently.
Epochs and synchronization phases do not overlap.
All coordination work is included in \(C_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{par}}=\sum_{t=0}^{R-1}\left(\max_iT_{i,t}+C_t\right).

notation.meaning: solver i computation time in epoch t
validation and synchronization time after epoch t

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel Epoch Runtime
Parallel Solver Cooperation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent heterogeneous solvers sharing validated optimization information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_K\) solve equivalent formulations of a minimization model \(M\) concurrently. Each solver publishes timestamped messages containing feasible incumbents, valid global bounds, or globally valid deductions. Before importing a message, a receiver verifies its model version, objective mapping, scope, and certificate; accepted information is merged into shared state \(H\). The shared incumbent value is the minimum accepted feasible value, and the shared lower bound is the maximum accepted valid lower bound. Terminate only when a solver supplies a valid terminal certificate or the global resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run equivalent solvers concurrently and merge only validated messages, using the best feasible incumbent and strongest valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: All participating formulations are equivalent for feasibility and objective value.
Messages identify model version and information scope.
Concurrent state updates are serialized or otherwise atomic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shared incumbent and bound remain valid for \(M\) despite concurrent execution.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this parallel cooperation protocol.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Parallel Solver Cooperation. The atomic message-merging protocol and certificate-validation requirements are specific and unsupported by any supplied source reference or locator.

children.title: Portfolio Solver Cooperation
children.top_down_role: Concurrent or scheduled searches using differentiated solver configurations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent or scheduled searches differentiated by solver or configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver portfolio is a finite family \(\mathcal P=\{S_1,\ldots,S_p\}\) whose members solve the same optimization problem but differ in at least one search-relevant choice, such as paradigm, formulation, parameterization, branching rule, random seed, or resource allocation. Its anytime incumbent at time \(t\) is the best solution verified against the common problem and returned by any member by time \(t\). Portfolio membership does not require shared internal search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio applies differentiated solver configurations to one problem and returns the best commonly verified result obtained by any member.
assumptions_latex: Every reported solution can be validated against the common problem.
Objective values use a common scale and optimization sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_{\mathcal P}(t)=\min_{1\le i\le p}U_i(t)\quad\text{for minimization}.

notation.meaning: best verified value returned by member i by time t

knowledge_statements.title: Diversified Solver Portfolio

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-hitting distribution for concurrently started randomized portfolio members.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_i\) be the time at which concurrently started member \(S_i\) first reaches a common declared target, and let \(T_{\mathcal P}=\min_iT_i\). Then \(\Pr(T_{\mathcal P}>t)=\Pr(\bigcap_i\{T_i>t\})\). If the \(T_i\) are mutually independent, \(\Pr(T_{\mathcal P}>t)=\prod_i\Pr(T_i>t)\); without independence, the product identity need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concurrent portfolio reaches a target when its first member does; under independent runtimes, its survival probability is the product of member survival probabilities.
assumptions_latex: All members use the same target and time origin.
The product formula requires mutual independence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathcal P}=\min_iT_i,\qquad \Pr(T_{\mathcal P}>t)=\prod_i\Pr(T_i>t)\ \text{under independence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Portfolio Completion Law
Portfolio Solver Cooperation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent CP–MIP portfolio with incumbent sharing and independent search states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\), objective \(f\), solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), and time limit \(T\), initialize the shared incumbent value \(U=+\infty\). Run every \(S_i\) concurrently with its own search state. Whenever \(S_i\) finds \(x\in F\) with \(f(x)<U\), atomically replace \(U\) and the incumbent by \(f(x)\) and \(x\), then broadcast the update. Each solver may discard any subproblem whose valid lower bound is at least \(U\). At time \(T\), return the best shared incumbent; if some solver proves its lower bound equals \(U\), return that incumbent with an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run diverse CP and MIP solvers concurrently, sharing improving incumbents; return the best solution, or certify optimality when a valid global bound meets it.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(f\) are identical across all solver models.
Every communicated incumbent is checked for membership in \(F\).
All pruning bounds are valid for the common minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in F\) is returned when found, and \(f(x^*)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) if a valid shared lower bound reaches \(f(x^*)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the portfolio-cooperation leaf, but no source supports the CP–MIP portfolio protocol. The optimality condition must specifically require a valid lower bound for the entire common problem, not an ambiguously solver-local bound.

children.title: Asynchronous Solver Cooperation
children.top_down_role: Information exchange without synchronized search rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Liveness condition when a global completion argument depends on exchanged information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If global termination depends on an inference generated by one solver being used by another, every such essential valid message must eventually be processed or its effect must be subsumed by independently certified information. Local solver completeness alone does not imply cooperative completeness when essential messages may be lost indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every message essential to a global completion proof must eventually be processed or replaced by independently certified information.
assumptions_latex: Some globally required closure depends on communicated inferences.
Local solver procedures are otherwise sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Cooperative completeness requires eventual processing or certified subsumption of essential messages}.
knowledge_statements.title: Eventual-Delivery Condition for Cooperative Completeness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Delay-Insensitive Safety of Globally Valid Monotone Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety invariant for asynchronous CP–MIP exchange independent of arrival order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every communicated set \(M\) contains the unchanged common feasible set \(F\), and solver \(i\) incorporates it by replacing \(Z_i^t\) with \(Z_i^t\cap M\). If \(F\subseteq Z_i^t\), then \(F\subseteq Z_i^t\cap M\), irrespective of message delay, duplication, or reordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally valid cuts and reductions remain safe under delay, duplication, and reordering when incorporated by intersection.
assumptions_latex: Every message is globally valid for the unchanged common model.
Incorporation is monotone intersection.
Translations between solver representations are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq Z_i^t\ \land\ F\subseteq M\ \Longrightarrow\ F\subseteq Z_i^t\cap M.

notation.meaning: solver i's current relaxation or domain region
valid set communicated by a message

knowledge_statements.title: Delay-Insensitive Safety of Globally Valid Monotone Information

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-driven cooperation with scoped validation and duplicate suppression independent for each sender stream.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each message from sender \(s\) has identifier \((s,k)\), declared model and assumption scope \(\sigma\), payload \(\phi\), and a checkable justification. Receiver \(i\) records processed identifiers separately for each sender stream. It validates \(\sigma\), the representation translation, and the justification before monotonically incorporating \(\phi\); duplicate identifiers are ignored, while receipt from one sender never suppresses an unseen message from another. Solvers continue without a global synchronization barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous receivers validate and incorporate messages independently while tracking identifiers per sender stream, so unrelated or reordered messages are not discarded.
assumptions_latex: Message identifiers are unique within each sender stream.
Every accepted payload is valid for its declared model and assumption scope after translation.
Incorporation is monotone and solution-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Delay, duplication, and cross-stream reordering do not invalidate accepted deductions or suppress unrelated messages.}
review_flags: A single receiver-wide scalar version is insufficient unless all messages use a genuinely global total order.
knowledge_statements.title: Per-Stream Asynchronous Cooperation Protocol

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global termination certificate accounting for search ownership, active work, and messages in transit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordinator may declare exact global completion at a consistent global cut only if a verified incumbent is recorded when required, every region in an exhaustive search-space partition is certified infeasible or unable to improve that incumbent, every solver is passive with no unrecorded owned region, and every communication channel is empty or contains only messages whose effects are already certified as subsumed or irrelevant to the declared result. Local solver quiescence or an empty receive queue at one process is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact asynchronous termination requires exhaustive certified region closure at a consistent cut, with no unaccounted work or relevant message in transit.
assumptions_latex: Search-space coverage and region ownership are explicitly recorded.
Every local infeasibility or bound certificate is valid for its declared region and model.
The termination detector establishes a consistent global cut and accounts for active work and channel contents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Certified exhaustive closure at the consistent cut implies valid global completion.}
review_flags: A specialized distributed termination-detection source should be attached when available.
The concrete encoding of the consistent-cut certificate depends on the cooperation architecture.
knowledge_statements.title: Consistent-Cut Certificate for Asynchronous Completion
Asynchronous Solver Cooperation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-driven cooperation without global synchronization barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let solver \(S_i\) maintain local state \(z_i\) and a monotonically increasing message version \(v_i\). Solvers execute independently. On deriving a valid inference \(m=(v,\phi)\), a solver publishes \(m\) without waiting for acknowledgments. Before using a received message, \(S_i\) verifies its model scope and validity, ignores it when \(v\leq v_i\), and otherwise incorporates \(\phi\) monotonically into \(z_i\) and sets \(v_i=v\). Terminate when a designated coordinator receives a valid global certificate, or when the resource limit is reached; return the best verified incumbent and all retained certificate data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solvers proceed independently and incorporate only newer, scope-valid messages; termination requires a valid global certificate or a resource limit.
assumptions_latex: Every published inference \(\phi\) is valid for its declared model scope.
Message versions are totally ordered per communication stream.
Incorporating a valid message never enlarges a solver's certified feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted inference remains valid despite message reordering, while completeness requires an independently valid global termination certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asynchronous-cooperation role is appropriate, but the protocol lacks evidence. Its single state v_i is also inconsistent with versions ordered per communication stream; a supported formulation must define per-stream version tracking or a globally ordered version space.

children.title: Delayed-Information Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity or usefulness limits caused by stale exchanged information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination boundary for concurrent solvers with messages or work in transit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A concurrent cooperative computation is globally quiescent only if every solver is passive, no passive solver can generate further work without receiving a message, and no work-producing message or subproblem remains in transit. A local empty queue, or simultaneous idleness observed without consistent global accounting, is not an exhaustion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global termination requires passive solvers and no work-producing messages or subproblems in transit.
assumptions_latex: Messages may be delayed or reordered.
Receiving a message may reactivate a solver or create work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{local idleness}\centernot\Rightarrow\text{global quiescence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Quiescence Requirement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unsound Reuse of a Branch-Local Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete stale-scope witness for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=Z_0\cup Z_1\). A delayed message certifies lower bound \(10\) only on \(Z_0\), while \(Z_1\) contains a feasible point of value \(5\). With verified incumbent \(U=8\), treating the bound as global would prune \(Z\) because \(10\ge8\), deleting the improving point in \(Z_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forgetting the scope of a branch-local bound can prune another branch containing a better solution.
assumptions_latex: The communicated lower bound is valid only on \(Z_0\).
The receiver incorrectly applies it to \(Z_0\cup Z_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(Z_0)=10\not\Rightarrow L(Z_0\cup Z_1)\ge10.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Reuse of a Branch-Local Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Staleness Does Not Revoke Global Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between delayed usefulness and delayed correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut or reduction valid for the unchanged global feasible set remains valid after arbitrary delay; delay can reduce usefulness without revoking soundness. Information valid only on a node, neighborhood, model version, or conditional region may be used after delay only when the receiver's current region lies within that validity scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delay alone does not invalidate globally valid information, but delayed local information requires a current-scope containment check.
assumptions_latex: The common model is unchanged for the global-validity claim.
Every scoped message records its validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq M\text{ remains true under delay, while scoped use requires }Z_{\mathrm{current}}\subseteq V_M.

notation.meaning: declared validity region of message M

knowledge_statements.title: Staleness Does Not Revoke Global Validity
Delayed-Information Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness and completeness limits caused by stale cooperative information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose solver \(S_i\) at time \(t\) uses a message generated at time \(t-d\), where \(d>0\). A delayed incumbent value may safely strengthen pruning only after its associated solution is verified feasible for the current common model. A delayed lower bound or cut may be used only if its validity region contains the current search region. Otherwise stale information can remove a feasible optimum. Moreover, absence of a message cannot certify exhaustion or infeasibility: termination is sound only when a global certificate accounts for every active or in-transit subproblem and message.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale information is safe only when still valid for the current model; missing messages cannot establish global completion, infeasibility, or optimality.
assumptions_latex: Messages may be delayed, duplicated, or reordered.
Solver states can change between message creation and receipt.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unchecked stale deductions can make pruning unsound, and local idleness alone does not imply global termination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and scope match the leaf, but the claims about stale deductions and accounting for active or in-transit work require authoritative sources on asynchronous correctness and distributed termination.

children.title: Cross-Solver Large-Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood construction or optimization delegated across paradigms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate returned by an exact cooperating neighborhood solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), neighborhood \(N(\bar x)\subseteq F\), and minimization objective \(f\), a feasible point \(x^N\in N(\bar x)\) and a valid lower bound \(L_N\le\min_{x\in N(\bar x)}f(x)\) certify neighborhood optimality when \(f(x^N)=L_N\). If \(f(x^N)\ge f(\bar x)\), they also certify that the delegated neighborhood contains no strict improvement over \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible neighborhood solution is neighborhood-optimal when its value meets a valid lower bound for the entire delegated neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The target solver's restricted feasible set represents exactly \(N(\bar x)\), or its certificate is soundly translated to that set.
The objective mapping preserves values and minimization sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x^N)=\min_{x\in N(\bar x)}f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Delegated-Neighborhood Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference between neighborhood and global conclusions in delegated LNS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate that exhausts or bounds only \(N(\bar x)\) establishes no global optimality claim unless \(N(\bar x)=F\). If \(N(\bar x)\subsetneq F\), there may exist \(y\in F\setminus N(\bar x)\) with \(f(y)<\min_{x\in N(\bar x)}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proving a delegated neighborhood optimal does not prove global optimality unless the neighborhood is the full feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(N(\bar x)\subseteq F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(\bar x)\subsetneq F\ \not\Rightarrow\ \min_{x\in N(\bar x)}f(x)=\min_{x\in F}f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Certificate Scope Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construct-delegate-validate-update protocol for cross-solver LNS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a verified incumbent \(\bar x_t\), the constructor selects a neighborhood \(N_t(\bar x_t)\), translates its restriction to the cooperating solver, and delegates exact or resource-limited search. A returned point \(x'_t\) replaces the incumbent only if it is verified in the common model, belongs to the declared neighborhood, and satisfies \(f(x'_t)<f(\bar x_t)\); otherwise retain \(\bar x_t\). Repeat until the declared resource, iteration, or stagnation rule holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct and delegate a neighborhood, then accept only a verified in-neighborhood strict improvement.
assumptions_latex: The initial incumbent is feasible.
Neighborhood and solution translations are sound.
Objective values use one common minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x_t\in F,\qquad f(\bar x_{t+1})\le f(\bar x_t).
knowledge_statements.title: Delegated Cross-Solver Neighborhood Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Division of neighborhood construction and restricted search between heterogeneous solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cross-solver large-neighborhood-search architecture has a constructor \(C\), a distinct repair or optimization solver \(S\), a verified incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), and a translation \(\tau\). The constructor defines \(N_C(\bar x)\subseteq F\), while \(S\) searches a target restriction whose accepted solutions translate back into \(N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One solver constructs an incumbent neighborhood and another searches a sound translation of it.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is feasible for the common model.
The translation preserves common decisions and objective values.
Every accepted target solution has a validated common-model inverse image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ accepted from }S\Longrightarrow \tau^{-1}(y)\in N_C(\bar x)\subseteq F.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solver LNS Architecture
Cross-Solver Large-Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One solver constructs a neighborhood and another optimizes it exactly or heuristically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent \(\bar{x}\in F\), a neighborhood constructor selects an index set \(R\) of variables to relax and fixes every remaining variable by \(x_j=\bar{x}_j\) for \(j\notin R\). It sends the restricted problem \(\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_j=\bar{x}_j\text{ for }j\notin R\}\) to a cooperating solver. If that solver returns a verified feasible \(x'\) with \(f(x')<f(\bar{x})\), set \(\bar{x}\leftarrow x'\); otherwise retain \(\bar{x}\). Repeat until the stopping rule holds, and return the best verified incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source solver fixes part of an incumbent, delegates the resulting neighborhood, and accepts only verified improving solutions from the cooperating solver.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the common feasible set represented consistently by both solvers.
\(\bar{x}\in F\) is verified before neighborhood construction.
Returned candidates are checked against the common model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent remains feasible and its objective value is nonincreasing across accepted minimization iterations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The neighborhood restriction and incumbent update are mathematically coherent and the algorithm kind fits, but no citation supports this specifically as cross-solver CP–MIP large-neighborhood search.

children.title: Hybrid Inference Exchange Interface
children.top_down_role: Bidirectional translation between domain inference and mathematical-relaxation information.

children.title: Domain-Bound Synchronization Interface
children.top_down_role: Synchronization of finite domains and numerical bounds between solver models.

children.title: Finite-Domain Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of discrete variable-domain restrictions between solver models.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange of sound finite-domain reductions between CP and MIP representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each shared integer variable \(x_j\), let the receiving solver store a finite domain \(D_j\subset\mathbb{Z}\). A sender communicates a reduction \(E_j\subseteq D_j\) together with justification valid for the common feasible set \(F\). After validating the variable map and justification, the receiver updates \(D_j\leftarrow D_j\cap E_j\). If the intersection is empty, it reports infeasibility for the message's validity scope; if it is a singleton, it fixes \(x_j\); otherwise it resumes propagation or search over the reduced domain. No value may be deleted solely because it is absent from an approximate relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver exchanges justified allowed-value sets; the receiver intersects domains, detects emptiness, and propagates singleton fixings without deleting unsupported values.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_j\) is finite and contained in \(\mathbb{Z}\).
The shared-variable mapping is exact.
Every communicated \(E_j\) contains all values attained by feasible solutions in its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(D_j\) by \(D_j\cap E_j\) preserves every feasible solution in the declared scope.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-Independent Aggregation of Sound Domain Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic behavior of finite-domain messages valid for one common scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) and \(E^1,\ldots,E^m\) be finite domains satisfying \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq D\) and \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq E^k\) for every \(k\). Then \(D^*=D\cap\bigcap_{k=1}^mE^k\) contains every feasible value. Intersection is associative, commutative, and idempotent, so message order and duplication do not change \(D^*\). If \(D^*=\varnothing\), then \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound same-scope domain restrictions may be intersected in any order; duplicates have no effect, and an empty result certifies scoped infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq D\).
\(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq E^k\) for every \(k\).
All messages use the same variable map and validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq D^*,\qquad D^*=\varnothing\Rightarrow F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Independent Aggregation of Sound Domain Reductions

children.title: Variable-Bound Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of numerical lower or upper variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Bound Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound synchronization of scalar bounds on shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a shared variable \(x_j\) currently satisfy \(l_j\leq x_j\leq u_j\). When a solver derives valid bounds \(\hat l_j\leq x_j\leq\hat u_j\) for the same search scope, the receiver verifies the variable and scope mappings and updates \(l_j\leftarrow\max\{l_j,\hat l_j\}\) and \(u_j\leftarrow\min\{u_j,\hat u_j\}\). For integer \(x_j\), it additionally sets \(l_j\leftarrow\lceil l_j\rceil\) and \(u_j\leftarrow\lfloor u_j\rfloor\). If \(l_j>u_j\), the declared scope is infeasible; otherwise the tightened interval is propagated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared bounds are reconciled by taking the larger lower bound and smaller upper bound, with integer rounding and empty-interval detection.
assumptions_latex: Communicated bounds are valid for the receiver's current search scope.
Both solvers use the same variable scaling and orientation.
Integrality is declared consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated interval contains every feasible value of \(x_j\) in the declared scope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic aggregation of scalar-bound messages sharing a validity scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq[l,u]\) and every message \(k\) supplies valid bounds \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq[\hat l^k,\hat u^k]\). Define \(l^*=\max\{l,\hat l^1,\ldots,\hat l^m\}\) and \(u^*=\min\{u,\hat u^1,\ldots,\hat u^m\}\). This aggregation is associative, commutative, and idempotent, preserves every feasible value, and satisfies \(l^*>u^*\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid same-scope bounds aggregate by maximum lower bound and minimum upper bound independently of arrival order; an empty interval certifies scoped infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq[l,u]\).
\(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq[\hat l^k,\hat u^k]\) for every \(k\).
All messages use one verified variable scaling, orientation, and scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq[l^*,u^*],\qquad l^*>u^*\Rightarrow F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Independent Aggregation of Valid Bounds

children.title: Domain-Bound Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Alignment of discrete domains with numerical bound representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Bound Reconciliation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconciliation of explicit finite domains with interval bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a shared integer variable \(x_j\), let the CP representation be \(D_j\subset\mathbb{Z}\) and the bound representation be \([l_j,u_j]\). Reconcile them by setting \(D'_j=D_j\cap[\lceil l_j\rceil,\lfloor u_j\rfloor]\), then, when \(D'_j\neq\varnothing\), set \(l'_j=\min D'_j\) and \(u'_j=\max D'_j\). If \(D'_j=\varnothing\), declare the common search scope infeasible. Iterate reconciliation after each accepted reduction until neither the explicit domain nor its interval hull changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the explicit integer domain with exchanged bounds, then return its minimum and maximum as reconciled bounds; an empty intersection certifies scoped infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(D_j\) and \([l_j,u_j]\) describe the same variable and search scope.
All prior reductions are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'_j=D_j\cap[\lceil l_j\rceil,\lfloor u_j\rfloor]\), and \([l'_j,u'_j]\) is its interval hull when \(D'_j\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination of repeated sound reconciliation over initially finite integer domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let shared variables have initial finite domains \(D_j^0\). Suppose every accepted strict reconciliation update deletes at least one currently allowed value, no update reintroduces a deleted value, and reconciliation stops on emptiness or when no domain changes. Then the process terminates after at most \(\sum_j|D_j^0|\) strict updates. If it terminates nonempty, each returned interval is the hull of its final explicit domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone reconciliation over finite domains terminates after at most one strict update per initially allowed value.
assumptions_latex: Every \(D_j^0\) is finite.
Strict updates are monotone value deletions.
No deleted value is reintroduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{strict}}\le\sum_j|D_j^0|.

notation.meaning: initial finite domain of shared variable j

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Monotone Reconciliation Termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits what explicit-domain reconciliation can communicate through scalar bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite nonempty integer domain \(D\), its interval hull \([\min D,\max D]\cap\mathbb Z\) equals \(D\) if and only if \(D\) is integer-convex. If \(D\) has a hole, the hull contains values not in \(D\); therefore transmitting only reconciled lower and upper bounds cannot communicate interior value deletions. For example, \(D=\{0,2\}\) has integer hull \(\{0,1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds preserve a finite integer domain exactly only when it has no holes; otherwise hull feedback loses interior deletions.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb Z\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D=[\min D,\max D]\cap\mathbb Z\iff D\text{ is integer-convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Hull Information Loss

children.title: Exchange Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where model mappings or stale state limit safe synchronization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Witness showing that an unvalidated scaling map can make an exchanged bound delete a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb Z:1\le x\le2\}\), and let the sender represent the shared quantity by \(z=2x\). The sender's bound \(z\ge2\) is valid on \(F\) and translates to \(x\ge1\). If the receiver incorrectly identifies \(z\) with \(x\) and applies \(x\ge2\), it deletes the feasible assignment \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid bound on a scaled variable becomes unsound when applied without converting the scale.
assumptions_latex: \(z=2x\) is the correct sender-to-receiver map.
\(F=\{1,2\}\) is the common feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\nsubseteq\{x:x\ge2\},\qquad F\subseteq\{x:2x\ge2\}.

notation.meaning: Correct scaling between sender and receiver variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Mismatch Unsoundness Witness
Exchange Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which exchanged domains and bounds remain sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_q\) be the feasible set of a declared search scope \(q\). An exchanged domain reduction \(D'_j\subseteq D_j\) is sound exactly when \(\{x_j:x\in F_q\}\subseteq D'_j\); exchanged bounds \([l'_j,u'_j]\) are sound exactly when \(\{x_j:x\in F_q\}\subseteq[l'_j,u'_j]\). These predicates can fail when the sender and receiver use different variable maps, scaling, integrality declarations, model versions, or search scopes. An unverified reduction crossing any such boundary must not be used for pruning or infeasibility certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exchanged restriction is safe only if it contains every feasible value in the same scope; mapping, scaling, version, or scope mismatches break consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(F_q\) denotes the common feasible set restricted to scope \(q\).
The receiver can identify the message's model version and scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any reduction failing the containment predicate is unsound and may delete a feasible solution.

notation.meaning: Feasible set in search scope q.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment predicates correctly express scoped soundness and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no evidence supports the asserted interface failure modes or their use as certification boundaries.

children.title: Logic-to-Linear Cut Translation
children.top_down_role: Conversion of logical consequences into relaxation-compatible refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-to-Linear Cut Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of a valid logical consequence into a linear relaxation cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let binary variables \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\) encode literals by \(\ell_i=y_i\) for a positive literal and \(\ell_i=1-y_i\) for a negated literal. The clause \(\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_n\) is satisfied by a binary assignment exactly when \(\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i\geq1\). If the clause is a logical consequence of the common constraint model, this inequality is valid for every encoded feasible integer solution and may be added to a linear relaxation. Its provenance and encoding map form the validation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid disjunction of encoded Boolean literals becomes a linear inequality requiring at least one literal to hold, thereby cutting off incompatible relaxation points.
assumptions_latex: Each \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\) has a fixed literal encoding.
The clause is valid for every feasible solution of the common model.
The linear model uses the same encoding map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_n\iff\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i\geq1\) on binary assignments, and the inequality is valid for all encoded feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer Exactness Does Not Imply Relaxation Ideality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact binary translation and continuous-relaxation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The clauses \((
eg y_1\lor
eg y_2)\), \((
eg y_1\lor
eg y_3)\), and \((
eg y_2\lor
eg y_3)\) translate to \(y_i+y_j\le1\) for every pair. After relaxing \(y\in[0,1]^3\), the point \((1/2,1/2,1/2)\) satisfies all three inequalities. Every satisfying binary assignment, however, obeys \(y_1+y_2+y_3\le1\). Thus exact clause translation on binary assignments need not describe their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause cuts can be exact for binary truth assignments yet admit fractional points outside the convex hull of satisfying assignments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct linear representation of weighted logical threshold consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For encoded literal truth values \(\ell_i\in\{0,1\}\), a cardinality consequence \(\sum_i\ell_i\ge k\) or \(\sum_i\ell_i\le k\) is already an exact linear inequality on binary assignments. More generally, a valid pseudo-Boolean consequence \(\sum_iw_i\ell_i\ge\beta\), with fixed rational weights, is a valid linear cut after substituting \(\ell_i=y_i\) for positive literals and \(\ell_i=1-y_i\) for negated literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cardinality and weighted pseudo-Boolean consequences become linear cuts by replacing each literal with its binary truth expression.
assumptions_latex: Every literal has a fixed faithful binary encoding.
The threshold consequence is valid in the declared model and scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_iw_i\ell_i\ge\beta\text{ is valid for every encoded feasible integer solution.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed implication form is a direct instance of the seed's clause translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary literal truth values \(a_1,\ldots,a_m,b\), the implication \((a_1\land\cdots\land a_m)\Rightarrow b\) is the clause \(\neg a_1\lor\cdots\lor\neg a_m\lor b\), whose seed translation simplifies to \(\sum_{i=1}^ma_i-b\le m-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed implication inequality is merely the existing clause translation after rewriting the implication as a clause.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i,b\in\{0,1\}\) are faithful literal encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a_1\land\cdots\land a_m)\Rightarrow b\iff\sum_{i=1}^ma_i-b\le m-1.

children.title: Relaxation Feedback Interface
children.top_down_role: Use of relaxation solutions and bounds in propagation and CP search control.

children.title: Relaxation-to-Domain Feedback
children.top_down_role: Use of relaxation information to restrict finite domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-to-Domain Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain tightening derived from valid relaxation bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a relaxation containing the current feasible set and let \(x_j\) be an integer variable with domain \(D_j\). Compute \(L_j=\min\{x_j:x\in P\}\) and \(U_j=\max\{x_j:x\in P\}\), whenever these optima are finite and certified. Update \(D_j\leftarrow D_j\cap[\lceil L_j\rceil,\lfloor U_j\rfloor]\). If the resulting domain is empty, declare the current scope infeasible; otherwise propagate the reduction. Relaxation solutions themselves do not justify deleting interior domain values unless an additional valid cut excludes them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified relaxation extrema tighten an integer domain by rounded bounds; fractional solutions alone cannot remove interior values.
assumptions_latex: The current feasible set is contained in \(P\).
The extrema are valid certified bounds for the current scope.
\(x_j\) is integer-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible value of \(x_j\) remains in \(D_j\cap[\lceil L_j\rceil,\lfloor U_j\rfloor]\).

notation.meaning: Finite domain of the integer variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of an interior finite-domain value by a certified conditioned relaxation test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the current feasible set, let \(x_j\) have finite integer domain \(D_j\), and for each tested \(v\in D_j\) let \(P_v\) satisfy \(F\cap\{x:x_j=v\}\subseteq P_v\). If infeasibility of \(P_v\) is certified, then \(v\) may be deleted. Thus \(D'_j=\{v\in D_j:P_v\text{ is not certified infeasible}\}\) contains every feasible value of \(x_j\); if \(D'_j=\varnothing\), the current scope is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior value may be removed when an outer relaxation conditioned on that value is certified infeasible; an unconditioned fractional solution alone cannot justify deletion.
assumptions_latex: \(x_j\) is integer-valued with finite domain \(D_j\).
\(F\cap\{x:x_j=v\}\subseteq P_v\) for every tested value \(v\).
Every reported infeasibility result is certified for the current scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x_j:x\in F\}\subseteq D'_j\), and \(D'_j=\varnothing\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Wise Relaxation Filtering

children.title: Relaxation-to-Propagation Feedback
children.top_down_role: Use of relaxation information to support further inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-to-Propagation Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid relaxation deductions activate or strengthen constraint propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_q\subseteq P_q\) be the feasible set and relaxation for search scope \(q\). Any relaxation-derived inequality \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) valid on \(P_q\), or any certified bound implied by it, is also valid on \(F_q\). After translating the inequality through an exact variable map, a propagation engine may add it as a redundant constraint and compute domain reductions. Such reductions are sound only if the propagator's inference rule is sound and the inequality remains valid throughout the receiving scope; a local relaxation inequality cannot be promoted to a wider scope without separate validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-valid inequality may drive propagation because it is valid for the enclosed feasible set, but only within its certified scope and encoding.
assumptions_latex: \(F_q\subseteq P_q\).
\(a^Tx\leq\beta\) is valid for \(P_q\).
Translation and propagation rules are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every domain reduction inferred from the translated inequality preserves all points in \(F_q\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of a nogood from certified infeasibility under a finite conjunction of decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_q\) be the feasible set in scope \(q\), let \(A=\bigwedge_{k=1}^m\ell_k\) be a conjunction of decision literals, and let \(P_{q,A}\) satisfy \(F_q\cap A\subseteq P_{q,A}\). If \(P_{q,A}=\varnothing\) is certified, then \(F_q\cap A=\varnothing\), so the nogood \(\neg A=\bigvee_{k=1}^m\neg\ell_k\) is valid in every receiving scope contained in the certificate's validity region and may be propagated there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified infeasibility of an outer relaxation under a conjunction of decisions yields a scoped nogood forbidding that conjunction.
assumptions_latex: \(F_q\cap A\subseteq P_{q,A}\).
Infeasibility of \(P_{q,A}\) is certified.
The receiving scope is contained in the certificate's validity region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_q\models\neg A\).

children.title: Relaxation-to-Search Feedback
children.top_down_role: Use of relaxation solutions or bounds in CP search control.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-to-Search Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation values and bounds guide branching without compromising correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node with relaxation \(P_q\), solve \(\min\{f(x):x\in P_q\}\) to obtain a valid lower bound \(L_q\) and, when attained, a relaxation solution \(x^R\). For minimization, prune the node if \(L_q\geq U\), where \(U\) is the verified incumbent value. Otherwise use \(x^R\), reduced costs, or relaxation violations only to rank branching variables, values, or neighborhoods. Create children whose feasible regions cover the parent feasible region, and continue until a valid stopping certificate or resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation bounds may prune nodes, while fractional values and related signals may guide branching only when the children still cover the parent region.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region at node \(q\) is contained in \(P_q\).
\(L_q\) is a valid lower bound and \(U\) comes from a verified incumbent.
Branching children cover the parent feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound pruning and guidance preserve every potentially improving feasible solution, and pruning is valid whenever \(L_q\geq U\).

children.title: Feedback Locality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search-context limits on relaxation-derived feedback.

knowledge_statements.title: Feedback Locality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for relaxation-derived feedback under branch-local assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the global feasible set and let node \(u\) impose local assumptions \(A_u\), giving \(F_u=F\cap A_u\). Feedback represented by a predicate \(q(x)\) may be installed globally only if \(q(x)\) holds for every \(x\in F\). If it is known only that \(q(x)\) holds for every \(x\in F_u\), then it is valid only at \(u\) and its descendants whose assumptions imply \(A_u\). Installing such feedback outside that subtree can remove a globally feasible solution and is therefore unsound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feedback derived using node-specific assumptions must remain in the corresponding subtree unless independently shown valid for every globally feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F_u=F\cap A_u\).
The exchanged predicate is used to exclude assignments violating \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local validity on \(F_u\) does not imply global validity on \(F\).

notation.meaning: assumptions active at search node u

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity follows from set inclusion and branch-local inference semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf and the set-inclusion claim is mathematically coherent, but no citation supports the intended CP-MIP feedback semantics or the asserted operational consequence. An inspectable hybrid-solver source is required.

children.title: Exchange Locality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Placement and validity scope of exchanged deductions and cuts.

children.title: Root-Level Exchange
children.top_down_role: Information exchanged during root processing.

assumptions_latex: \(F_r=F\cap A_r\).
The receiving solver preserves the meaning of \(I_r\) under translation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Root-level exchange identifies when and where \(I_r\) is communicated; reuse at a region with feasible set \(F_S\) is sound exactly when \(F_S\subseteq\{x\in X:I_r(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: common feasible set in the shared variable space
region satisfying the assumptions active at the root
inference exchanged while processing the root

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exchange time and semantic validity scope are distinct
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange communicated while the cooperating solvers process the root node; its reuse scope is determined separately by semantic validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the shared assignment space, let \(F\subseteq X\) be the common feasible set, and let the root node \(r\) have active region \(A_r\subseteq X\), so \(F_r=F\cap A_r\). A root-level exchange communicates an inference \(I_r:X\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) while the cooperating solvers process \(r\). If \(I_r(x)\) holds for every \(x\in F_r\), it is sound during that root processing. At another search region \(S\), including a descendant or a restarted search, reuse is sound only if every point in its feasible set \(F_S\) satisfies \(I_r\). Thus derivation at the root does not by itself make the inference either root-only or globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root-level exchange is communicated during root processing, but its later reuse depends on whether the inference remains valid over the later search region.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Level Exchange

children.title: Global Exchange
children.top_down_role: Information valid across the maintained search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inference exchange valid throughout the complete hybrid search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) denote the feasible set of the common model. An exchanged predicate \(g(x)\) is global if \(g(x)\) holds for every \(x\in F\) independently of the current search node, incumbent, propagation state, or temporary bound. A receiving solver may retain and enforce such a predicate at every node, provided its translation preserves the predicate's meaning. If the derivation uses any local assumption not valid on all of \(F\), the exchange is not global.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global exchange transmits an inference valid for every common feasible solution and therefore reusable throughout the search under semantics-preserving translation.
assumptions_latex: Both solvers represent the same feasible set \(F\) on shared variables.
Translation between solver representations preserves satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate may be enforced globally exactly when \(F\subseteq\{x:g(x)\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global validity is characterized by implication from the common feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the condition \(F\subseteq\{x:g(x)\}\) correctly expresses global validity under semantics-preserving translation. No cited source establishes this terminology or its use in the specified hybrid interface.

children.title: Node-Local Exchange
children.top_down_role: Information restricted to a search node or descendant region.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange whose validity depends on assumptions at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(u\), let \(A_u\) be its active branching decisions and local domain restrictions, and let \(F_u=F\cap A_u\). An exchanged predicate \(h_u(x)\) is node-local when \(h_u(x)\) holds for every \(x\in F_u\), but global validity on \(F\) has not been established. It may be enforced at \(u\) and at a descendant \(v\) only when \(A_v\) implies \(A_u\); it must be discarded or revalidated outside that scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local inference is valid at its derivation node and descendants retaining all supporting assumptions, but nowhere else without revalidation.
assumptions_latex: \(F_u=F\cap A_u\).
\(h_u\) is valid for every point in \(F_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At descendant \(v\), reuse is sound if \(A_v\Rightarrow A_u\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: descendant validity follows from preservation of supporting assumptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and descendant-scope condition are coherent when node assumptions are interpreted as predicates or feasible regions. The record nevertheless lacks an inspectable source for node-local exchange semantics in a CP-MIP architecture.

children.title: Scope Promotion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions limiting promotion of local information to broader validity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness showing that validity below one branch does not imply root validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the global feasible set be \(F=\{0,1\}\) for a binary variable \(x\). At node \(u\), let \(A_u=\{x=0\}\), so \(I(x)\equiv(x=0)\) is valid on \(F_u=F\cap A_u=\{0\}\). Promoting \(I\) to the root is unsound because the globally feasible assignment \(x=1\) violates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inference that repeats a branch assumption is valid below that branch but cannot be promoted to the root.
assumptions_latex: \(A_u\) is the branch predicate \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_u\subseteq\{x:I(x)\},\qquad F\nsubseteq\{x:I(x)\}.

notation.meaning: Locally valid inference proposed for promotion.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Dependent Inference Cannot Be Promoted
Scope Promotion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient semantic test for promoting local inference scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be an inference derived under assumptions \(A_u\), and let \(S\) be a proposed larger search region with feasible set \(F_S\). Promotion of \(I\) from node-local scope to \(S\) is sound exactly when every point feasible in \(S\) satisfies \(I\), namely \(F_S\subseteq\{x:I(x)\}\). It is sufficient to provide a derivation of \(I\) using only constraints valid throughout \(S\). Merely observing \(I\) at node \(u\), or dropping assumptions from its derivation without revalidation, does not justify promotion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local inference may be promoted precisely when it is valid for every feasible point in the proposed larger scope.
assumptions_latex: The receiving solver interprets \(I\) identically throughout \(S\).
\(F_S\) includes all model and search restrictions valid throughout \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scope promotion is sound if and only if \(F_S\subseteq\{x:I(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set within the proposed scope

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: promotion is sound exactly when the inference is valid over the enlarged feasible region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the boundary leaf, and the displayed inclusion is the correct semantic validity test. The necessary-and-sufficient promotion claim is nontrivial in this interface context and has no cited source.

children.title: Primal-Bound Transfer Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of primal candidates, partial decisions, and objective bounds.

children.title: Incumbent Recovery Methods
children.top_down_role: Cross-solver validation and improvement of complete candidate solutions.

children.title: Incumbent Transfer
children.top_down_role: Movement of complete candidate solutions between solver models.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct transfer of a complete feasible solution between cooperating solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a complete source assignment \(\bar x\) and a shared-variable map \(T\), form the receiving assignment \(y=T(\bar x)\). Convert values according to the declared variable domains, reject the transfer if a required variable is unmapped or a converted value violates its domain, and validate \(y\) against every receiving-side constraint. If validation succeeds and \(f(y)\) improves the current incumbent value under the receiving solver's objective convention, install \(y\) as the new incumbent; otherwise retain the existing incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a complete feasible solution into the receiving model, validate it fully, and accept it only when it improves the incumbent objective.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) specifies the correspondence and value conversion for all required variables.
Both solvers use compatible objective sense and scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either the validated improving assignment \(y\) or the unchanged incumbent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incumbent acceptance requires complete feasibility and objective improvement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits direct incumbent transfer, and the mapping, receiving-side validation, and objective comparison are internally consistent. The prescribed cross-solver protocol is implementation-sensitive and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Incumbent Completion
children.top_down_role: Extension of transferred candidates to satisfy the receiving model.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of a transferred partial assignment into a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the receiving model have feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), and let a transferred partial assignment fix \(x_i=a_i\) for \(i\in J\). Solve the completion subproblem \(\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_i=a_i\text{ for all }i\in J\}\), or its maximization analogue, subject to a prescribed resource limit. If a feasible solution \(x^c\) is found, validate it in the full receiving model and install it only if it improves the incumbent; if the subproblem is infeasible or no validated solution is found, report completion failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete transferred fixings by solving the residual receiving model, then accept only a fully validated improving solution.
assumptions_latex: The transferred values belong to the receiving domains.
The completion subproblem retains every receiving-side constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a validated improving completion \(x^c\) or a failure status.

notation.meaning: indices fixed by the partial assignment

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completion is a residual optimization problem under transferred fixings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits incumbent completion, and the residual optimization formulation distinguishes a completed feasible solution from the transferred partial assignment. No source supports this particular completion and acceptance protocol in the target hybrid architecture.

children.title: Incumbent Repair
children.top_down_role: Modification of transferred candidates that fail receiving-model validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of feasibility by minimally modifying an infeasible transferred candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a receiving feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), a transferred candidate \(\bar x\in X\), and a nonnegative deviation measure \(d\), solve \(\min\{d(x,\bar x):x\in F\}\), optionally breaking ties by the original objective. Under a resource limit, return a feasible minimizer or best feasible point found. Validate the returned point against the complete receiving model and accept it as an incumbent only when it satisfies the receiving objective-improvement rule; return failure if no feasible repaired point is found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair an infeasible transferred candidate by minimizing deviation over the receiving feasible set, followed by full validation and incumbent comparison.
assumptions_latex: \(d(x,\bar x)\geq 0\) is defined for every \(x\in X\).
The repair model contains all receiving-side feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted repair lies in \(F\) and satisfies the incumbent acceptance rule.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility repair is naturally formulated as minimum deviation over the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits incumbent repair and the minimum-deviation formulation is coherent. The choice of repair formulation, resource-limited return behavior, and incumbent protocol require an inspectable source.

children.title: Cross-Solver Candidate Validation
children.top_down_role: Assessment of candidate compatibility across solver representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solver Candidate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiving-side certificate for accepting a candidate generated by another solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a receiving model with domains \(D_i\), constraints \(c_j(x)\), objective \(f\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_j\), a transferred complete assignment \(\bar x\) is validated when each \(\bar x_i\in D_i\), every constraint residual satisfies the receiving solver's test \(c_j(\bar x)\leq\varepsilon_j\) after canonical translation, and the recomputed objective equals the transferred objective within the declared objective tolerance. The validation record consisting of the mapped values, residuals, and recomputed objective certifies acceptance only for the receiving model and its stated tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance requires receiving-side checks of domains, every constraint, and the recomputed objective, with all translations and tolerances recorded.
assumptions_latex: Every receiving constraint has a specified residual convention.
Variable and objective translations are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing all recorded checks certifies feasibility and objective consistency under the receiving solver's tolerances.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cross-solver acceptance requires independent feasibility and objective checks in the receiving representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is defensible because the statement specifies a validation record witnessing receiving-side checks. However, the residual conventions, tolerances, objective-consistency test, and claimed certification scope are numerical-protocol choices with no supporting citation.

children.title: Restricted-Search Transfer Methods
children.top_down_role: Handoffs preserving unresolved decisions or defining restricted searches.

children.title: Partial-Assignment Transfer
children.top_down_role: Handoffs preserving specified decisions while leaving others unresolved.

assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in J\), \(\tau(i)\) is a receiving-variable index and \(\phi_i(\bar x_i)\) is defined.
All receiving constraints remain active during propagation and residual search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a fully validated completion, a certified infeasibility result for the restricted receiving model, or a no-solution-found status when the resource limit is reached.

notation.meaning: map from selected source indices to receiving indices
value-conversion map for selected source variable i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transferred partial values define a restricted receiving problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted search induced by a consistently mapped assignment on a subset of shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a source assignment, let \(J\) be a set of selected source-variable indices, let \(\tau\) map each \(i\in J\) to a receiving-variable index, and let \(\phi_i\) convert the value of source variable \(i\) to the corresponding receiving domain. Form the receiving fixings \(y_{\tau(i)}=\phi_i(\bar x_i)\) for all \(i\in J\). Reject the entire transfer if any selected variable is unmapped, if two transferred fixings assign different values to the same receiving variable, or if any converted value lies outside its receiving domain. Otherwise propagate all fixings in the complete receiving model. If propagation certifies inconsistency, report the restricted model infeasible; otherwise search the residual model under a prescribed resource limit and return only a fully validated completion. The partial assignment itself is not an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map all selected source values into a consistent set of receiving-side fixings, reject an invalid transfer as a whole, and search the resulting restricted model for a fully validated completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment Transfer

children.title: Neighborhood Transfer
children.top_down_role: Handoffs defining restricted search regions for the receiving solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a source-centered neighborhood as a receiving-side restricted search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a mapped reference assignment \(\bar y\), a neighborhood function \(N(\bar y,\Delta)\subseteq Y\), and receiving feasible set \(F_Y\), form the restricted region \(R=F_Y\cap N(\bar y,\Delta)\). Verify that every variable and distance component used by \(N\) has compatible receiving semantics. Search \(R\) under a prescribed resource limit, validate each candidate in the complete receiving model, and return the best accepted candidate according to the receiving objective. If compatibility fails or \(R\) is empty, reject the neighborhood transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a source-centered neighborhood into the receiving model, search its intersection with the feasible set, and validate all returned candidates.
assumptions_latex: The reference assignment is mapped into the receiving variable space \(Y\).
The neighborhood parameter \(\Delta\) has a declared receiving-side interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted output belongs to \(F_Y\cap N(\bar y,\Delta)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: neighborhood search restricts the feasible set by a reference-centered region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits neighborhood transfer and the restricted region is defined consistently. The compatibility test and transfer protocol are source-dependent, and no citation supports them; additionally, a source should clarify that 'best' means best candidate found within the resource limit rather than a proven optimum over the neighborhood.

children.title: Transferred-Fixing Scope
children.top_down_role: Coverage and lifetime of decisions fixed during cross-solver transfer.

knowledge_statements.title: Transferred-Fixing Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search scope over which transferred variable fixings remain active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be the transferred variable indices and let \(a_J\) be their mapped values. The scope of the transferred fixing is a designated search region \(S\) in which every processed subproblem includes \(x_J=a_J\). The fixing is global only if \(x_J=a_J\) is valid for every globally feasible solution; otherwise it defines a restricted search and must be removed when control leaves \(S\). Descendant reuse is sound only while no operation relaxes or contradicts the transferred equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transferred fixings remain active only in their designated restricted-search region unless proved valid for every globally feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: The mapped values \(a_J\) belong to the receiving variable domains.
The scope \(S\) is explicitly associated with the restricted search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within \(S\), all searched points satisfy \(x_J=a_J\); outside \(S\), the equalities require independent global justification.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixings define a restricted feasible set unless globally implied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and correctly separates a restricted-search fixing from an equality valid for all global feasible solutions. No inspectable source supports the designated-scope and descendant-reuse semantics in the target hybrid interface.

children.title: Neighborhood Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits arising when solver representations encode different restricted regions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the common feasible set represented by both solver abstractions.
The source neighborhood is \(N_S\subseteq X\).
The target-to-common correspondence \(\Lambda\subseteq X_T\times X\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact compatibility requires \(\mathcal L(F_T\cap R_T)=F\cap N_S\) and a feasible common lift for every point in \(F_T\cap R_T\); replacing equality by inclusion gives conservative compatibility.

notation.meaning: Common feasible set in the common solution space.
Source-solver neighborhood in the common solution space.
Target feasible set and installed target restrictions, respectively.
Set of feasible common lifts of a target set under the specified correspondence.
Incumbent whose preservation may be required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety boundary for transferring a restricted-search neighborhood between CP and MIP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the common feasible set, let \(N_S\subseteq X\) be the source neighborhood, let \(F_T\subseteq X_T\) be the target feasible set, and let \(R_T\subseteq X_T\) be the restrictions installed in the target solver. Let \(\Lambda\subseteq X_T\times X\) be the specified target-to-common correspondence and define \(\mathcal L(Y)=\{x\in F:\exists y\in Y\text{ with }(y,x)\in\Lambda\}\). The transfer is exactly compatible when every \(y\in F_T\cap R_T\) has a corresponding point in \(F\) and \(\mathcal L(F_T\cap R_T)=F\cap N_S\). It is conservative, though possibly incomplete, when every such target point has a feasible common lift and \(\mathcal L(F_T\cap R_T)\subseteq F\cap N_S\). If a restricted target point has no feasible common lift, or its feasible lift lies outside \(N_S\), target conclusions cannot be attributed to the source neighborhood. If preservation of an incumbent \(x^I\in F\) is required, one must additionally have \(x^I\in N_S\) and a point \(y^I\in F_T\cap R_T\) with \((y^I,x^I)\in\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighborhood transfer is exact when every restricted target point has a feasible common lift and the lifted restricted target set equals the source neighborhood within the common feasible set. Inclusion gives conservative compatibility; non-liftable or outside-neighborhood target points make attribution unsafe.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood Compatibility Boundaries

children.title: Cross-Abstraction Bound Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Comparison and aggregation of bounds produced by distinct solver abstractions.

children.title: Primal-Bound Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Comparison of feasible-solution bounds across solver abstractions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Bound Reconciliation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconciliation of incumbent bounds for a common minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose solver \(s\) reports a feasible solution \(x_s\) with local objective value \(u_s\). If feasibility is preserved by a lift \(\lambda_s(x_s)\in F\) and the common objective satisfies \(f(\lambda_s(x_s))=a_su_s+b_s\) with \(a_s>0\), then \(\bar u_s=a_su_s+b_s\) is a valid primal upper bound. The reconciled bound is \(U=\min_{s\in S_V}\bar u_s\), where \(S_V\) contains only solvers whose lifted solutions have been validated. A reported value lacking a feasible lift or an objective-preserving conversion must not update \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert each validated incumbent to the common objective scale and take the minimum; unliftable or incomparable incumbents cannot update the global upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The common problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\).
Each accepted incumbent has a validated feasible lift.
Each objective conversion has positive scale \(a_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^\star\le U=\min_{s\in S_V}(a_su_s+b_s)\).

notation.meaning: Primal bound reported in solver s's objective scale.
Lift from solver s's solution representation to the common space.

children.title: Dual-Bound Reconciliation
