children.top_down_role: Comparison of relaxation or proof-supported bounds across solver abstractions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Reconciliation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconciliation of globally valid relaxation bounds for a common minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose solver \(s\) proves a local lower bound \(\ell_s\) over a relaxation containing the image of every point in \(F\). If its objective conversion is order preserving and satisfies \(f(x)\ge a_s\ell_s+b_s\) for every \(x\in F\), where \(a_s>0\), then \(\bar\ell_s=a_s\ell_s+b_s\) is a valid common lower bound. The reconciled dual bound is \(L=\max_{s\in S_G}\bar\ell_s\), with \(S_G\) restricted to globally valid bounds. A local, conditional, or neighborhood-specific bound cannot enter \(S_G\) without separately proving global applicability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize globally valid lower bounds to the common objective and take their maximum; local or conditional bounds cannot be treated as global.
assumptions_latex: The common problem is a minimization problem with optimum \(f^\star\).
Each accepted relaxation contains the image of the common feasible set.
Each bound conversion preserves objective order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\max_{s\in S_G}(a_s\ell_s+b_s)\le f^\star\).

notation.meaning: Lower bound proved by solver s.

children.title: Conditional-Bound Reconciliation
children.top_down_role: Alignment of bounds valid only under specified decisions or contexts.

assumptions_latex: The common problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\).
All bound values have been converted to the common minimization objective scale.
Each lower bound \(L_i\) carries a validity region \(D_i\subseteq X\) and satisfies \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_i\).
Each incumbent value \(U_i\) carries a witness \(x_i\in F\) satisfying \(U_i=f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With the stated empty-set conventions, \(L(Q)\le\inf_{x\in F_Q}f(x)\), and every finite accepted \(U_i\) satisfies \(\inf_{x\in F_Q}f(x)\le U_i\).

notation.meaning: Current branch, neighborhood, or assignment condition.
Validity region attached to lower bound i.
Common feasible set restricted by Q.
Reconciled conditional lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability rule for bounds proved only under branch, neighborhood, or partial-assignment conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_Q=F\cap Q\) be the feasible region of a minimization subproblem. Suppose a normalized lower bound \(L_i\) has validity region \(D_i\subseteq X\), meaning that \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_i\). The recorded metadata certifies applicability to the subproblem whenever \(F_Q\subseteq D_i\), and the reconciled lower bound is \(L(Q)=\max\{L_i:F_Q\subseteq D_i\}\), with \(L(Q)=-\infty\) if no bound is eligible. A conditional incumbent value \(U_i=f(x_i)\) is usable only when its witness satisfies \(x_i\in F_Q\); define \(U(Q)=\min\{U_i:x_i\in F_Q\}\), with \(U(Q)=+\infty\) if no witness is eligible. Dropping validity metadata or replacing containment by mere nonempty intersection does not certify a node-wide pruning bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validity-region metadata certifies a conditional lower bound for the current subproblem when the whole current feasible region lies inside that validity region. A conditional incumbent is usable only with a feasible witness in the current region; empty eligible sets yield the usual infinite bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Bound Reconciliation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cover Aggregation of Conditional Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconciliation of lower bounds whose validity regions collectively cover a subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_Q\) be a minimization feasible region and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_m\), with \(m\ge1\), cover it: \(F_Q\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mD_i\). If \(L_i\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_Q\cap D_i\), then \(L_{\mathrm{cov}}=\min_{1\le i\le m}L_i\) is a valid lower bound on \(F_Q\). Taking the maximum is generally invalid unless a maximizing bound is valid throughout \(F_Q\). Empty pieces may be omitted; omitting a nonempty uncovered piece destroys the cover certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional lower bounds over regions covering the current subproblem combine by their minimum; their maximum is unsound unless the selected bound applies everywhere.
assumptions_latex: \(F_Q\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mD_i\).
\(L_i\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F_Q\cap D_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_iL_i\le\inf_{x\in F_Q}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Validity region of conditional lower bound i
Lower bound obtained from a covering family

knowledge_statements.title: Cover Aggregation of Conditional Lower Bounds

children.title: Cross-Abstraction Bound Comparability
children.top_down_role: Compatibility limits among bounds produced from different model abstractions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Abstraction Bound Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparability criterion for objective bounds produced by different solver abstractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two reported bounds are cross-abstraction comparable when they refer to the same optimization direction and common feasible problem, each carries a validity region, and each admits an order-preserving conversion to one common objective scale. For affine conversions this requires \(v_s\mapsto a_sv_s+b_s\) with \(a_s>0\). After conversion, two lower bounds may be ordered by their numerical values only on a region contained in both validity regions; primal values additionally require feasible witnesses. Values are not comparable when objective conventions, feasibility semantics, or validity regions cannot be reconciled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds are comparable only after aligning optimization direction, objective scale, feasible semantics, and validity regions; primal bounds also require feasible witnesses.
assumptions_latex: Each solver exposes its objective convention and bound validity metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Comparable bounds induce a valid numerical order on the intersection of their certified validity regions.

notation.meaning: Bound value in solver s's local objective scale.
Converted value on the common objective scale.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Optimal Generating Multiplier and Optimal Primal-Dual Pair p. 77

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Optimal Generating Multiplier and Optimal Primal-Dual Pair p. 77

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is coherent, but the cited nonlinear primal-dual section is indirect and does not establish the stated cross-solver comparability criterion, including validity-region and feasible-witness requirements. A direct source on heterogeneous solver bound exchange or a precisely matching formal interface is required.

children.title: Cross-Solver Justification System
children.top_down_role: Information required to justify cross-solver pruning, learning, and global refinement.

children.title: Hybrid Node-Pruning Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates supporting infeasibility- or bound-based pruning across solver models.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Node-Pruning Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable infeasibility and bound-dominance certificates shared across solver models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node with common feasible region \(F_Q\) and incumbent bound \(U\), a hybrid pruning certificate is either an infeasibility certificate \(C_{\varnothing}\) whose verifier establishes \(F_Q=\varnothing\), or a bound certificate \((C_L,L)\) whose verifier establishes \(f(x)\ge L\) for every \(x\in F_Q\). The node may be pruned in the first case, and in the second case when \(L\ge U\). Cross-solver acceptance additionally requires validation of the variable map, objective conversion, and certificate validity region; an unverified solver status alone is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is prunable by a verified infeasibility certificate or by a verified lower bound at least as large as the incumbent upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The common problem is minimized over \(F_Q\).
The incumbent value \(U\) is a valid global upper bound.
Certificate checking uses exact or conservatively sound arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_Q=\varnothing\) or \(L\ge U\) with \(L\le\inf_{x\in F_Q}f(x)\) certifies safe pruning.

notation.meaning: Common feasible region at the node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes pruning for finding an optimum from enumeration of every optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization node have certified lower bound \(L\), and let a verified incumbent have value \(U\). For finding one optimum or proving the optimal value, \(L\ge U\) certifies that the node contains no strictly improving solution. For enumerating every optimal solution, \(L=U\) does not certify that the node contains no additional optimum; pruning then requires an additional exclusion or completeness argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality with the incumbent rules out improvement but does not rule out additional co-optimal solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f(x)\) for every feasible completion in the node.
The incumbent is feasible and has objective value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
L\ge U\Rightarrow 
exists x	ext{ in the node with }f(x)<U,\qquad L=U
ot\Rightarrow 
exists x	ext{ in the node with }f(x)=U.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Pruning Objective Boundary

children.title: Reason-Conflict Translation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Translation of explanations into reusable conflicts, nogoods, or cuts.

children.title: Inference-Reason Representation
children.top_down_role: Solver-specific structures recording support for propagated deductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Inference-Reason Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal implication form of a propagation reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the solver state domain and let \(p_1,\ldots,p_k,q\) be Boolean or bound literals interpreted over \(D\). An inference reason for propagating \(q\) is represented by the valid implication \((p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\Rightarrow q\), meaning that every \(x\in D\) satisfying all antecedent literals also satisfies \(q\). The representation must retain the validity context \(D\), the literal semantics, and any numerical tolerances. The empty antecedent represents an unconditional inference. A tuple of antecedents without contextual validity does not suffice for cross-solver reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation reason is a context-valid implication from antecedent literals to the propagated literal, with literal meanings and numerical conventions retained.
assumptions_latex: Each literal has a fixed truth interpretation over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\models (p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\Rightarrow q\).

notation.meaning: Domain or solver context in which the inference is valid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering among inference reasons with the same conclusion and validity domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be finite sets of antecedent literals with \(B\subseteq A\), and let \(q\) be a conclusion literal. If \(D\models(\bigwedge_{p\in B}p)\Rightarrow q\), then that reason subsumes the reason with antecedent set \(A\), because \(D\models(\bigwedge_{p\in A}p)\Rightarrow q\). Merely deleting antecedents from a valid reason does not establish the smaller reason's validity; its implication must be verified independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified reason with fewer antecedents and the same conclusion is stronger, but antecedents cannot be dropped without revalidating the implication.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq A\).
Both reasons use the same domain and literal semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\models\left(\bigwedge_{p\in B}p\Rightarrow q\right)\Longrightarrow D\models\left(\bigwedge_{p\in A}p\Rightarrow q\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Reason Subsumption

children.title: Conflict Representation
children.top_down_role: Solver-specific structures recording incompatible decisions or conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nogood representation of an inconsistent combination of literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a validity domain and let \(p_1,\ldots,p_k\) be literals. A conflict is represented by the nogood \(
eg(p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\), equivalently by the clause \(
eg p_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg p_k\), provided no point \(x\in D\) satisfies every \(p_i\). The representation includes the domain \(D\), the literal-to-variable map, and the semantics of strict or non-strict bounds. It is globally reusable only when \(D\) contains the entire common feasible set; otherwise it remains conditional on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict is a domain-valid nogood forbidding simultaneous truth of specified literals; its reuse scope is determined by the domain where inconsistency was proved.
assumptions_latex: Each \(p_i\) has a fixed truth interpretation over \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(D\models
eg(p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\), equivalently \(D\models
eg p_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg p_k\).

notation.meaning: Literal participating in the inconsistent assignment.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering among nogoods over a common validity domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C'\subseteq C\) be sets of literals interpreted on the same domain \(D\). If \(D\models\neg\bigwedge_{p\in C'}p\), then \(D\models\neg\bigwedge_{p\in C}p\); hence the nogood for \(C'\) subsumes the nogood for \(C\). A conflict \(C\) is inclusion-minimal on \(D\) when it is valid and no proper subset of \(C\) is a conflict on \(D\). Minimality is not required for validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid conflict with fewer literals subsumes each extension of it; inclusion-minimality strengthens the conflict but is not required for correctness.
assumptions_latex: \(C'\subseteq C\).
All literals have identical semantics and share validity domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\models\neg\bigwedge_{p\in C'}p\;\Longrightarrow\;D\models\neg\bigwedge_{p\in C}p.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Subsumption and Minimality

children.title: Reason-to-Conflict Translation
children.top_down_role: Conversion of inference support into reusable conflict information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution step eliminating an intermediate propagated literal during conflict derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1\models A\lor q\) and \(D_2\models B\lor\neg q\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are disjunctions of literals and \(q\) has identical truth semantics in both clauses. Then the resolvent \(A\lor B\) is valid on \(D_1\cap D_2\). Consequently, repeated resolution of a conflict clause with valid reason clauses preserves validity on the intersection of all participating validity domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolving valid reason or conflict clauses on complementary occurrences of one identically interpreted literal yields a valid resolvent on their common validity domain.
assumptions_latex: The resolved literal \(q\) has identical truth semantics in both clauses.
Both parent clauses are valid on their stated domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_1\models A\lor q,\quad D_2\models B\lor\neg q\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D_1\cap D_2\models A\lor B.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preserving Resolution of Reasons
Reason-to-Conflict Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivation of a nogood when a propagated literal contradicts the current state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a valid reason \((p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\Rightarrow q\) on domain \(D\) and a current state entailing \(p_1,\ldots,p_k,
eg q\). Initialize the conflict literal set as \(C=\{p_1,\ldots,p_k,
eg q\}\). Output the nogood \(
eg( igwedge_{r\in C}r)\), equivalently \(
eg p_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg p_k\lor q\), together with domain \(D\) and the literal mapping. Resolution with other valid reasons may subsequently remove propagated literals, but each resolution step must preserve validity on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine a valid implication with the negation of its conclusion to obtain a context-tagged nogood, optionally resolving it with other valid reasons.
assumptions_latex: The input implication is valid throughout \(D\).
The current state entails every antecedent and \(\neg q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\models\neg(p_1\land\cdots\land p_k\land\neg q)\).

notation.meaning: Set of literals forming the initial conflict.
Validity domain inherited from the reason.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and logical translation are plausible, but the cited general CP section does not directly support conflict construction, context inheritance, or validity-preserving resolution. Because these algorithmic details depend on the precise conflict-analysis framework, a direct source is required.

children.title: Conflict-to-Cut Translation
children.top_down_role: Conversion of conflict information into master-compatible refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-to-Cut Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear inequality representation of a Boolean nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k\}\) be a conflict, and associate each literal \(p_i\) with a binary truth variable \(z_i\) satisfying \(z_i=1\) exactly when \(p_i\) is true. The nogood \(\neg(p_1\land\cdots\land p_k)\) is represented exactly by the linear cut \(\sum_{i=1}^k z_i\le k-1\). If \(p_i\) is a positive binary literal \(x_j=1\), use \(z_i=x_j\); if it is \(x_j=0\), use \(z_i=1-x_j\). The cut inherits the conflict's validity domain and is global only when the literal encoding and conflict are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode each conflict literal by a binary truth variable; forbidding all literals simultaneously yields the exact cut that their sum is at most one less than their count.
assumptions_latex: Every conflict literal has an exact binary truth-variable encoding.
The input nogood is valid on its recorded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg(\bigwedge_{i=1}^k p_i)\iff\sum_{i=1}^k z_i\le k-1\).

notation.meaning: Set of literals in the conflict.
Binary truth variable encoding literal i.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

children.title: Translation Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on preserving validity, scope, or strength across representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Way Channeling Does Not Preserve Reverse Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of equivalence-based translation through a one-way bridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,x\in\{0,1\}\). In the source representation impose \(p\leftrightarrow(x=1)\), so \(x=1\Rightarrow p=1\) is valid. Suppose the target bridge retains only \(p\Rightarrow x=1\), represented by \(p\le x\). The target assignment \((p,x)=(0,1)\) satisfies \(p\le x\) but falsifies \(x=1\Rightarrow p=1\). Therefore the source inference cannot be translated in the reverse direction through this one-way bridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-way channel can preserve its declared implication while invalidating an inference that relies on the missing converse.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) and \(x\) are binary.
The target model contains only the one-way bridge \(p\le x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\le x\not\models(x=1\Rightarrow p=1).
knowledge_statements.title: One-Way Channeling Does Not Preserve Reverse Inference
Translation Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for translating reasons, conflicts, and cuts between solver representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A translation \(T\) from source literals to target constraints is fidelity preserving on domain \(D\) when every source literal and its image have identical truth values for all corresponding points in \(D\), and source validity implies target validity after translation. Under this condition, valid implications and nogoods remain valid, and exact Boolean encodings preserve equivalence. Fidelity fails if \(T\) is only heuristic, loses strict-bound or tolerance semantics, omits auxiliary-variable conditions, or applies a locally valid statement outside \(D\). A one-way relaxation may transfer a valid consequence only in its proved implication direction; it cannot justify an equivalence-based conflict or cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translation is faithful only with domain-correct semantic preservation; lost tolerances, auxiliary conditions, locality, or reversed one-way implications can invalidate conflicts and cuts.
assumptions_latex: Source and target points are related by an explicit correspondence on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Semantic equivalence on \(D\) preserves reasons and conflicts; a proved one-way implication preserves only consequences in that direction.

notation.meaning: Translation from source literals to target constraints.
Domain on which translation fidelity is asserted.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the semantic cautions are plausible, but neither cited locator directly supports the full hybrid translation-fidelity criterion, especially tolerance semantics, auxiliary-variable conditions, locality, and one-way translation limits. Direct evidence is required.

children.title: Certificate Reuse Metadata
children.top_down_role: Context and persistence metadata governing safe certificate reuse.

children.title: Certificate Locality
children.top_down_role: Node, subtree, model, or global contexts limiting safe certificate use.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Locality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity scope attached to a reusable pruning or inference certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a certificate \(C\), its locality region \(D_C\subseteq X\) is a recorded set on which the verifier establishes the certified claim. At a node with feasible region \(F_Q\), reuse of \(C\) is sound when \(F_Q\subseteq D_C\). A global certificate has \(F\subseteq D_C\); a subtree certificate may instead use the region defined by ancestral branch decisions, and a neighborhood certificate uses its neighborhood restrictions. Mere intersection \(F_Q\cap D_C\ne\varnothing\) is insufficient for pruning the whole node. Any strengthening, deletion, or remapping of assumptions requires recomputing or conservatively shrinking the locality region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is reusable only where its validity region contains the entire current feasible region; overlap alone does not justify node-wide inference or pruning.
assumptions_latex: The certificate verifier records a validity region \(D_C\).
The current node has common feasible region \(F_Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_Q\subseteq D_C\) is sufficient for sound certificate reuse at the node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe locality reuse when only the current application region shrinks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If certificate \(C\) is valid throughout \(D_C\) and a current region satisfies \(F_Q\subseteq D_C\), then any narrowed region \(F'_Q\subseteq F_Q\) also satisfies \(F'_Q\subseteq D_C\). Thus narrowing the application region alone does not require changing the recorded locality, provided the certificate's own dependencies and semantics remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate valid on a node remains local-valid on any descendant or restriction contained in that node, unless its own dependencies or semantics change.
assumptions_latex: The certificate remains valid on the same region \(D_C\).
Only the intended application region is narrowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'_Q\subseteq F_Q\subseteq D_C\Longrightarrow F'_Q\subseteq D_C.
review_flags: Clarifies that feasible-region strengthening alone preserves containment; dependency or semantic changes remain lifetime/provenance concerns.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Region Narrowing

children.title: Certificate Provenance
children.top_down_role: Solver state, inference source, transformation stage, or subproblem origin attached to a certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata identifying the model state and inference process from which a reusable cross-solver certificate originated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For model versions indexed by \(v\), the provenance of a certificate \(c\) is a tuple \(P(c)=(s,v,A,h,r)\), where \(s\) identifies the producing solver, \(A\) identifies its inference procedure, \(h\) is a digest of the constraints and bounds used, and \(r\) records the solver result supporting \(c\). A consumer may attribute \(c\) to that derivation only if the supplied tuple is immutable and the digest recomputed from the declared dependency set equals \(h\). Provenance identifies an origin; it does not by itself establish validity under a different model version.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate provenance records the producing solver, inference procedure, model version, dependency digest, and supporting result, with an integrity check against the declared dependencies.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is communicated between solvers as a purported logical or optimization certificate.
Model versions and dependency sets have stable identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(c)=(s,v,A,h,r)\) uniquely records the declared origin of \(c\), subject to digest agreement.

notation.meaning: digest of the certificate's declared dependencies

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational definition of auditable certificate provenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational definition fits Certificate Provenance, but no source supports this particular tuple, digest requirement, or the claim that it uniquely records origin. The conclusion should distinguish integrity of declared metadata from uniqueness or validity.

children.title: Certificate Lifetime
children.top_down_role: Persistence intervals, invalidation events, or retirement conditions for retained certificates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient full-validation condition for continuing certificate validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(c\) was verified at \(M_s\) from complete dependency record \(D(c)\). Reuse at \(M_t\) is sound if the certificate remains authentic, every dependency retains equivalent meaning and is entailed by \(M_t\), its locality contains the intended region, and its arithmetic and tolerance semantics are unchanged or revalidated. Dependency entailment alone is insufficient when another condition fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserved dependencies support reuse only together with certificate integrity, locality, semantic mappings, and numerical compatibility.
assumptions_latex: \(D(c)\) is complete for the original derivation.
The original certificate was successfully verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Auth}(c)\wedge M_t\models D(c)\wedge\operatorname{ScopeOK}(c,M_t)\wedge\operatorname{SemOK}(c,M_t)\Longrightarrow V(c,M_t).
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Preservation Reuse Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation followed by restoration and revalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) certify \(x=0\) from the active constraint \(x=0\). At \(M_0\) the constraint is active, at \(M_1\) it is removed while \(x\in\{0,1\}\), and at \(M_2\) the identical constraint and semantics are restored and \(c\) is reverified. Then \(0,2\in\Lambda(c)\) but \(1\notin\Lambda(c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing and later restoring a dependency can give a certificate lifetime with a gap.
assumptions_latex: The restored constraint has the original semantics.
The certificate is reverified at \(M_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0,2\in\Lambda(c),\quad1\notin\Lambda(c).
knowledge_statements.title: Noninterval Certificate Lifetime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Possibly noncontiguous lifetime of a reusable certificate across model states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certificate \(c\) and model-state sequence \((M_t)_{t\in T}\), define \(\Lambda(c)=\{t\in T:V(c,M_t)=\mathrm{true}\}\), where \(V\) checks certificate integrity, dependencies, semantic mappings, numerical conventions, and intended scope. The lifetime \(\Lambda(c)\) need not be an interval because an invalidating change may later be reversed and the certificate revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate's lifetime is the set of model states where full reuse validation succeeds, which need not be continuous.
assumptions_latex: The verifier checks integrity, dependencies, semantics, numerical conventions, and scope.
Model states have stable identities sufficient for revalidation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Lambda(c)=\{t:V(c,M_t)\};\qquad \Lambda(c)\text{ need not be order-convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Admissibility Times
Certificate Lifetime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity interval of a reused certificate under monotone and nonmonotone changes to a hybrid model state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) be justified by assumptions \(D(c)\) at model state \(M_t\). Its lifetime is the maximal interval \([t_0,t_1)\) such that, for every \(t\) in that interval, the active model \(M_t\) entails every member of \(D(c)\). Thus \(c\) remains admissible after changes that preserve all its dependencies, including constraint additions when its derivation used only retained assumptions. Its lifetime ends before the first deletion, relaxation, domain enlargement, numerical-tolerance change, or semantic remapping that makes some dependency unavailable or inequivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate remains reusable exactly while every assumption used in its derivation is still entailed by the active model state.
assumptions_latex: \(D(c)\) contains all constraints, bounds, mappings, and tolerance conventions used to derive \(c\).
Model states \(M_t\) have a defined entailment relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\) is reusable at time \(t\) if and only if \(M_t\models d\) for every \(d\in D(c)\).

notation.meaning: complete dependency set of certificate c
active model state at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Dependency preservation is relevant to certificate lifetime, but validity need not form one interval, and dependency entailment alone is insufficient unless the original certificate and its complete dependency record are valid. An authoritative incremental-solving or certificate-reuse source is required.

children.title: Cooperative Solver Runtime
children.top_down_role: Operational mechanisms for invoking solvers and maintaining consistent duplicated state.

children.title: Solver Invocation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Synchronous invocation of external inference or optimization services.

children.title: Callback-Based Cooperation
children.top_down_role: In-process synchronous cooperation triggered at solver events.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal validity scope of an artifact computed from a callback snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If artifact a is computed from callback snapshot s with dependencies D(a), it may be applied at receiving state s' only when s' entails every dependency in D(a); otherwise it must be revalidated or discarded. Equality of event type or variable identifiers is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback response is reusable beyond its generating snapshot only while all supporting assumptions remain valid.
assumptions_latex: The generating snapshot and complete dependencies of a are identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s'\models D(a)\text{ is required for direct application of }a\text{ at }s'.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Snapshot Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which auxiliary callbacks preserve primary-solver soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the callback-free primary solver is sound. Callback cooperation remains sound if every incorporated artifact is verified as a constraint or bound valid on its declared current subtree, or as a feasible incumbent for the current model and objective, and callback failure or rejection causes no pruning or certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks preserve soundness when every accepted artifact is validated for its current scope and callback failure has no logical effect.
assumptions_latex: The callback-free primary solver is sound.
Every accepted artifact is validated for the current model and scope.
Failure or rejection does not remove search states or certify a conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sound}(P)\land\operatorname{ValidatedCallbacks}\Rightarrow\operatorname{Sound}(P_{cb}).

notation.meaning: primary solver without and with callbacks

review_flags: revised_from_builder: removed unsupported equality of callback and callback-free conclusion sets
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Soundness Envelope
Callback-Based Cooperation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous cooperation in which one solver invokes another while processing a search event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a primary model \(M\), an auxiliary-solver map \(S\), and eligible event types \(E\). Initialize the primary search and shared identifier map. Whenever event \(e\in E\) occurs at state \(z\), construct a request \(q(e,z)\), invoke \(S(q(e,z))\) synchronously, and validate the returned object \(a\) against the current model version. If \(a\) is a valid bound, solution, propagation, or certificate, incorporate it through an interface permitted at \(e\); otherwise discard it. Stop when the primary solver terminates and return its status, incumbent, bound, and accepted cross-solver certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At selected search events, the primary solver synchronously calls an auxiliary solver, validates its response, and incorporates only interface-permitted information.
assumptions_latex: Every shared variable and constraint has a stable cross-model identifier.
The callback contract specifies which model modifications are legal at each event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every incorporated response is validated against the model state associated with its callback event.

notation.meaning: auxiliary-solver request formed from event and state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits callback-based cooperation, but callback legality, synchronous invocation, validation, and accepted response types are interface-dependent claims with no cited solver-interface source.

children.title: Service-Based Cooperation
children.top_down_role: External inference or optimization exposed through a service boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety condition for retried or multiply delivered service responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If transport can deliver response r more than once, the receiver must deduplicate by a stable response identifier or apply an idempotent transformation T_r satisfying T_r(T_r(z))=T_r(z).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate service responses are safe only with deduplication or idempotent application.
assumptions_latex: The transport may duplicate requests or responses.
The response identity is stable across retries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_r\circ T_r=T_r\quad\text{or r is committed at most once}.

notation.meaning: receiver-state transformation induced by response r

review_flags: revised_from_builder: title no longer assumes a particular delivery guarantee
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Delivery Safety

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When remote transport preserves an abstract solver-oracle contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let O(q) be the admissible verified answers to request q. Replacing an in-process oracle by a service preserves the caller's mathematical soundness when every accepted response a is associated with q, is compatible with the current model version, satisfies a\in O(q), and communication failure is treated as no answer rather than as a mathematical conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A remote service safely substitutes for an oracle when accepted responses satisfy the same checked contract and communication failure yields no inference.
assumptions_latex: Requests and responses cannot be silently misassociated.
The caller validates the oracle contract and model-version scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\text{ accepted for }q\Rightarrow a\in O(q).

notation.meaning: admissible verified answers to request q

review_flags: revised_from_builder: limited conclusion to sound substitution rather than unspecified full equivalence
knowledge_statements.title: Service Substitution Condition
Service-Based Cooperation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-based cooperation between independently executing solver services with explicit version checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input solver services \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\), a shared identifier map, and a versioned message protocol. A service \(S_i\) sends a request \((i,j,v,p)\) containing destination \(j\), model version \(v\), and payload \(p\). Service \(S_j\) returns \((v,a,\sigma)\), where \(a\) is an inference or solution artifact and \(\sigma\) is its status. The receiver accepts \(a\) only if its identifiers resolve, its provenance is valid, and version \(v\) remains compatible with the receiver's current state. Services continue independently until a coordinator's termination predicate holds, then return the aggregated status and accepted artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent solver services exchange versioned requests and artifacts; receivers accept responses only after identifier, provenance, and compatibility checks.
assumptions_latex: Message delivery is authenticated or otherwise protected from undetected corruption.
Compatibility of two model versions is decidable from recorded changes and artifact dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An artifact \(a\) affects another service only after validation against the receiving service's current model state.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits service-based cooperation, but the proposed message schema, compatibility test, provenance rules, and coordinator behavior are an uncited protocol design rather than a sourced standard formulation.

children.title: Invocation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Timeout, reentrancy, availability, or response-validity risks at cooperation boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A response valid at its request version can be unsafe at the receiving version.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At version v, let M_v contain x\ge1 and return that bound. Delete the supporting constraint before receipt, obtaining M_{v'} with feasible point x=0. Importing x\ge1 at v' removes a feasible point although the artifact was valid at v.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a supporting constraint can make an earlier valid bound unsafe to import.
assumptions_latex: x=0 is feasible in M_{v'}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_v\models x\ge1\quad\text{and}\quad M_{v'}\not\models x\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Bound After Constraint Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical meaning of an invocation without a conclusive verified result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A timeout, unavailable service, or UNKNOWN status supplies neither a feasible solution nor an infeasibility or objective-bound certificate unless a separate artifact was completed and verified before interruption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Timeout, unavailability, and unknown status justify no pruning by themselves.
assumptions_latex: No separately completed and verified artifact was returned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{TIMEOUT}\lor\mathrm{UNKNOWN}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}.
knowledge_statements.title: Timeout and Unknown-Status Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Liveness boundary for synchronous nested invocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a primary execution holds an exclusive non-reentrant resource L while synchronously invoking an auxiliary execution that must acquire L before returning, the wait-for graph contains a cycle and the cooperation can deadlock. Mathematical validity of prospective artifacts does not remove this liveness failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous auxiliary invocation can deadlock when it reacquires a resource held by the waiting caller.
assumptions_latex: L is exclusive and non-reentrant.
The primary execution waits for the auxiliary execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\to A\to L\to P\text{ is a deadlock cycle}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reentrancy and Blocking Boundary
Invocation Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which an auxiliary invocation cannot safely modify the primary solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an auxiliary invocation starts from model version \(v\) and returns artifact \(a\). Safe incorporation fails whenever the current version \(v'\) neither equals \(v\) nor entails every dependency of \(a\), or whenever \(a\) uses unresolved identifiers, exceeds the callback's permitted operations, lacks a conclusive status, or violates the common numerical convention. Concretely, if \(a\) proves \(x\le 0\) using a constraint deleted between \(v\) and \(v'\), importing that bound can remove feasible solutions. Across this boundary, the response must be rejected, revalidated, or recomputed rather than incorporated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A response is unsafe when its dependencies, identifiers, status, permitted operations, or numerical conventions do not match the receiving solver state.
assumptions_latex: Each returned artifact declares its model version and dependencies.
The receiving solver can test identifier and interface compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If compatibility fails, incorporating \(a\) is not validity-preserving and \(a\) must be rejected, revalidated, or recomputed.

notation.meaning: model version used by the auxiliary invocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and dependency-loss example fit the leaf. However, failure of a compatibility check establishes that incorporation is unjustified, not necessarily that the artifact is mathematically invalid, and no solver-interface source supports the full boundary list.

children.title: Separate-Model Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of variable identities, constraints, bounds, and solution state across models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of transferred incumbents and objective bounds between separate models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_C,F_M be current feasible sets and let \pi_C,\pi_M map local solutions to shared semantic decisions. A solution x\in F_C becomes an incumbent for model M only after constructing y\in F_M with \pi_M(y)=\pi_C(x) and evaluating y under the receiving objective convention. Bounds may be combined only when their optimization direction, objective normalization, feasible-region scope, and assumptions agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred solution needs a feasible receiving-model lift, and bounds are comparable only under matching objective and validity scopes.
assumptions_latex: The semantic projections \pi_C and \pi_M are defined.
Each bound records its objective convention and validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in F_C\not\Rightarrow x\text{ is a receiving-model incumbent or its bound is globally comparable}.

notation.meaning: current feasible sets of the two models

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-State Synchronization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matching identifiers and stored bounds do not establish matching semantic domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If x_C=q and x_M=10q, assigning both local variables the identifier of q and the stored interval [0,10] represents respectively q\in[0,10] and q\in[0,1]. Thus identifier equality and syntactic bound equality do not imply synchronization without the representation map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identically named variables with identical stored bounds can denote different semantic domains when their encodings differ.
assumptions_latex: The two models use different numerical encodings of the shared quantity q.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{id}(x_C)=\operatorname{id}(x_M)\not\Rightarrow D_C(q)=D_M(q).
knowledge_statements.title: Identifier Agreement Without Semantic Synchronization
Separate-Model Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant for distinct CP and MIP models representing shared decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M^{\mathrm{CP}}_t\) and \(M^{\mathrm{MIP}}_t\) be model states with shared semantic variables indexed by \(I\), and let \(\phi_t\) map their representations. They are synchronized at time \(t\) when \(\phi_t\) is defined on every shared active object, corresponding variable domains and fixed values agree, every transferred constraint has equivalent meaning under \(\phi_t\), and every imported solution or bound is tagged with a compatible version. Synchronization requires atomic propagation of additions, deletions, bound changes, and identifier remappings before either model consumes cross-model information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate CP and MIP models are synchronized when shared identities, domains, transferred constraints, versions, bounds, and solutions agree under an explicit mapping.
assumptions_latex: Both models expose stable identifiers and versioned updates.
The mapping \(\phi_t\) specifies any scaling or encoding differences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every shared index \(i\in I\), \(D^{\mathrm{CP}}_{i,t}=\phi_t^{-1}(D^{\mathrm{MIP}}_{i,t})\), with equivalent transferred state.

notation.meaning: CP and MIP model states at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: synchronization invariant for duplicate models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The synchronization invariant fits the node, but the domain and codomain of the representation map are unspecified, making its inverse-image conclusion insufficiently typed. The asserted atomic-update requirement is architectural and also needs a source.

children.title: Solver State Reuse Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Reuse and controlled replacement of solver state across cooperation rounds.

children.title: Incremental Solver State
children.top_down_role: Persistent solver state reused across related cooperation rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness distinction between reusable hints and retained logical conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A retained basis, incumbent candidate, branching score, or search hint may initialize a later solve without being trusted as a certificate. If feasibility is checked and every pruning or terminal conclusion is derived under the current model, using or rejecting the hint can change runtime and search order but cannot create an invalid certified conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start information affects performance rather than correctness when all logical uses are revalidated under the current model.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility, bounds, pruning, and terminal conclusions are checked under the current model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ValidatedUse}(h,M)\Rightarrow\operatorname{SoundnessIndependentOfHint}(h).
review_flags: revised_from_builder: removed equality of certified-outcome sets, which need not hold for incomplete or resource-limited runs
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Neutrality
Incremental Solver State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable solver state maintained across a sequence of related model versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a versioned model sequence \((M_t)_{t\ge 0}\), an incremental solver state is a pair \(Z_t=(M_t,R_t)\), where \(R_t\) contains retained search data such as learned constraints, propagation structures, bases, incumbents, bounds, and branching statistics. An update \(\Delta_t\) transforms \(Z_t\) into \(Z_{t+1}\) by applying the model change and retaining precisely those elements of \(R_t\) whose declared dependencies remain entailed by \(M_{t+1}\). Reuse is sound only when retained logical artifacts remain valid; heuristic statistics may be retained separately without being treated as certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental state combines the current model with reusable search artifacts, retaining only logically valid artifacts after each versioned update.
assumptions_latex: Each logical artifact in \(R_t\) has recoverable dependencies.
Updates \(\Delta_t\) produce identifiable model versions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_{t+1}=(M_{t+1},R_{t+1})\) with every logical \(r\in R_{t+1}\) valid for \(M_{t+1}\).

notation.meaning: retained solver artifacts at version t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits incremental solver state, but retaining precisely all dependency-preserved artifacts assumes complete, recoverable dependencies and does not describe common solver-specific restrictions. An authoritative incremental-solving source is needed.

children.title: Inference Caches
children.top_down_role: Retained propagation, feasibility, bound, or certificate results keyed to reusable contexts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound reuse under a context stronger than the recorded supporting context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a cache entry records a valid implication A\Rightarrow a and A contains every logical dependency of a. For any current context C, the cached inference a is sound whenever C\models A. Syntactic equality of C and A is sufficient but unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached inference is reusable in any current context entailing its complete supporting context.
assumptions_latex: A\models a.
A contains every logical dependency of a.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (A\models a)\land(C\models A)\Rightarrow C\models a.
knowledge_statements.title: Entailment-Based Cache Reuse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness effect of removing inference-cache entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every miss invokes the underlying inference procedure and cached entries are not the sole record of unresolved search obligations, deleting any subset of cache entries cannot introduce an invalid inference. Eviction can increase recomputation or change timing; completeness is preserved when the fallback procedure supplies every inference required for completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eviction affects performance, not soundness, and preserves completeness when misses use the required underlying inference procedure.
assumptions_latex: Cache misses invoke the underlying inference procedure.
The cache is not the sole record of unresolved search obligations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K'\subseteq K\Rightarrow\operatorname{Sound}(K')\text{ whenever the fallback procedure is sound}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Eviction Neutrality
Inference Caches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-indexed storage of previously computed propagations, bounds, conflicts, or feasibility results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inference cache for model state \(M\) is a finite map \(K:q\mapsto(a,D,v)\), where the query key \(q\) identifies an inference request, \(a\) is the stored answer, \(D\) is the complete set of model assumptions supporting that answer, and \(v\) is its originating version. A lookup at a current model \(M'\) is a cache hit only when the query semantics are unchanged and \(M'\models d\) for every \(d\in D\). Otherwise the entry is stale and must not be used as a logical inference, although it may be recomputed and replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inference cache stores answers with complete dependencies and versions; a cached answer is reusable only when its query and every recorded dependency remain valid.
assumptions_latex: Cache keys encode all query parameters that can affect an answer.
Logical cache entries record complete dependency sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(K(q)=(a,D,v)\), then the entry is reusable under \(M'\) only if the query semantics are unchanged and \(M'\models d\) for every \(d\in D\).

notation.meaning: complete dependency set supporting a cached answer

children.title: Restart Policies
children.top_down_role: Controlled solver-state replacement following invalidation, stagnation, or excessive accumulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Increasing-budget restart variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose b_0>0 and \gamma>1. Run with budget b_k=b_0\gamma^k and, absent terminal status, restart under the retention policy. For any required uninterrupted budget B>0, the first nonnegative index with b_k\ge B is k=\max\{0,\lceil\log_\gamma(B/b_0)\rceil\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric schedule multiplies successive run budgets by a fixed factor and eventually supplies every finite uninterrupted budget.
assumptions_latex: \gamma>1.
Restarts preserve the model and all retained logical artifacts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k=\max\{0,\lceil\log_\gamma(B/b_0)\rceil\}\Rightarrow b_k\ge B.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Restart Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition preventing restarts from starving finite complete search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite instance whose uninterrupted complete search finishes within budget B_{finish}, restarting preserves completeness if unresolved frontier coverage is retained, or if some run i receives b_i\ge B_{finish}. Infinitely many runs with b_i<B_{finish} that repeatedly discard the frontier need not terminate or prove infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completeness requires retained unresolved coverage or an eventually long-enough uninterrupted run.
assumptions_latex: The underlying uninterrupted procedure is complete and finishes within finite budget B_{finish} on the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{retainFrontier}\lor(\exists i:b_i\ge B_{finish})\Rightarrow\operatorname{complete};\quad (\forall i:b_i<B_{finish})\text{ need not be complete}.

notation.meaning: budget sufficient for an uninterrupted complete run

knowledge_statements.title: Completeness Under Restarting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness preservation independent of restart frequency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restarting preserves soundness when the model semantics are unchanged, every retained logical artifact remains valid, and every retained incumbent is feasible for the current model. Restart frequency may affect progress and runtime but cannot by itself create a valid-looking false feasibility, bound, or optimality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart frequency does not affect soundness when the model and retained artifacts remain valid.
assumptions_latex: The restarted model has unchanged semantics.
Retained logical artifacts and incumbents remain valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SoundBeforeRestart}\Rightarrow\operatorname{SoundAfterRestart}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Soundness
Restart Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for discarding search trajectory while selectively retaining valid reusable state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a solver state \(Z_t=(M_t,R_t)\), restart statistics \(u_t\), a trigger predicate \(T(u_t)\), and a retention predicate \(V(r,M_t)\). Continue the current search while \(T(u_t)\) is false. When \(T(u_t)\) becomes true, terminate the current search trajectory, retain \(R'_t=\{r\in R_t:V(r,M_t)\}\), discard the remaining trajectory-dependent state, initialize a new root search on \(M_t\) using \(R'_t\), and reset the prescribed statistics. Output the first terminal solution status reached, together with any valid incumbent and bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart trigger ends the current search trajectory, preserves artifacts passing a validity predicate, and initializes a new root search.
assumptions_latex: The trigger \(T\) depends only on observable restart statistics.
The predicate \(V\) distinguishes valid reusable artifacts from trajectory-dependent state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After a restart, the new search uses exactly \(R'_t=\{r\in R_t:V(r,M_t)\}\) from the previous trajectory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and abstract restart procedure fit the leaf, but no source supports this trigger-and-retention policy. The stated output also presumes eventual terminal status without a termination assumption.

children.title: Reuse Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model changes or context shifts that make retained state unsafe or ineffective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes feasibility artifacts from objective-dependent artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Changing only the objective preserves objective-independent feasibility consequences but can invalidate incumbent rankings, reduced costs, objective cutoffs, objective bounds, and optimality certificates. An objective-dependent artifact is reusable only after a validity-preserving transformation or revalidation for the new objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective change preserves feasibility deductions but generally invalidates objective-dependent search and certification artifacts.
assumptions_latex: The constraint-defined feasible set is unchanged.
No equivalence between the old and new objectives has already been certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'=F\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{Valid}_{c'}(r_c).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Change Invalidation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between ineffective guidance and unsafe retained conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stale branching score, activity value, or priority need not be unsound when used only to order otherwise valid choices, although it may degrade performance. The same datum requires current-model validation before it may prune, declare infeasibility, or certify a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale heuristic guidance may be ineffective without being unsound, but cannot be promoted to a logical conclusion without validation.
assumptions_latex: Ordering-only use removes no feasible state and certifies no terminal status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{stale}(h)\land\operatorname{orderingOnly}(h)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{unsound};\quad\operatorname{logicalUse}(h)\Rightarrow\operatorname{revalidate}(h).
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Staleness Versus Logical Invalidity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp preservation boundary for retained logical consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r be a consequence of model M. If \operatorname{Sol}(M')\subseteq\operatorname{Sol}(M) and all symbols in r retain their meanings, then r remains valid for M'. Under relaxation, validity need not persist because a newly admitted solution may violate r.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logical consequences survive semantic strengthening with unchanged meanings but need not survive relaxation.
assumptions_latex: All symbols occurring in r have unchanged semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sol}(M')\subseteq\operatorname{Sol}(M)\land M\models r\Rightarrow M'\models r;\quad \operatorname{Sol}(M)\subsetneq\operatorname{Sol}(M')\not\Rightarrow M'\models r.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening–Relaxation Asymmetry
Reuse Invalidation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model changes beyond which retained logical or numerical solver artifacts cease to be sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an artifact \(r\) be valid for model \(M\) under dependencies \(D(r)\). Reuse crosses an invalidation boundary at model \(M'\) when some dependency is no longer entailed, an identifier changes meaning, a variable encoding or objective convention changes incompatibly, or numerical tolerances cease to support the recorded conclusion. For example, a learned inequality derived using \(x\le 1\) need not remain valid after that bound is relaxed to \(x\le 2\). At the boundary, \(r\) must be discarded or rederived; merely updating its version tag cannot restore soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse becomes invalid when a dependency, semantic identity, encoding, objective convention, or required numerical tolerance is no longer preserved.
assumptions_latex: The artifact \(r\) records the assumptions required for its logical validity.
Model changes from \(M\) to \(M'\) are auditable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(M'\not\models d\) for some \(d\in D(r)\), then \(r\) cannot be reused as a valid inference for \(M'\).

children.title: Assignment Master with CP Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Assignment or allocation decisions coordinated with resource-constrained scheduling subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Master with CP Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based decomposition with master assignment decisions and CP scheduling feasibility subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let binary \(y_{ij}\) assign job \(i\) to resource \(j\), and let \(Y\) contain the master assignment and allocation constraints. For fixed \(y\in Y\), define \(\mathcal S(y)\) as the set of start times and optional intervals satisfying precedence, release, deadline, and resource constraints induced by \(y\). The hybrid problem is \[\min_{y\in Y}\left\{c^\top y+Q(y):\mathcal S(y)\ne\varnothing\right\},\qquad Q(y)=\min_{s\in\mathcal S(y)}g(y,s).\] The MIP master chooses \(y\); a CP scheduling subproblem either supplies a schedule and value or returns a valid infeasibility explanation for master refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP master selects assignments, while a CP subproblem schedules the selected jobs and returns either a schedule or valid infeasibility feedback.
assumptions_latex: The master-feasible set \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\) represents assignment and allocation restrictions.
For fixed \(y\), the CP model exactly represents the intended scheduling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A master assignment \(y\) is feasible for the hybrid model if and only if \(y\in Y\) and \(\mathcal S(y)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: binary assignment of job i to resource j
CP-feasible schedules induced by assignment y

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Assignment Master with CP Scheduling, but the cited CP overview and restricted-master section do not specifically locate the claimed CP–MIP decomposition or infeasibility-feedback mechanism. The sets, cost vector, and scheduling objective also require explicit domains before this exact formulation can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Production-Scheduling Feasibility Coupling

children.title: Capacity Planning Decisions
children.top_down_role: Aggregate resource availability choices passed from the production master.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Planning Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete master decisions that install or activate capacity subsequently consumed by a scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite set of resources and \(T\) a finite set of planning periods. A capacity-planning decision is an integer vector \(z=(z_{jt})_{j\in J,t\in T}\) satisfying \(z_{jt}\in\{0,1,\ldots,U_{jt}\}\), where each selected unit contributes capacity \(a_{jt}\ge 0\). Given base capacity \(C^0_{jt}\), the installed capacity is \(C_{jt}(z)=C^0_{jt}+a_{jt}z_{jt}\). A downstream schedule \(s\) is capacity-admissible only if its resource usage satisfies \(u_{jt}(s)\le C_{jt}(z)\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(t\in T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity-planning variables choose integer numbers of identical resource units; base capacity plus the selected additions bounds resource use in every downstream schedule.
assumptions_latex: The sets \(J\) and \(T\), base capacities \(C^0_{jt}\), unit contributions \(a_{jt}\), and integer upper bounds \(U_{jt}\) are given.
The scheduling model measures usage \(u_{jt}(s)\) in units compatible with \(C_{jt}(z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every capacity-admissible schedule \(s\) satisfies \(u_{jt}(s)\le C_{jt}(z)\) for all \(j\in J\) and \(t\in T\).

notation.meaning: number of identical capacity units selected for resource j in period t
installed capacity induced by the planning decision

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Applications and special types of mathematical programming model p. 67

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Applications and special types of mathematical programming model p. 67

children.title: Lot-Sizing Decisions
children.top_down_role: Production quantities, setup choices, or inventory commitments preceding detailed scheduling.

knowledge_statements.title: Lot-Sizing Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon lot-sizing variables passed from a production-planning master to a scheduling subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For products \(i\in I\) and periods \(t=1,\ldots,T\), lot-sizing decisions comprise production quantities \(q_{it}\ge 0\), setup indicators \(y_{it}\in\{0,1\}\), and end-of-period inventories \(s_{it}\ge 0\). Given demands \(d_{it}\), initial inventories \(s_{i0}\), capacities \(C_t\), processing coefficients \(a_i\), and valid bounds \(U_{it}\), they satisfy \[s_{i,t-1}+q_{it}=d_{it}+s_{it},\qquad q_{it}\le U_{it}y_{it},\qquad \sum_{i\in I}a_iq_{it}\le C_t.\] In a CP–MIP hybrid, the selected vector \((q,y)\) determines the jobs and aggregate resource loads submitted to detailed scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lot-sizing chooses production quantities and setups while enforcing inventory balance, setup linking, and aggregate capacity; these choices induce the jobs checked by detailed scheduling.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) are finite.
\(d_{it},C_t,a_i,U_{it}\ge 0\), with each \(U_{it}\) a valid production bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((q,y,s)\) is an aggregate-feasible lot-sizing plan whose induced jobs may still require a scheduling-feasibility check.

notation.meaning: production quantity, setup indicator, and ending inventory
demand for product i in period t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited uncapacitated lot-sizing section does not adequately support the displayed capacitated formulation or the asserted production-to-scheduling coupling. A capacitated lot-sizing or production-planning/scheduling hybrid source is required.

children.title: Schedule Feasibility Checks
children.top_down_role: Detailed temporal checks for aggregate production commitments.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Feasibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CP feasibility certificate for jobs induced by fixed production-planning decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J(q,y)\) be the finite set of jobs induced by fixed lot-sizing decisions. Job \(j\) has duration \(p_j\), release time \(r_j\), deadline \(d_j\), resource demand \(u_{jk}\), and start time \(S_j\). A schedule-feasibility certificate is an assignment \(S\) satisfying \[r_j\le S_j,\qquad S_j+p_j\le d_j\quad(j\in J),\] every required precedence relation \(S_i+p_i\le S_j\), and, at every time \(\tau\), \[\sum_{j:S_j\le\tau<S_j+p_j}u_{jk}\le C_k\quad(k\in K).\] Direct evaluation of these finitely stated constraints verifies that the master decision admits a detailed schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment of job start times certifies that all induced jobs meet their time windows, precedences, and resource capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(J(q,y)\) and \(K\) are finite.
\(p_j\ge0\), and all time and resource data are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed start-time assignment certifies scheduling feasibility of the fixed master decision \((q,y)\).

notation.meaning: jobs induced by the lot-sizing decision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically recognizable, but the generic CP citation does not specifically support this cumulative-resource scheduling formulation or its use as a certificate for fixed lot-sizing decisions.

children.title: Scheduling Infeasibility Feedback
children.top_down_role: Master-level refinements derived from infeasible detailed schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Infeasibility Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based cut derived from an infeasible scheduling subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let binary master literals \(z_\ell=\bar z_\ell\), indexed by \(\ell\in L\), fix a production decision whose induced scheduling subproblem is infeasible. If a subset \(C\subseteq L\) is itself sufficient for infeasibility, then the nogood \[\sum_{\ell\in C:\bar z_\ell=1}(1-z_\ell)+\sum_{\ell\in C:\bar z_\ell=0}z_\ell\ge1\] is valid for every master solution admitting a feasible schedule. The core \(C\), together with a CP infeasibility explanation establishing that its literals cannot be jointly extended to a schedule, is a verifiable feedback certificate excluding the current assignment and every assignment containing the same core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explained infeasible core yields a nogood requiring at least one responsible master literal to change, thereby excluding all decisions containing that core.
assumptions_latex: \(z_\ell\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(\ell\in L\).
Fixing \(z_\ell=\bar z_\ell\) for all \(\ell\in C\) makes the scheduling subproblem infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nogood is valid for the projection of all production decisions having a feasible detailed schedule.

notation.meaning: value in the rejected master solution

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nogood is valid under the stated infeasible-core assumption, but neither cited locator specifically supports CP explanations or logic-based infeasibility feedback to a MIP master.

children.title: Cost Relaxations with Resource Propagation
children.top_down_role: Mathematical cost and capacity bounds combined with specialized resource inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost Relaxations with Resource Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of a valid objective relaxation with sound CP resource-domain filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:x\in F\}\), where \(F\subseteq X\) includes detailed resource constraints. Let \(R\supseteq F\) be a tractable cost relaxation and let \(P:X\to X\) be a sound resource-propagation operator satisfying \(F\cap D=F\cap P(D)\) for every current domain \(D\subseteq X\). Then \[L(D)=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in R\cap P(D)\}\] is a valid lower bound on every feasible completion in \(D\). If \(R\cap P(D)=\varnothing\), the node is infeasible; if \(L(D)\) is no smaller than the incumbent value, the node may be pruned without removing an improving feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound resource propagation shrinks domains without losing feasible solutions; optimizing a relaxation over the reduced domain gives a valid cost bound for pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\).
\(P\) preserves all points of \(F\) in every current domain.
An incumbent feasible objective value is available when bound pruning is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D)\) is a valid minimization lower bound, and emptiness or incumbent domination permits sound pruning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Separate generic references to LP relaxation and CP do not substantiate the combined propagation-and-bound principle, particularly the preservation identity and resulting pruning claims.
