children.title: MIP Routing with CP Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Route selection coordinated with detailed scheduling subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Routing with CP Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative route selection in a MIP master and detailed temporal feasibility in CP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a directed graph \(G=(V,A)\), routing costs \(c_a\), service jobs, and scheduling constraints. Initialize a MIP master over \(x_a\in\{0,1\}\) with routing and aggregate-capacity constraints. Repeatedly solve \[\min\sum_{a\in A}c_ax_a\] subject to the master constraints; submit the selected arcs and induced job orders to a CP scheduling subproblem. If CP returns a feasible schedule, retain the route-schedule pair and stop when the master bound proves optimality. If CP returns an explained infeasible core \(C\) of selected arcs or order literals, add a valid nogood excluding \(C\), then re-solve. Report infeasibility when the master becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP chooses routes, CP schedules their operations, and explained scheduling conflicts become master cuts until a certified solution or infeasibility is obtained.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and the scheduling domains are finite.
Every returned nogood excludes only route assignments with no feasible schedule.
Each master problem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the algorithm returns a feasible route-schedule pair with a master optimality certificate, or certifies infeasibility after exhaustive valid cuts.

notation.meaning: indicator that arc a is selected

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited modeling and introductory CP sections do not establish this route-master/CP-scheduling algorithm, its conflict feedback, or its finite optimality and infeasibility conclusions.

children.title: Route Master with Loading or Packing Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Network decisions checked against loading, packing, or sequencing feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Route Master with Loading or Packing Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Route master decisions checked by vehicle-specific loading or packing models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a routing instance and item dimensions, weights, and compatibility data. Solve a MIP master whose binary variables \(x_a\) select routes and whose assignment variables \(z_{iv}\) allocate item \(i\) to vehicle \(v\), subject to network flow and aggregate vehicle-capacity constraints. For every used vehicle, solve a CP subproblem seeking placements or loading sequences for \(\{i:z_{iv}=1\}\). A feasible placement validates that vehicle. From any explained infeasible item set \(C\), add the master cut \[\sum_{i\in C}z_{iv}\le |C|-1.\] Repeat until every used vehicle is validated, or the master is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses routes and item-to-vehicle assignments; packing subproblems validate each load and return cuts forbidding infeasible item combinations.
assumptions_latex: The item and vehicle sets are finite.
Each returned set \(C\) is infeasible for vehicle \(v\) independently of unselected items.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output combines master-feasible routes with a feasible detailed load for every used vehicle, or establishes infeasibility under the accumulated valid cuts.

notation.meaning: assignment of item i to vehicle v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The item-set cut is valid under the stated core assumption, but the cited generic IP and CP sections do not support the routing/loading decomposition or its termination conclusion.

children.title: Routing Relaxations with Time-Window Propagation
children.top_down_role: Network relaxations strengthened by temporal-domain inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Routing Relaxations with Time-Window Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation of a routing relaxation with sound temporal-domain propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a directed graph \(G=(V,A)\), travel times \(t_{ij}\), and service windows \([e_i,l_i]\). Initialize arrival domains \(D_i=[e_i,l_i]\) and a routing relaxation over arc variables \(0\le x_{ij}\le1\). Iterate to a fixed point: remove an arc \((i,j)\) whenever \[\min D_i+t_{ij}>\max D_j;\] propagate temporal bounds along mandatory arcs by intersecting \(D_j\) with \([\min D_i+t_{ij},\infty)\) and \(D_i\) with \(( -\infty,\max D_j-t_{ij}]\); then re-solve the routing relaxation and fix or delete arcs justified by its bounds. Stop with infeasibility if any domain becomes empty; otherwise return the strengthened relaxation and domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-window propagation deletes temporally impossible arcs and tightens arrival domains; re-solving the routing relaxation can trigger further sound temporal inference.
assumptions_latex: Travel times satisfy \(t_{ij}\ge0\).
Only arcs proved mandatory or impossible are fixed by relaxation-based inference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed point preserves every time-window-feasible route while strengthening its routing relaxation and temporal domains.

notation.meaning: current arrival-time domain at vertex i
service time window at vertex i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic relaxation and CP citations do not support the stated time-window propagation algorithm. The rule for fixing or deleting arcs from relaxation bounds is also not specified precisely enough to independently assess the claimed fixed-point preservation.

children.title: Geometric Allocation Hybrid Family
children.top_down_role: Selection and assignment decisions coupled to geometric placement and non-overlap reasoning.

children.title: Selection Master with CP Packing
children.top_down_role: Costed selection coordinated with geometric packing subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Master with CP Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Costed item selection in MIP coupled to geometric packing feasibility in CP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input items \(I\), values \(v_i\), selection costs \(c_i\), and a container region \(B\). Solve a binary master over \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\) maximizing \(\sum_{i\in I}(v_i-c_i)y_i\), subject to aggregate size and business constraints. For the selected set \(S=\{i:y_i=1\}\), solve a CP model assigning each item a permitted orientation and position in \(B\), with containment and pairwise non-overlap. If packing is feasible, return the selection and placement when its master bound proves optimality. If a subset \(C\subseteq S\) is packing-infeasible, add \[\sum_{i\in C}y_i\le |C|-1\] and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A costed master selects items; CP attempts to pack them geometrically, and each infeasible subset produces a valid selection cut.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and every orientation domain are finite.
Each reported core \(C\) is not jointly packable in \(B\).
The master is solved exactly at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns an optimal selection admitting a certified packing, or proves that no master-feasible selection is packable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infeasible-subset cut is plausible under its assumption, but the cited sources do not specifically support the selection-master/CP-packing architecture or its global optimality conclusion.

children.title: Bin Assignment with Placement Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Container assignments checked against detailed placement constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Bin Assignment with Placement Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detailed placement certificate for a fixed item-to-bin assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{ib}\in\{0,1\}\) assign each rectangular item \(i\) of oriented width \(w_i\) and height \(h_i\) to one bin \(b\) of dimensions \(W_b\times H_b\). Placement feasibility is certified by coordinates \((X_i,Y_i)\) satisfying, whenever \(z_{ib}=1\), \[0\le X_i\le W_b-w_i,\qquad 0\le Y_i\le H_b-h_i,\] and, for every distinct pair assigned to the same bin, at least one disjunct \[X_i+w_i\le X_j,\quad X_j+w_j\le X_i,\quad Y_i+h_i\le Y_j,\quad Y_j+h_j\le Y_i\] holds. These inequalities are directly checkable and certify containment and non-overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinates and separation disjunctions certify that every assigned rectangle lies inside its bin and no two rectangles in one bin overlap.
assumptions_latex: Every item is assigned to exactly one bin.
Item orientations, widths, and heights are fixed for the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignment \(z\) is placement-feasible for the displayed bins.

notation.meaning: assignment of item i to bin b
lower-left placement coordinate of item i
width and height of bin b

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment and non-overlap certificate is standard and internally coherent, but the cited generic disjunctive-programming and CP locators do not specifically document rectangular placement feasibility.

children.title: Layout Relaxations with Non-Overlap Propagation
children.top_down_role: Linear layout bounds combined with specialized geometric inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Layout Relaxations with Non-Overlap Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear layout lower bounds strengthened by sound geometric domain filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible placements of finitely many rectangles in a region \(B\), including containment and pairwise non-overlap disjunctions, and let \(R\supseteq F\) be a linear relaxation used to minimize layout cost \(c^Tx\). For current coordinate domains \(D\), suppose non-overlap propagation produces \(P(D)\) with \(F\cap D=F\cap P(D)\). Then \[L(D)=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in R\cap P(D)\}\] is a valid lower bound. Empty propagated domains certify infeasibility; otherwise coordinate tightening or a forced relative-order disjunct may strengthen \(R\) without excluding any feasible layout.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound non-overlap propagation narrows coordinate domains and may force relative orders; a linear relaxation over those domains remains a valid layout bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
Propagation preserves every feasible placement in the current domains.
The rectangle set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation and relaxation can be iterated while preserving feasibility and validity of the minimization lower bound \(L(D)\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation-bound argument is plausible, but the cited sources do not directly support non-overlap propagation, forced geometric order disjuncts, or their integration with a layout relaxation.

children.title: Logical Allocation Hybrid Family
children.top_down_role: Aggregate allocation or cost structure coupled to detailed logical compatibility and sequence rules.

children.title: Workforce Assignment with Roster Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Staffing decisions combined with detailed sequence and rule feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Workforce Assignment with Roster Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate staffing assignment in MIP followed by employee-level roster feasibility in CP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input employees \(E\), shifts \(S\), skills, coverage requirements, assignment costs, and roster rules. Solve a MIP master over \(x_{es}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfying skill eligibility and aggregate coverage while minimizing \(\sum_{e,s}c_{es}x_{es}\). Submit each employee's assigned shifts to a CP subproblem enforcing temporal non-overlap, rest, sequence, and workload rules. If all rosters are feasible, return the assignment and rosters when the master bound proves optimality. From an explained infeasible set \(C\subseteq E\times S\), add \[\sum_{(e,s)\in C}x_{es}\le |C|-1\] and re-solve. Stop as infeasible if the master becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP meets coverage and skill requirements; CP validates detailed rosters and returns nogoods for shift combinations violating rest, sequence, or workload rules.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(S\) are finite.
Every returned core \(C\) cannot be extended to a rule-feasible roster.
The master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination yields a cost-optimal assignment admitting detailed feasible rosters, or certifies infeasibility under valid feedback cuts.

notation.meaning: assignment of employee e to shift s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic IP and CP citations do not establish this workforce-master/roster-subproblem algorithm, the form of its explained cores, or the asserted optimality and infeasibility guarantees.

children.title: Configuration Selection with Logical Completion
children.top_down_role: Costed component selection combined with compatibility and completion reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Selection with Logical Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Costed component selection in MIP completed and validated by finite-domain logical reasoning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input components \(I\), costs \(c_i\), required features, and logical compatibility and completion constraints. Initialize a MIP master over \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\), minimizing \(\sum_{i\in I}c_iy_i\) subject to linearized feature coverage and known incompatibilities. Submit the selected literals to a CP or SAT-style completion subproblem that assigns remaining option variables and enforces all logical constraints. If a completion exists, return it when the master bound proves optimality. If the subproblem explains infeasibility by selected-literal core \(C\), add \[\sum_{i\in C}y_i\le |C|-1\] and repeat. Report infeasibility when no master selection remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP chooses costed components; logical completion assigns remaining options, while explained incompatible selections become nogoods in the master.
assumptions_latex: The component and option domains are finite.
Every core \(C\) is logically inconsistent with all possible completions.
The master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns a minimum-cost master selection with a complete logically feasible configuration, or certifies that none exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected-literal cut is valid under the strong stated core assumption, but the cited generic modeling sections do not support the MIP/CP-or-SAT completion architecture or its termination guarantees.

children.title: Facility Assignment with Operational Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Location or assignment decisions checked against detailed operating constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(I\), \(J\), and \(K\) are finite.
Each predicate \(\Phi_k\) depends only on the declared master decisions and finite-domain operational variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\) is hybrid-feasible exactly when it satisfies the master constraints and every \(\Phi_k(x,y)\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: indicator that facility i is opened
indicator that customer j is assigned to facility i
operational CP feasibility predicate for block k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master facility and assignment decisions linked to finite-domain operational feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let facilities be indexed by \(i\in I\), customers by \(j\in J\), and operational blocks by \(k\in K\). Let \(f_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(c_{ij}\in\mathbb R\) be facility-opening and assignment cost coefficients. A hybrid representation is
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}f_i y_i+\sum_{i\in I,j\in J}c_{ij}x_{ij}: y_i,x_{ij}\in\{0,1\},\ \sum_{i\in I}x_{ij}=1\ (j\in J),\ x_{ij}\le y_i\ (i\in I,j\in J),\ \Phi_k(x,y)\text{ is satisfiable for every }k\in K\right\}.
\]
Here each predicate \(\Phi_k\) is a CP operational model, such as a scheduling, sequencing, or resource-feasibility model. An infeasible subproblem may return a valid master constraint excluding every assignment covered by its explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary facility and assignment choices form the master problem; each operational block must admit a feasible CP completion, with explanations optionally returned as valid master constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Facility Assignment with Operational Subproblems

children.title: Network Operations Hybrid Family
children.top_down_role: Network design and operation models combining strong flow relaxations with specialized logical or temporal constraints.

children.title: Network Design with Operational CP Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Infrastructure decisions coordinated with detailed operational feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) and \(S\) are finite.
The master set \(M\) is a mixed-integer linear set.
Each \(\Psi_s\) has a decidable finite-domain satisfaction problem for fixed \((y,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A design \((y,z)\in M\) is feasible exactly when \(\Psi_s(y,z)\) is satisfiable for all \(s\in S\).

notation.meaning: operational CP predicate for scenario s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary infrastructure design with CP predicates representing detailed network operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph and \(S\) a finite set of scenarios or periods. For each \(a\in A\), let \(y_a\in\{0,1\}\) select arc \(a\); let \(z\) collect the other mixed-integer design variables. Let \(c\) and \(d\) be conformable real cost vectors. A network-design hybrid has the form
\[
\min\left\{c^\top y+d^\top z:(y,z)\in M,\ \Psi_s(y,z)\text{ is satisfiable for every }s\in S\right\},
\]
where \(M\) contains linear design, budget, and optional aggregate-flow constraints. Each finite-domain predicate \(\Psi_s\) enforces operational requirements for scenario or period \(s\), including routing, switching, timing, compatibility, or service rules. Thus the master proposes infrastructure and every CP subproblem checks whether that infrastructure supports a permitted operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear mixed-integer master selects network infrastructure, while scenario-indexed CP subproblems test whether detailed routing, switching, timing, and service operations can be completed.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Design with Operational CP Subproblems

children.title: Flow Relaxations with Logical Network Constraints
children.top_down_role: Network-flow bounds combined with configuration, switching, or service constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is the node-arc incidence matrix of the finite graph \(G\).
Every feasible solution of the integral network model satisfies the stated flow equations, capacity inequalities, and logical predicate \(L(y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(R\cap\{(f,y):L(y)\}\) contains every feasible solution of the integral network model and hence is a valid relaxation; minimizing over it gives a valid lower bound, and maximizing over it gives a valid upper bound.

notation.meaning: flow of commodity k on arc a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous multicommodity-flow relaxation strengthened by logical restrictions on network configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph, let \(K\) be a finite commodity set, let \(u_a\ge0\) be the capacity of arc \(a\in A\), and let \(y_a\in[0,1]\) be the relaxed configuration variable for that arc. For each \(k\in K\), let \(f_a^k\ge0\) denote its arc flow and let \(b^k\) be its node-balance vector. The flow-relaxation component is
\[
R=\left\{(f,y): Bf^k=b^k\ (k\in K),\ \sum_{k\in K}f_a^k\le u_a y_a\ (a\in A),\ 0\le y_a\le1\ (a\in A)\right\}.
\]
A logical network model adds a predicate \(L(y)\), encoding switching, configuration, adjacency, or service rules and defined on every relaxed configuration at which it is evaluated. The hybrid relaxation uses \(R\cap\{(f,y):L(y)\}\), or applies sound CP propagation associated with \(L\) while retaining \(R\) for objective bounds. If every feasible solution of the integral network model belongs to this set, minimizing over the set yields a valid lower bound and maximizing over it yields a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous flow model supplies bounds while a logical predicate restricts admissible relaxed configurations. Provided every feasible integral network remains in the intersection, it is a valid relaxation, giving a lower bound for minimization and an upper bound for maximization.
knowledge_statements.title: Flow Relaxations with Logical Network Constraints

children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determining whether a CP–MIP hybrid is effective, scalable, complete, and certifying.

children.title: Favorable Hybrid Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures in which complementary propagation and relaxation strengths can be isolated.

children.title: Inference-Relaxation Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Substructures that are strong for one paradigm and weak for the other.

children.title: CP Inference Advantage
children.top_down_role: Substructures where constraint propagation supplies the stronger reduction mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: CP Inference Advantage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable dominance condition for CP propagation on the shared master-variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a domain box for shared finite-domain variables, let \(P_C(D)\subseteq D\) be the box remaining after a CP propagator reaches its prescribed fixpoint, and let \(P_M(D)\subseteq D\) be the domain reduction obtained from the chosen MIP relaxation and bound-tightening routine. CP has an inference advantage on a family \(\mathcal D\) when
\[
P_C(D)\subseteq P_M(D)\quad\text{for every }D\in\mathcal D,
\]
with strict inclusion for at least one \(D\in\mathcal D\), or when CP detects infeasibility for some \(D\) that the MIP routine does not. The comparison is meaningful only for fixed encodings, inference levels, and resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CP has an inference advantage when its fixed-point propagation uniformly removes at least the values removed by the selected MIP routine, and sometimes removes more or detects infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Both routines operate on the same shared-variable domain boxes \(D\in\mathcal D\).
The CP consistency level, MIP relaxation, tightening routine, and resource limit are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: CP inference dominates on \(\mathcal D\) if \(P_C(D)\subseteq P_M(D)\) for all \(D\in\mathcal D\), with a strict improvement on at least one instance.

notation.meaning: specified family of comparable domain boxes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the CP-inference terminal, but the cited general CP modeling section does not inspectably support this particular uniform dominance definition, its comparison with MIP tightening, or the resource-qualified infeasibility alternative. A specialized propagation-versus-relaxation source is required.

children.title: MIP Relaxation Advantage
children.top_down_role: Substructures where linear relaxation supplies the stronger bounding mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Relaxation Advantage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bound-dominance condition for the MIP relaxation at hybrid search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a minimization problem and a family \(\mathcal N\) of hybrid search nodes. Let \(L_M(N)\) be the valid lower bound obtained by solving the selected MIP relaxation at node \(N\), and let \(L_C(N)\) be the lower bound supplied by the selected CP relaxation or inference procedure. MIP has a relaxation advantage on \(\mathcal N\) when
\[
L_M(N)\ge L_C(N)\quad\text{for every }N\in\mathcal N,
\]
with strict inequality for at least one node. For maximization, reverse the inequality. This comparison presupposes identical node restrictions, objective convention, and resource limit; otherwise it does not define relaxation dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, MIP has a relaxation advantage when its valid node bounds are never weaker than the chosen CP bounds and are strictly stronger somewhere.
assumptions_latex: Both methods use the same node restrictions and objective.
\(L_M(N)\) and \(L_C(N)\) are valid lower bounds under a fixed resource convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: MIP relaxation dominance on \(\mathcal N\) is characterized by \(L_M(N)\ge L_C(N)\) for all \(N\in\mathcal N\), strictly for some \(N\).

notation.meaning: MIP-relaxation lower bound at node N
CP-derived lower bound at node N
family of comparable hybrid search nodes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound-dominance condition is precise and the content kind fits, but the cited LP-relaxation section does not inspectably support the comparative CP-MIP hybrid criterion or its resource convention. A source treating comparable CP and MIP bounds in a hybrid setting is required.

children.title: Complementarity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Model boundaries where inference gains can reinforce relaxation gains.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-variable mappings through which CP inference and MIP bounds strengthen one another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be the shared variables, \(X_M\) a MIP relaxation, and \(X_C\) a CP constraint system. A complementarity interface consists of sound maps \(T_{M\to C}\) and \(T_{C\to M}\). Given a MIP state \(S_M\), the message \(T_{M\to C}(S_M)\) may contain valid variable bounds or fixed literals; given a CP state \(S_C\), the message \(T_{C\to M}(S_C)\) may contain valid bound changes, clauses, or linear inequalities. Soundness requires that every globally feasible \(x\) satisfy every transmitted restriction. Alternating both maps to a fixpoint therefore preserves the feasible set while potentially strengthening both component states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementarity interface exchanges only globally valid bounds, literals, clauses, or inequalities between MIP and CP, so repeated communication can strengthen both without deleting feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: The MIP and CP components use an explicit mapping of their shared variables \(x\).
Every transmitted restriction is valid for all globally feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixpoint application of \(T_{M\to C}\) and \(T_{C\to M}\) preserves every globally feasible assignment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is internally sound and appropriate for the interface terminal. The supplied component-level CP and LP-relaxation citations do not, however, support the bidirectional maps, permissible message types, or alternating-fixpoint claim. Those interface-specific assertions require a specialized hybrid source.

children.title: Strength Imbalance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where one paradigm contributes too little to justify hybrid coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength Imbalance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where one component contributes no strict inference or bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_C(N)\) and \(P_M(N)\) denote the shared-variable domains after CP and MIP processing at node \(N\), and let \(L_C(N)\) and \(L_M(N)\) be valid lower bounds for minimization. A strength-imbalance boundary favoring MIP occurs when
\[
P_C(N)=P_M(N)\quad\text{and}\quad L_C(N)\le L_M(N)
\]
for every relevant node, with CP producing no additional certificate used by the master. The symmetric boundary favoring CP exchanges the component labels. Beyond such a boundary, the dominated component cannot improve pruning under the fixed interface; any hybrid benefit must instead come from lower computational cost, diversification, or a richer interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strength imbalance occurs when one component never improves domains, bounds, or usable certificates beyond the other under the fixed interface, eliminating complementary pruning benefits.
assumptions_latex: Both components are compared on identical nodes under fixed encodings and resource limits.
Only domain reductions, objective bounds, and transmitted certificates count as hybrid contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If one component makes no strict contribution on any relevant node, complementarity-based pruning improvement is unavailable under the fixed interface.

notation.meaning: CP- and MIP-derived minimization lower bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the terminal, but no source is supplied for the proposed dominance metrics or the conclusion that complementary pruning is unavailable under the fixed interface. The mathematical formulation is specialized enough that standard-field rationale alone is insufficient.

children.title: Weakly Coupled Repeated Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Block, resource, scenario, route, or machine decompositions supporting reusable inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Coupled Repeated Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated blocks connected only through a low-dimensional master decision vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hybrid feasibility system has weakly coupled repeated subproblems if it can be written as
\[
x\in X,\qquad \exists z^k\in Z_k:\ F_k(x_{J_k},z^k)\quad(k=1,\ldots,m),
\]
where the local variables \(z^1,\ldots,z^m\) are pairwise disjoint and different blocks interact only through master subvectors \(x_{J_k}\). The coupling is weak relative to the block descriptions when each interface \(J_k\) is small and the predicates \(F_k\) share a common parameterized structure. Fixing \(x\) then separates feasibility into \(m\) independent CP subproblems, enabling repeated propagation procedures and reusable explanations indexed by interface assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblems are weakly coupled when their local variables are disjoint, they communicate only through small master interfaces, and fixing the master makes all blocks independent.
assumptions_latex: The index set of blocks is finite.
Local variable sets \(Z_k\) are pairwise disjoint.
Each predicate \(F_k\) depends on other blocks only through \(x_{J_k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(x\), global subproblem feasibility is equivalent to independent satisfiability of \(F_k(x_{J_k},z^k)\) for every \(k\).

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
